tools.name: exec

format.definition:
start: pragma_source | plain_source
pragma_source: PRAGMA_LINE NEWLINE SOURCE
plain_source: SOURCE

PRAGMA_LINE: /[ \t]*\/\/ @exec:[^\r\n]*/
NEWLINE: /\r?\n/
SOURCE: /[\s\S]+/

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.name: request_user_input_async
tools.description: Ask the user one or more questions during ongoing work. Use this tool only to request missing information, preferences, constraints, clarification, or approval. The tool returns immediately without ending the turn or waiting for a reply; any reply arrives asynchronously as a new user message. Keep questions concise, self-contained, and easy to understand, using a level of detail appropriate to the user and task. The UI always allows a free-text answer, including when suggested options are provided. A preselected option is not submitted automatically.

questions.description: One or more self-contained questions to present together, in display order.

options.description: Suggested answers, in display order. Put the recommended answer first; the first option is preselected by default. The user can select one option or enter a free-text answer. Do not include an Other option or a free-text placeholder; the UI provides free-text input automatically. Omit options for a free-text-only question.

title.description: The complete question shown to the user, including any context needed to answer it.

tools.name: clock
tools.description: Tools for reading and waiting on time.

tools.name: sleep
tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn. Returns the elapsed wall-clock time.

duration_ms.description: How long to sleep in milliseconds. Must be between 1 and 43200000.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-astra`: Frontier intelligence for the most demanding work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-sol`: Previous generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-luna`: Fast and affordable model for easier tasks. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-5.6-sol`: Older generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: mcp__cua_repl
tools.description: UI automation through cua_repl using the initialized cua API.

tools.name: js
tools.description:
Control native apps or browsers on the user’s computer by reading or operating UI. Prefer purpose-built skills, connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available.

On the first invocation of `cua_repl`, or after resetting it, execute exactly one of the API calls shown below, optionally assigning its result to a variable. Do not add other API calls, waits, or snapshots to that invocation.
The tool result will include documentation and, when creating or selecting a tab or selecting an app, its initial UI state. Selecting a browser does not open a tab. Read that result before continuing.
Use only APIs described in the tool instructions or returned documentation.

When you need an inventory of available apps, browsers, and tabs, get a snapshot of all enabled surfaces. Otherwise, use the relevant entry point below:

```javascript
await cua.getState();
```

Use the first matching browser control option from the user's request:

For a tab @-mention (`mention=tab-v1`):
Pass the complete `plugin://...` URL to get the referenced tab.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ mention: tabMentionUrl });
```

For an existing tab identified by URL in browser context (including the current IAB tab):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ url }, { browser: browserId });
```

Known tab ID (`tabId` or `providerTabId`) and browser (name or browser @-mention):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: browserId });
```

To open a URL in the in-app browser (`@Browser`):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab("iab", url, { visible: boolean });
```

To open a URL in another named browser: pass its name directly; do not call `getBrowser` first.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab(browserName, url, browserOptions);
```

Known URL, only when the user has not specified a browser by name or @-mention:

```javascript
let browser = await cua.getBrowser({ url });
```

Browser IDs and options:

- `"mcpapps"`: use `cua.getBrowser({ id: "mcpapps" })` for existing full-screen MCP Apps in the task’s side panel.
- `"iab"` (in-app browser): in `createBrowserTab`, use `visible: true` to show the browser; `false` to keep it hidden.
- `"dot"` (Dot): use only when present in browser inventory. It accesses tabs on Dot's active main thread. `cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: "dot" })` selects an existing tab. `cua.createBrowserTab("dot", url, { visible: boolean })` creates one with the same visibility options as `"iab"`.
- `"chrome"` (@Chrome), `"edge"` (@Edge): pass a short, emoji-prefixed `sessionName` (e.g. `"🔎 Task"`) to `createBrowserTab` when starting a task.

On Windows, choose the requested window by app and title from the inventory. Pass the selected window's ID as returned.

```javascript
let app = await cua.getApp({ windowId: selected.id });
```

To add other content to the tool result, use `nodeRepl.write(value)` for text or other values and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(image)` for images. The APIs listed above already display their documentation or UI state; do not wrap their results in `write` or `emitImage`.

If your context begins with a summary of an existing computer use task, call `await cua.rewriteDocumentation()` before continuing the computer use task to ensure you have a complete view of the necessary documentation.

Several `cua_repl.js` calls may work toward the same goal. As soon as you observe the final outcome of the CUA part of the task, make your next tool call `cua_repl.js` with only `completion_summary`, exactly once. Do this before using another tool for the next part of the user’s request or sending your reply, even if the overall request continues. If you hand control to the user, wait to summarize until the handoff has ended and you’ve observed the final outcome of the CUA part of the task. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

code.description: JavaScript to execute using the initialized cua_repl runtime.

completion_summary.description: Write a headline for the observed outcome in three to six words total. Start with a past-tense verb and name the result in plain language, as in 'Booked a plumber for Thursday' or 'Renewed vehicle registration'. Leave identifiers, values, and explanations for the reply.

timeout_ms.description: Optional execution timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000 (30 seconds) when omitted.

title.description: Short user-facing description of what this code block is doing. Prefer a few words in present-progressive form, such as 'Checking the mobile layout' or 'Comparing prices', over imperative or past-tense titles.

tools.description: Reset the persistent cua_repl JavaScript session. All JavaScript bindings are discarded. The next cua_repl.js call initializes a fresh runtime for the enabled surfaces. This does not close browser tabs or native apps, or erase their state. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images, videos, and audio using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When an app or connector generates or edits media, prefer native media already displayed inline or a local output file already returned by the tool. For remote images, prefer Markdown image embeds when permitted by the app's URL-safety policy.
- When presenting media that cannot be displayed directly, including remote video and audio, use the app's preview or display tool when available. Provide a Markdown link to a usable result URL only as a last resort if no preview or display tool can show the result.
- Do not download remote media to bypass the app's restrictions on presenting it to the user.
- When sending or referencing a local image, video, or audio file, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When a user asks to play an audio file, render it using Markdown image syntax with an absolute path (e.g., ![audio](/absolute/path.mp3)).
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Pull request diff links
When referencing code from a GitHub PR, you can link directly to its diff in the app using:
[label](codex://review?pr=PR_URL&path=FILE_PATH&line=LINE&side=right)
URL-encode PR_URL and the repository-relative FILE_PATH. Use a verified one-based LINE from the current PR diff. Use side=left for the original code or side=right for the updated code. Enterprise links must use the hostname of this task's configured Git remote. Use ordinary file links for workspace code.

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, use the MCP server's `load_workspace_dependencies` tool (`mcp__codex_app__load_workspace_dependencies`) to find the bundled runtime and libraries.

### Automations
- When you write or rewrite an automation prompt, keep it within 10,000 estimated tokens.
- When the user asks to manage an app automation, set a reminder, or schedule a recurring task, use the relevant Automations action to help the user. Do not write raw automation directives by hand.
- Create an automation when the user wants a reminder, a recurring report, or a standing alert for future events.
- Do not create an automation to track a specific job or task through a milestone, failure, or completion. If the user asks you to watch a run or task to completion, keep checking in the current task and follow through when the requested condition is met.
- Unless the user asks for periodic updates, notify them only on a meaningful change, completion, failure, or required user action.
- When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.
- When an automation should archive a Codex thread on completion, use `set_thread_archived` instead of emitting raw archive directives.

### Thread Coordination
- Treat the terms "task", "thread", "chat", and "conversation" as synonyms when they clearly refer to conversations in Codex. Use "chat" when referring to conversations in the product. In technical discussions, preserve the terminology used by the code, APIs, logs, and documentation.
- When the user asks to create, fork, inspect, continue, hand off, pin, archive, unarchive, permanently delete, rename, or otherwise manage Codex threads, search for the relevant thread tool first: `create_thread`, `fork_thread`, `list_threads`, `list_archived_threads`, `read_thread`, `wait_threads`, `send_message_to_thread`, `handoff_thread`, `set_thread_pinned`, `set_thread_archived`, `delete_thread`, or `set_thread_title`.
- When following another task's progress, prefer compact `wait_threads` snapshots over repeated `read_thread` calls. Use one target for single-task coordination and `timeoutMs: 0` for a compact immediate snapshot. `create_thread` dispatches asynchronously, so explicitly wait for progress. Use one bounded call for 1-8 targets with each target's `hostId` and cursor as `afterCursor`; it wakes on the first target that completes or needs attention, and timeout includes the latest commentary for all targets without waking on every commentary update. An up-to-date cursor suppresses already-delivered final text. Separate waits from one task may run serially. Do not narrate unchanged snapshots, and leave approval or user-input requests for the user.
- Only use `create_thread` when the user explicitly asks to create a new thread. Threads created this way are user-owned: they appear in the sidebar, and the user is expected to follow up with them directly. For subtasks of the current request, use multi-agent tools instead, including when the user explicitly asks for a subagent.
- After a successful `create_thread` call, emit `::created-thread{threadId="..."}` for a created thread or `::created-thread{clientThreadId="..."}` for queued worktree setup on its own line in your final response.

### Inline Code Comments
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive when you need to attach feedback directly to specific code lines.
- Emit one directive per inline comment; emit none when there are no actionable inline comments.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3).
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.
</app-context>

## Product definition

FORGE is a goal-driven, persistent-router autonomous Agent system. Its primary interface is one continuous conversation. The user does not open or switch task sessions to work with different Agents.

## User-facing continuity versus internal concurrency

The product intentionally separates the conversational surface from execution concurrency:

- **Conversation**: the stable user-visible timeline.
- **Router**: the persistent user-facing Agent identity. It receives all user messages and owns the response.
- **Quest**: a durable objective inferred or explicitly requested by the user.
- **Task Node**: a unit of work inside a Quest DAG.
- **Worker Session**: a private, isolated execution context assigned to one or more task nodes.
- **Event**: a durable fact about state transition, progress, request, result or failure.

A single conversation can contain multiple simultaneous Quests. The Router resolves follow-up references using active Quest state, recency, project context and explicit user references. If ambiguity is material, it asks one concise clarification rather than silently attaching a message to the wrong Quest.

## Router responsibilities

1. Maintain conversational continuity and the Router Task Capsule.
2. Classify each message as chat, create, continue, update, status or approval.
3. Resolve the target Quest.
4. Plan and maintain Quest DAGs.
5. Compose a team from model capability profiles and role contracts.
6. Request approval under Review autonomy.
7. Dispatch hidden Worker Sessions.
8. Consume Worker events and decide which ones merit user-facing delivery.
9. Replan on blocker, failure, evidence gap or changed user goal.
10. Produce one coherent user-facing response.

The Router is not a monolithic prompt with an ever-growing transcript. It operates over bounded recent turns, a compact capsule, Quest state, event cursor and retrieved evidence.

## Worker visibility policy

Worker sessions are hidden by default. The UI may show a task/activity panel with Worker role, state, progress summary and artifacts, but never exposes each Worker as a separate chat that the user must manage.

Workers send structured messages:
- `accepted`
- `progress`
- `help_requested`
- `blocked`
- `artifact_ready`
- `review_requested`
- `completed`
- `failed`

The Router decides whether to surface an event immediately, batch it, or wait for the final result. Important blockers and approvals are surfaced immediately. Routine progress can be coalesced to avoid spamming the conversation.

## Model intelligence

The Model Registry is a resource catalog, not a role catalog. A model can serve many roles; a role can be assigned to different models. Capability scores must carry provenance, sample count, timestamp and confidence. Unknown is not zero and must not be fabricated.

## Reference implementation boundaries

DSH/Super-agent informs persistent Router, hidden Workers, durable task routing and event handoff. Codex informs harness boundaries, event-oriented execution, tool safety and context compaction. Claude Code public documentation informs subagent contracts, hooks and permission concepts. FORGE implements its own runtime and data model rather than shelling out to these products.
# Router, Quest and Worker Protocol

## Core loop

1. Load a bounded snapshot of RouterState, recent turns, Quest summaries and events.
2. Call the configured Provider outside the database write transaction for a structured decision.
3. Validate the decision and resolve Quest references; ask the user when multiple targets remain plausible.
4. Commit the user message, decision effects, response and applicable cursor changes atomically after version checks.
5. Authenticated user approval is required for governed actions; model output cannot grant it.

M4–M5 implement durable DAG scheduling, Worker event consumption and the native Worker Loop. Mock protocol tests remain distinct from real provider demonstrations; the current real JSON completion demonstration proves syntax validation only. Chain-of-Recall memory remains M6 work. Worker help creates a durable Router composition request and a pending team proposal; no model event grants approval.

## Message envelope

Every internal message should include:
- `message_id`
- `conversation_id`
- `quest_id` (nullable)
- `task_node_id` (nullable)
- `sender_type` and `sender_id`
- `message_type`
- `correlation_id`
- `payload`
- `created_at`

## Event envelope

Events are append-only and sequence-numbered. Consumers must be idempotent. Event delivery is at-least-once; handlers record their last processed sequence. Do not assume exactly-once delivery.

## Router-to-Worker messages

`ASSIGN_TASK`, `CANCEL_TASK`, `PAUSE_TASK`, `RESUME_TASK`, `REQUEST_STATUS`, `REQUEST_REVISION`.

## Worker-to-Router messages

`ACCEPTED`, `PROGRESS`, `HELP_REQUESTED`, `BLOCKED`, `ARTIFACT_READY`, `REVIEW_REQUESTED`, `RESULT`, `FAILED`.

## Notification policy

- Immediate: approval needed, blocked, destructive-risk warning, user clarification needed, final result.
- Coalesced: routine progress, repeated tool status, heartbeat.
- Silent by default: internal reasoning, raw chain-of-thought, low-level polling.
- Never expose hidden Worker private reasoning. Surface concise status, decisions and evidence.

## Quest resolution

Resolution priority:
1. Explicit Quest ID or task card reference.
2. Direct semantic match against active Quest title/goal and recent conversation.
3. Ask clarification if multiple plausible targets remain; do not guess a current Quest.

Do not attach an unrelated new request to the most recently active Quest just because it is recent.
# Model Registry and Dynamic Team Composition

## Model Profile dimensions

Identity: provider, model_id, display_name, version, endpoint, enabled.
Capabilities: reasoning, math, coding, architecture, research, writing, design, vision, tool_use, instruction_following.
Performance: TTFT, tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, reliability, timeout rate.
Economics: input/output/cache price, currency, updated timestamp.
Limits: context window, max output, rate limits, concurrency.
Features: streaming, tool calls, JSON mode, image/audio/video input.
Provenance: provider metadata, FORGE benchmark, online observations, user override.
Uncertainty: sample_count, measured_at, confidence interval or confidence label.

Never fabricate model capabilities or pricing. Provider metadata may be unavailable; retain `unknown`.

## Benchmark dimensions
- Math: answer correctness and proof/derivation rubric.
- Coding: tests, hidden tests, patch correctness and regression.
- Planning: dependency completeness, feasibility, rework rate.
- Research: source validity, coverage and factual consistency.
- Tool use: schema accuracy, success and policy compliance.
- Design: visual tasks, constraint coverage and human blind review; text-only self-ratings are insufficient.
- Speed: real TTFT and generation speed measurements.
- Cost: observed usage multiplied by verified price metadata.

## Role Template
A role defines objective, responsibilities, input contract, output schema, required capabilities, allowed tools, risk class, context budget and acceptance criteria. It must not hard-bind one provider/model.

## Team composition
Initial explainable baseline:
1. Filter enabled, healthy models compatible with modality/tool requirements.
2. Score task fit using capability profiles with confidence weighting.
3. Apply cost, latency, context and concurrency constraints.
4. Select role coverage and penalize redundant capabilities/coordination overhead.
5. Return top candidates and explain selection.
6. In Review mode, ask the user to approve the plan/team.

Later research: constrained set selection, complementarity, online routing and dynamic re-composition. Compare against single-best-model and fixed-team baselines.

## M5 implementation and evidence

The current bounded composer implements single_model, greedy, coverage and complementarity strategies with capability provenance/confidence, context/output, exact tool scope, token, currency/cost and concurrency constraints. Unknown measurements remain unknown. Eight preset roles coexist with complete, bounded dynamic contracts; every approved DAG node has one member. Model identity never grants permissions.

Team approval binds the exact plan and selected profile hashes. Worker help can request a separately approved replacement; only settled unfinished assignments may be replaced, with at most three replacements per Quest and no budget refund. Completed nodes retain their original run and historical approval evidence. Execution requires a current approved team; a separate verifier-only historical lookup permits proved superseded approvals, excludes revoked contracts and checks run creation against approval/supersession time.

The synthetic-team-v2 experiment compares four strategies and confidence/coordination ablations on three fixed scenarios. It measures selection mechanics, not real provider task quality. See [M5 report](PHASE1_MILESTONE5_REPORT.md) for actual results and limitations.
# Context, Memory, Governance and Evidence

## Context Compaction
The system must preserve task continuity, not merely summarize chat. A Task Capsule includes goal, success criteria, confirmed facts with evidence refs, hypotheses with status, decisions, completed/pending steps, blockers, constraints, artifacts, next action and source event cursor.

Compaction:
1. Snapshot authoritative state and recent events.
2. Generate structured capsule.
3. Validate required fields and references.
4. Archive old messages rather than destroying them.
5. Rebuild context from policy + capsule + relevant evidence + recent turns.
6. Record token counts, compaction version and recovery checks.

## Chain of Recall
Router recall indexes Quests, decisions, artifacts and evidence. Every recalled fact includes source and freshness. Distinguish verified facts from model hypotheses. On conflict, prefer newer verified evidence and surface uncertainty.

### M6 implementation in progress

The Core derives a project source from the bound Workspace, Task sources from
Quest records, decision and failure sources from a fixed set of Core events, and
artifact sources from trusted evidence records. Working context remains the
unarchived Session messages; Quest records are L1, the Workspace source is L2,
and failure experience is L3. Event payloads and evidence remain hypotheses
about their content: a trusted record establishes that Core recorded an event or
verification at that time, not the truth of a domain claim or the current state
of a file. The public memory write interface rejects a caller's attempt to label
an arbitrary claim confirmed. A recall result identifies sources, timestamps,
freshness, conflicts and related Quests; unknown freshness remains unknown.

Source indexing is incremental and transactional. Event, Quest and evidence
cursors advance with the derived index; source snapshots are hashed and checked
against current Core rows and plan revisions on read. Revoked sources are
excluded. Each synchronization processes a bounded batch and reports whether
more work remains. Retrieval uses indexed terms and a bounded candidate page;
its cursor and omission count signal incomplete results and must not be treated
as proof that an omitted Quest does not exist. Candidate ambiguity must remain
visible to the Router. This is still under integration and acceptance; see
[current status](STATUS.md) and the [synthetic study](PHASE1_MILESTONE6_CONTEXT_EXPERIMENT.md).

Only evidence with a recorded plan revision is indexed as a plan-bound source.
The general `ArtifactVerifier` can create records without that revision; these
are indexed as historical, explicitly unbound observations and cannot establish
the current plan's completion or the present contents of a file. Events without
a resolvable plan revision are skipped rather than assigned the Quest's current
revision. The index is derived data and is not an authorization or
task-completion authority.

## Governance
Default Review mode. Policy engine, not model, grants permissions. Risk levels:
- R0 read-only analysis.
- R1 reversible writes inside approved workspace.
- R2 external side effects or shared resource mutation.
- R3 deletion, credential access, payment, production action.
R3 defaults to deny or explicit secondary confirmation.

Approval is bound to a specific plan/action and parameter digest. Agent cannot elevate its own permissions. Budgets cover tokens, cost, time, tool calls and concurrency.

## Evidence
Task completion requires evidence from trusted tools or independent verification. Model claims are not evidence. Test evidence records command, environment, exit code, report path and timestamp. Evidence graph links Task, Worker, ToolCall, Artifact, TestRun, Decision and Approval.

# FORGE v4 — Persistent Router Agent System

FORGE is a self-built, general-purpose autonomous Agent desktop application.

## Engineering status — 2026-11-15

Milestones 1–4 provide persistence, governance, a Provider-backed Router, a model registry, Quest DAGs and durable events. Milestone 5 adds the native Worker Loop, approved dynamic teams, governed tools and independent execution evidence. Milestone 6 adds bounded context archives, sourced recall and unified model-call budget admission; its final local suite passed 372 tests and one bounded real-provider continuation succeeded after five recorded diagnostic failures. See the [M5 report](docs/PHASE1_MILESTONE5_REPORT.md) and [M6 report](docs/PHASE1_MILESTONE6_REPORT.md). Milestone 7 remains in progress; its [backend hardening round](docs/PHASE1_MILESTONE7_BACKEND_HARDENING.md) passed 488 local tests, while desktop acceptance is deferred and final integration and packaging remain to be verified.

See [current status](docs/STATUS.md), the [Phase 0 audit report](docs/PHASE0_AUDIT.md), and the report's dependency-ordered development plan. The release references `codex/MASTER_PROMPT.md`, but that file is missing from the supplied archive.

**The user has one persistent conversation.** A persistent Router Agent owns that conversation and coordinates multiple long-running Quests and hidden Worker Sessions. Workers have isolated execution contexts, but they are never presented as separate user conversations.

## Product invariants

1. One persistent user-facing conversation per workspace.
2. One persistent Router identity and resumable state per workspace.
3. Multiple durable Quests can run behind that conversation.
4. Worker Sessions are private execution contexts, not user-facing chats.
5. Worker events are selectively relayed into the single conversation timeline.
6. Model Provider, Model Profile, Role Template, Agent Instance, Quest and Session are separate domain entities.
7. Model Registry uses provider metadata, FORGE benchmark results, online performance and explicit user overrides.
8. Team composition combines reusable role templates with bounded dynamic role synthesis.
9. FORGE owns its Agent Loop, Router, Worker Runtime, Tool Engine, Memory, Governance and Evidence.
10. Codex, DSH and Claude Code are architectural references only, never execution backends.

## What this release contains

- Typed Python domain layer and repository interfaces.
- SQLite persistence with schema versioning and transaction boundaries.
- Persistent `main` conversation and Router identity.
- Quest lifecycle state machine and hidden Worker Session records.
- Durable event log with sequence cursor.
- Model Registry and explainable capability-fit team composition baseline.
- Provider gateway and explicit unconfigured provider; Mock protocol tests are labelled.
- FastAPI API with input validation and consistent error handling.
- React single-conversation UI with background Quest panel.
- Automated tests for persistence, lifecycle, router classification and team composition.
- Architecture, threat model, ADRs, detailed roadmap and Codex execution prompts.

## Important maturity statement

This is an engineering foundation with bounded, locally tested context recovery and recall. The Router uses a configured Provider or explicitly fails. Mock protocol tests, synthetic experiments and real-provider demonstrations are identified separately. User history and active Quest counts remain bounded; large histories can fail closed, and general task correctness and final desktop integration remain open. A proposal record alone never proves execution.

## Backend setup

The model-driven Router requires explicit provider configuration. Set the process environment
variables `FORGE_PROVIDER_ID`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_KIND` (for example `openai_compatible`),
`FORGE_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REF` (for example
`FORGE_PROVIDER_KEY_EXAMPLE`), `FORGE_ROUTER_MODEL_ID`, and
`FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` (an operator-supplied maximum context window). Put the actual
credential only in the process environment variable named by the credential reference. Set
`FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_TOOLS=true` and `FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_JSON_SCHEMA=true` only when
the provider supports them. Without configuration the Core starts but Router message calls fail
explicitly; no keyword or mock provider is selected automatically. The optional `request_id`
in a message request allows safe retry: reuse it only for the same input.
For live calls, register an enabled model with the same provider and model ID and explicitly set
both `tool_calling_support` and `structured_output_support` to supported. Unknown capabilities
are rejected. Values submitted through the model API are recorded as user overrides.

The Router reads a bounded snapshot and calls the provider outside the database write
transaction. A successful decision and its messages commit together; provider errors, invalid
decisions, or budget failures leave no messages or Quest changes for that turn. The caller can
retry with the same request ID. The context budget uses a conservative UTF-8 byte estimate,
reserves output and request overhead, and also respects a known registry context window. Tool
access is limited to read-only Core queries. Worker execution separately requires approved plan/team contracts and governed tool permissions.

Python 3.11+ recommended.

```bash
cd backend
python -m venv .venv
# Windows PowerShell:
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
# macOS/Linux:
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-lock.txt
python -m pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation -e .
pytest
python -m forge_api
```

The lock file is verified on Windows with Python 3.13; other platforms and Python versions have not been verified. The editable installation requires build tooling already available. API documentation endpoints are disabled.

### Core authentication and development bootstrap

Core requires a fresh cryptographically random 32-byte process secret; `.env` is explicitly rejected. For manual browser development, supply it as 64 hex characters in `FORGE_CORE_SECRET` using a protected input method and enter the same secret into the UI's password field. Never place it in command history, source files, URLs, logs, or persistent browser storage. In the native desktop integration, the parent supplies the secret through a private pipe and the UI receives the derived session bearer in memory. Restarting Core invalidates old bearer tokens. Native integration is still undergoing final verification.

The unauthenticated public loopback `/health` returns only liveness and a random per-process session challenge; an authenticated request also receives Router identity and background status. A trusted client computes the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 over the UTF-8 challenge using the decoded 32-byte secret, and sends `Authorization: Bearer <digest>` on API requests. Requests without an Origin are allowed only with authentication and a loopback peer and Host; browser requests must also use an explicitly allowed Origin. These boundaries protect against unauthorized webpages and other untrusted clients; they do not protect secrets from an attacker who can read the same OS user's process memory. Keep the development server and any allowed origin trusted.

The authenticated user API supports `POST /api/approvals`, `GET /api/approvals?quest_id=...`, `GET /api/approvals/{id}`, and POSTs to `/{id}/decision` or `/{id}/revoke`. Workspace grants use `GET`/`POST /api/quests/{id}/grants` and `POST /api/quests/{id}/grants/revoke`. Decisions and grants record the authenticated local user, not a caller-supplied actor. The bearer represents that user; it must never be exposed to a model or registered as an Agent tool. These routes do not execute actions or accept trusted evidence. The M7 desktop approval and scope controls are under integration testing.

### Workspace and Settings

`python -m forge_api` is the shared Core launcher. From the repository root on Windows, `./scripts/run-backend.ps1` sets up the virtual environment and uses that launcher without shell activation. Pass `-WorkspaceRoot 'D:\YourWorkspace'` to the script, or `python -m forge_api --workspace-root 'D:\YourWorkspace'` directly. Workspace roots must be absolute paths.

The default Workspace is independent of the checkout, installation and shell directory:

| OS | Default Workspace root |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%/FORGE/workspaces/default` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/FORGE/workspaces/default` |
| Linux | `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/forge/workspaces/default` |

The database defaults to `<WorkspaceRoot>/data/forge.sqlite3`. Settings are loaded as follows:

1. Choose the root using `--workspace-root`, then the process variable `FORGE_WORKSPACE_ROOT`, then the OS default (in that order). A root in `.env` is rejected because the root determines which file to read.
2. Load `<WorkspaceRoot>/.env` if present. `FORGE_ENV_FILE` in the process environment can select another file; relative file names resolve from the root. An explicitly selected missing file is an error. The shell directory's `.env` is ignored. Copy `backend/.env.example` to the selected Workspace root.
3. Process variables override file values. Supported settings are `FORGE_WORKSPACE_ID`, `FORGE_DB_PATH`, `FORGE_HOST` and `FORGE_PORT`; empty values and invalid ports fail startup. `.env` does not expand variables or modify the process environment.
4. Resolve relative database paths from the root and normalize them to absolute paths. The default Workspace ID is a hash of the normalized root; an explicit stable ID supports moving a Workspace. A database already bound to another ID is rejected.

The CLI and desktop Core bootstrap use the same Workspace settings and a new process secret. Direct `uvicorn forge_api.main:app` requires the same secret and loopback binding; prefer the shared launcher.

After a workspace restore, a restore fence blocks writes until an offline review succeeds. Close the desktop and Core, inspect the restored workspace and rollback directory, then use the packaged Python executable with the exact manifest hash and rollback directory shown by the application (replace every placeholder):

```powershell
& 'C:\path\to\packaged\python.exe' -I -m forge_api.maintenance review-restore --workspace-root 'C:\path\to\workspace' --manifest-sha256 '<64-lowercase-hex>' --rollback-directory '.forge-previous-<32-hex>' --reason '<10+ character review reason>'
```

The review validates the source hash, rollback directory name, reason, historical receipts and budget state; unresolved effects or reservations cause it to fail closed. Acknowledging an unknown native operation is a separate action and does not clear the restore fence or establish that the operation succeeded.

Legacy databases are **not discovered or moved automatically**. If an earlier version used `backend/data/forge.sqlite3` or another CWD-relative location, stop its Core process, back up the database with SQLite's backup API (or copy the database and WAL files together while stopped), and set `FORGE_DB_PATH` to its absolute path. The first successful open migrates it in place to the current schema without changing the Router ID or existing records. Migration failure rolls back the entire pending chain; unknown future versions and ambiguous version metadata are rejected. Downgrades are unsupported.

Events and pending Outbox rows commit in the same transaction as their associated business changes. Durable per-consumer delivery uses leases, fencing, bounded retries, Inbox deduplication and dead-letter/replay records. Historical events migrate as pending. External tool effects require their own durable intents and receipts; event delivery alone does not make external effects exactly once.

### Approved Worker execution

Workers consume an approved Quest DAG and a separately approved team. Tool scopes, provider/model identity and token/tool/time/concurrency budgets are bound to those contracts. File writes additionally require a workspace grant; HTTPS/MCP actions require exact action approval and an operator allowlist. `FORGE_TOOL_NETWORK_HOSTS_JSON` is a JSON host list (at most 64); `FORGE_MCP_SERVERS_JSON` maps server names to `{"url":"https://example.invalid/mcp","tools":["example_tool"]}` (at most 16 servers), with the HTTPS host included in the allowlist. Defaults are empty and deny network access. These values are operator configuration, never model output. `jsonschema` validates Worker result contracts; it does not judge domain correctness. Help/reassignment produces a pending team proposal for authenticated approval. An uncertain action cannot be silently retried or discarded during replacement. Unsupported or failed fixed JSON criteria require manual review; infrastructure verification retries are bounded to three attempts.

An approved dependent Worker may read a bounded receipt from a successful direct
predecessor only when its plan node, approved role and effective Worker tool
scope all permit `worker_read_action_receipt`. Its initial context contains at
most 32 upstream references and an omission indicator; a reference is not proof
until the read checks the current plan and receipt provenance. Returned content
remains untrusted and retains the source execution mode (`live` or `mock`); a
mock receipt is not promoted to live evidence. Completion rechecks the recorded
tool result. Temporary capacity pressure queues work without treating it as a
semantic failure retry. Lease generations fence ownership; the separate bounded
failure-retry count is recorded by retry events, and authorization retries do
not consume that failure limit.

Model calls through the Gateway share a durable admission ledger, including Router, planner, team composer, benchmark and Worker calls. Configure these trusted process environment variables before enabling a provider:

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `FORGE_MODEL_TOKEN_LIMIT` | Total token reservation ceiling; defaults to `0`, which rejects model calls until explicitly configured. |
| `FORGE_MODEL_CONCURRENCY_LIMIT` | Concurrent admitted attempts; defaults to `1`. |
| `FORGE_MODEL_REMOTE_MAX_SECONDS` | Optional trusted upper bound on remote execution duration. Without one, an attempt with unknown outcome retains its concurrency slot; a client timeout alone cannot establish that remote execution stopped. |
| `FORGE_MODEL_SCOPE_LIMITS_JSON` | Optional array of `{"scope":"quest","scope_id":"<quest-id>","token_limit":10000,"concurrency_limit":1}` entries; scope may be `workspace`, `quest`, or `worker`. Approved task contracts also impose their own limits. |
| `FORGE_PRICE_BOUNDS_JSON` | Optional operator-provided provider/model price ceilings. Unknown prices remain unknown; token-only admission applies when no cost ceiling is configured. |
| `FORGE_MODEL_COST_LIMIT_MICROUNITS`, `FORGE_MODEL_COST_CURRENCY` | Optional global currency ceiling and three-letter currency; both require trusted price bounds and reconciled historical cost. |
| `FORGE_MODEL_HISTORICAL_COST_MICROUNITS` | Operator-reconciled pre-cutover global cost in the configured currency. Unknown historical cost is never assumed to be zero. |
| `FORGE_MODEL_SCOPE_COST_RECONCILIATIONS_JSON` | Optional array of `{"scope":"quest","scope_id":"<quest-id>","currency":"USD","cost_microunits":0}` entries for operator-reconciled historical scope cost. |

An unknown or interrupted remote outcome remains reserved until a trusted remote execution bound and isolation period permit recovery. Without a trusted bound the slot remains reserved; there is currently no operator interface for reconciling an individual unknown attempt. Do not infer that a timeout cancelled the remote request. Current real-provider demonstrations and reproducible research scripts are described in the [M5 report](docs/PHASE1_MILESTONE5_REPORT.md).

# Phase 1 Milestone 6 — Context, Recall and Model Budget

Status: local M6 engineering verification passed. The results below are local engineering
evidence; they do not establish general model quality or unrestricted autonomous
operation.

Context archives preserve source references and user instructions, validate
archive integrity on rebuild, and support bounded Worker context with tool
receipt recovery. Memory indexes Core Quest, Workspace, decision, failure and
artifact sources in bounded incremental batches. Source snapshots are checked
against their current records; revocation, expiry, historical provenance and
plan binding remain visible. Model-derived or manually supplied claims remain
hypotheses. Model-call budget admission is being integrated across call sites.
The tested OpenAI-compatible endpoint returned additional decision fields despite
receiving `response_format` with a strict JSON schema. Gateway now also sends the
format schema as a system instruction; strict validation still rejects invalid
outputs, and a provider capability declaration does not guarantee compliance.
The [synthetic study](PHASE1_MILESTONE6_CONTEXT_EXPERIMENT.md) records its
fixed inputs, baselines, ablations, observed byte counts and limitations.

Gateway admission is configured through trusted process environment settings
documented in the README: `FORGE_MODEL_TOKEN_LIMIT` (default 0, denying calls),
`FORGE_MODEL_CONCURRENCY_LIMIT`, `FORGE_MODEL_REMOTE_MAX_SECONDS`,
`FORGE_MODEL_SCOPE_LIMITS_JSON`, `FORGE_PRICE_BOUNDS_JSON`,
`FORGE_MODEL_COST_LIMIT_MICROUNITS`, `FORGE_MODEL_COST_CURRENCY`,

`FORGE_MODEL_SCOPE_COST_RECONCILIATIONS_JSON`. Historical currency amounts
must be reconciled by the operator; unknown amounts are not assumed zero.
Without a trusted remote execution bound, unknown attempts keep their slot and
there is no individual-attempt operator reconciliation interface yet.

## Capacity and remaining boundaries

The Router capsule preserves every distinct user utterance; continued growth can
eventually exceed the configured context budget and fail closed. Unlimited
conversation continuity is not solved. Task context currently permits at most
100 active Quests and reads a Quest's evidence and receipts without pagination.
Memory synchronization is limited to 100 batches of up to 256 source rows per
type during Router admission and explicitly fails when the backlog remains;
recall examines pages of at most 512 candidates and reports omissions. Future
work needs per-Quest constraint association, relevant source re-reading and
evidence pagination without losing user constraints.

General artifact verification without a plan revision is indexed as an unbound
historical observation. It does not prove a current file or plan is correct.
Events without a resolvable plan revision are omitted. Source content is data,
not an instruction or a permission. Real-provider M6 performance and model
quality remain unmeasured; no external model call is implied by the study.

## Live context diagnostics

Five bounded real-provider runs were retained under `.local/phase1/milestone6/`.
All five failed the end-to-end continuation check even though the SQLite Router
identity, 60 synthetic constraints and source readback checks passed. The first
made one HTTP attempt and returned a truncated response at the 512-token output
limit; the Python process failed, although its PowerShell wrapper did not
propagate that failure. The second made one HTTP attempt and ended in a
`DomainError`; the specific reason was not preserved and remains unknown.
The third made one successful HTTP attempt, then its second logical generate was
rejected by FORGE's conservative local 30,000-token reservation ceiling, with no
second HTTP attempt. The fourth used a 75,000-token ceiling and made one HTTP
attempt, but the model requested five tools and Core rejected the batch at its
four-tool limit. The fifth made two HTTP attempts and observed the tool limit,
but its final response used fields outside the strict Router decision schema;
Core rejected it. A database check confirmed the model's Quest ID matched the
original target. Across the two attempts, reported input was 11,403 tokens and
output was 2,127 tokens. This exposed the need to include the schema in model-visible
messages for providers that do not reliably enforce response-format parameters.
Fixes were applied and the final suite passed. The failures are not provider outage evidence
and cannot be counted as a successful recovery demonstration. No monetary cost
was available; the calls used token-only limits.

The sixth bounded run, after the tool-limit and schema-message fixes, passed.
One real HTTP attempt returned a strictly validated `continue_quest` decision
matching the original target. The same Router identity, 60 synthetic constraints,
105 cancelled synthetic Quests and source hash/readback checks were preserved.
It reported 5,420 input and 532 output tokens (5,952 total); the 75,000-token
figure was an admission ceiling, not usage. Cost was unavailable. Across all six
runs there were seven actual HTTP attempts; the third run's second logical
generate was rejected locally and did not send another HTTP request. This is one
narrow successful continuation scenario, not proof of general model quality.

## Next milestone dependencies

M7 remains unimplemented and no desktop Alpha success is claimed. The planned
ownership is Native integration (Context owner), backend bootstrap, backup and
bounded semantic harness (Budget owner), and desktop UI plus final evidence
(Memory owner). The proposed packaging pins a CPython embeddable runtime and
hash-locked wheels, with offline NSIS packaging. Native startup must use a
private pipe, dynamically allocated port and EOF shutdown, together with a
Workspace mutex and Windows Job Object. Each Core generation gets a new secret;
the UI receives only its derived bearer. Windows credential-vault testing is
limited to temporary dummy credentials. These are design dependencies, not
implemented or verified capabilities.

Desktop acceptance must cover Chinese IME composition so Enter does not submit
mid-composition; failed network, 401 and 409 sends must retain the draft and
the same request ID for safe retry and expose the actual error. Browser and
native clients keep the bearer only in memory and reconnect on Core generation
changes. Activity shows Worker state without creating additional conversations.
Lists need loading, empty, error and pagination states. `GET /api/conversation`
currently returns the latest 200 messages without a history cursor; it must be
extended with the backend owner before the UI can claim that the entire long
conversation is browsable.

### 2.1 Context 分层（L0-L3）与 compaction

**实现了哪几层。** 没有"层"字段驱动分层，分层是召回项上的来源标签：

- L1 = Quest 记录 / 决策事件 / 验证证据派生项（`memory.py:568`）
- L2 = Workspace 项目身份（`memory.py:470-485`，`:474`）
- L3 = 失败经验（`worker.failed/blocked/tool.execution_uncertain`，`memory.py:536-545,568`）
- **L0 只在白名单里**：`memory.py:70` 允许 `{"L0","L1","L2","L3"}`，全仓 grep 仅命中该行。未归档的"工作上下文"没有 L0 记录，它是 `router.py:118-124` 直查 `messages` 的 live 窗口。

结论：**L1/L2/L3 已有（Core 派生），L0 缺失**；分层是可检索标签，不是可插拔存储层。

**compaction 触发。** 两条真实触发点，条件相同：

- 用户消息链 `router.py:569-577`：`len(json(messages)) > context_limit//2` 或 `len(messages) > 50`，且 `len(messages) > 10`，每轮 `compact_router(keep_recent=10)` 后 `continue` 重取快照；上限 100 次否则 `DomainError`（`:573-574`）。
- 后台通知链 `router.py:421-433`：同阈值。
- 硬边界：消息数 ≤10 时永不压缩，单条超大只能失败关闭（`router.py:256-257`、`:291-292`）。

**摘要生成方式：模板/数据库拼装，不是模型生成。** `context_service.py:302-323`：

### 2.2 constraint 抽取与索引：**不存在**

- 抽取：无。相关代码仅 `context_service.py:107`（把 `quests.metadata` 当 constraints 透传）、`:316`（继承旧 capsule）、`router_domain.py:30`（字段声明）、`memory.py:86`（允许 `kind="constraint"`）。`router.py:882-887`、`:908-913` 构造 `TaskCapsule` 只填 `quest_id/goal/next_action/source_event_cursor`，`constraints` 恒为 `[]`。
- 索引：无。`memory_terms` 只索引 Quest/事件/证据/Workspace 快照（`memory.py:22-24,122-124,169`）；`sync_sources` 不扫 `messages`（`:188-199`）。
- 冲突检测：**只有** `memories.memory_key` 同键不同 statement 的 `conflicted` 标记（`memory.py:410-430`），而 `remember()` 无生产调用方 → 运行期不生效。

- 现存"约束不丢"靠两件事：user 消息逐字进 `hypotheses`（`context_service.py:17-45`）+ `quests.metadata` 透传。`docs/PHASE1_MILESTONE6_REPORT.md:41-42` 也承认 "Future work needs per-Quest constraint association"。

### 2.3 Recall 检索实现

- **纯词项索引，无语义向量**：`_terms`（`memory.py:12-17`）做 ASCII 词 + 中文 bigram，上限 128；排序=候选集合字典序（`:372` `sorted(candidate_set)[:513]`）；无 TF-IDF/相似度/embedding（`backend/src` 全量无 embedding/vector/cosine/faiss/numpy 命中）。
- 候选边界：每词 513（`:359`）、按 quest 索引 513（`:367`）、`refs` 直并（`:371`），总候选 513，消费前 512（`:372-374`）；`limit`/`max_bytes` 双限，超限计 `omitted` 并给 `cursor`（`:584-600`）。
- 来源可靠性：每项带 `trust`（`core_workspace|core_record|core_event|verified_evidence`）、`source_hash`、`plan_binding`（`bound|unbound`）、`trust_scope`（`memory.py:564-581`，明确"仅证明来源记录，不证明领域真值"）；召回时逐项重算快照哈希并与当前 Core 行比对（`:446-563`），不一致即丢弃（`test_memory_m6.py:231-232`）。
- 反幻觉硬约束：`status="confirmed"` 一律拒绝（`memory.py:76-77`），召回项恒 `hypothesis`（`:475,569`；`test_memory_m6.py:136,191,304`）。
- 冲突：仅 `memory_key` 维度（第 2.2 节），派生源无冲突合并。
- 过期过滤：`valid_until`（`memory.py:401`）；撤销源 `revoked_memory_sources` 逐项过滤（`:403-409,450-457`；`test_memory_m6.py:192-196,360-382`）。
- 事实层缺口：capsule 顶层 `facts` 永为 `[]`（`context_service.py:308`；`test_context_m6.py:84` 明确断言）。可信证据只在 `tasks[].facts`/`evidence_refs`（`context_service.py:136-145`），未上卷到会话级事实。

### 2.4 Agent 间通信协议

- 消息类型是**常量集合**，不是 enum 类型系统：`WORKER_COMMANDS`（6）与 `WORKER_FACTS`（7）为 `frozenset`（`event_domain.py:16-36`），`URGENT_EVENTS`（`:37-44`）；payload 自由 JSON（`events.payload TEXT`，`migrations.py:69-72`），无 per-type schema。
- **持久化消息 + 状态机是真实的**：`events`+`outbox` 同事务（`store.py:141-158`）；`event_deliveries.state CHECK ('pending','leased','delivered','dead','skipped')`（`dispatcher_schema.py:13-20`）；`event_inbox` 带 `notice_attempts/notice_next_attempt/notice_dead_at/notice_token`（`:23-31`）；`worker_inbox`（`worker_schema.py:5-8`）在 `worker_runtime.py:1071-1096` 转成 user 消息并注明"untrusted, not authority"。

- 缺口：①`worker.command.assign` 只在 `event_domain.py:18` 定义，全仓无生产点；worker 实际由 `WorkerScheduler.tick` → `manager.start` 启动（`worker_runtime.py:1886-1893`）。②无"agent→agent 直接消息"类型；`worker.help_requested` 只进 composer（`main.py:354`），限 2 次（`worker_runtime.py:763-768`）。③路由白名单硬编码在 `_routable`（`dispatcher.py:144-161`），新增消费者需改代码。

### 2.5 治理：风险分级、审批绑定、预算熔断

- **风险分级：真实且失败关闭。** `ACTION_RISKS` 固定映射 6 个动作（`governance.py:16-25`）；未知名 `DomainError("Unknown action is denied")`（`:38-42`）；R3 在申请与授权两侧恒拒（`:191-192`、`:353-354`）；R0/R1 要求 `parameters["path"]` 落在 `resource_scope` 内（`:361-367`），R1 还要匹配当前 plan_revision 的 `task_grants`（`:370-379`）。
- **审批绑定：真实且强。** 7 元组绑定（quest_id、plan_revision、action_type、parameter_digest、resource_scope、risk、policy_version，`:387-395`）；不匹配即置 `REVOKED`/`EXPIRED` 并抛错（`:396-417`）；`consumed_at IS NULL` 单次消费（`:403-406`）；过期在读取与决策两处检查（`:254-268`、`:307-311`）；完成门要求 `decided <= consumed < expires`（`evidence.py:36-52`）。工具侧有等价检查并原子消费（`tool_engine.py:369-399`）。
- **预算熔断：真实，双层次。** ①模型层：`admit` 逐次 HTTP 预留（`model_call_budget.py:145-455`），`settle` 发现超用置 `breached=1`（`:468-482`），此后 `admit` 直接 `BudgetExceeded("ledger is fenced")`（`:170-173`）；429 冷却共享（`:116-133`，`tests/test_model_call_budget.py:280`）。②Worker 层：token/cost 预留失败即 `worker.blocked`（`worker_runtime.py:1396-1447`，`reason_code=token_budget|cost_budget`），叠加 `steps/tool_spent` 上限（`:1301-1303,1643-1645`）。
- 运维缺口：`breached=1` 之后只有"重新对账"路径（`model_call_budget.py:182-193` 要求 `reconciled_cost`），**没有运营解封接口**；触发后需手改库。
- 漂移风险：风险表有两份 —— `governance.ACTION_RISKS`（`governance.py:16-25`）与各工具 `risk` 字段（`tool_domain.py:97-191`），靠"工具名 == action_type"对齐（R2 仅 `browser_get`/`mcp_call` 两表都有，`tool_domain.py:178,191`）。新 R2 工具若忘加名，审批会因 "Unknown action is denied" 失败（失败关闭，但会卡死功能）。

## 2. 重点问题逐条回答

### 2.1 Context 分层（L0-L3）与 compaction

**实现了哪几层。** 没有"层"字段驱动分层，分层是召回项上的来源标签：

- L1 = Quest 记录 / 决策事件 / 验证证据派生项（`memory.py:568`）
- L2 = Workspace 项目身份（`memory.py:470-485`，`:474`）
- L3 = 失败经验（`worker.failed/blocked/tool.execution_uncertain`，`memory.py:536-545,568`）

**compaction 触发。** 两条真实触发点，条件相同：

- 用户消息链 `router.py:569-577`：`len(json(messages)) > context_limit//2` 或 `len(messages) > 50`，且 `len(messages) > 10`，每轮 `compact_router(keep_recent=10)` 后 `continue` 重取快照；上限 100 次否则 `DomainError`（`:573-574`）。
- 后台通知链 `router.py:421-433`：同阈值。
- 硬边界：消息数 ≤10 时永不压缩，单条超大只能失败关闭（`router.py:256-257`、`:291-292`）。

**摘要生成方式：模板/数据库拼装，不是模型生成。** `context_service.py:302-323`：

- `goal/success_criteria` ← `quests` + `quest_requirements`（`:290-307`，并在 `rebuild_router` `:352-371`、`router.py:126-136` 重取，避免过期）
- `facts` ← 上一版 capsule（`:308`，**恒为空**，见第 2.3 节）
- `hypotheses` ← `_merge_messages`（`:17-45`）：user 消息逐字保留、去重、绑 `source_refs`；非 user 消息截断 256 字符并标 `omitted`
- `tasks` ← `_task_context`（`:48-161`）：逐 Quest 拉 requirements/approved plan/task_nodes/evidence/receipts
- `constraints` ← `legacy.get("constraints", ...)`（`:316`），只继承旧 `router_state.capsule`

整模块无 provider/runtime import，无模型调用 —— 刻意的确定性模板。

**来源引用与可恢复性（本模块最强项）。**

- 每条 source 存 `{"id","hash": sha256(row)}`（`:324`）；归档行自带 `source_hash/capsule_hash`（`:176-197`）
- 每次重建都重算 hash 并逐条 `_verify_source`（`:199-220`、`:241-261`）
- 原文不删：`messages` 全量保留（`test_context_m6.py:19` 断言 8 条仍在）；可经 `read_source` 读回（`context_service.py:530-537`），Router 侧 `read_context_source` 支持 `offset_chars`/`max_chars≤2048` 分片并回传 `source_sha256`（`router.py:714-747`；`test_context_m6.py:495-566` 用 4 片拼回原文并逐片校验）
- Worker 侧同理：只允许读回已归档 ordinal（`worker_runtime.py:1129-1204`），并对读回内容二次比对（`:1155-1167`）

### 2.2 constraint 抽取与索引：**不存在**

- 抽取：无。相关代码仅 `context_service.py:107`（把 `quests.metadata` 当 constraints 透传）、`:316`（继承旧 capsule）、`router_domain.py:30`（字段声明）、`memory.py:86`（允许 `kind="constraint"`）。`router.py:882-887`、`:908-913` 构造 `TaskCapsule` 只填 `quest_id/goal/next_action/source_event_cursor`，`constraints` 恒为 `[]`。
- 索引：无。`memory_terms` 只索引 Quest/事件/证据/Workspace 快照（`memory.py:22-24,122-124,169`）；`sync_sources` 不扫 `messages`（`:188-199`）。
- 冲突检测：**只有** `memories.memory_key` 同键不同 statement 的 `conflicted` 标记（`memory.py:410-430`），而 `remember()` 无生产调用方 → 运行期不生效。
- 过期检测：同样只在 `memories.valid_until`（`memory.py:401`、`:418-419`）。另有"计划版本失效"：plan_revision 变化把派生源置 `active=0`（`:220-223,268-272,288-292`）—— 版本失效，不是时间过期。
- 现存"约束不丢"靠两件事：user 消息逐字进 `hypotheses`（`context_service.py:17-45`）+ `quests.metadata` 透传。`docs/PHASE1_MILESTONE6_REPORT.md:41-42` 也承认 "Future work needs per-Quest constraint association"。
- 真实供应商的 `constraints_preserved=true`（`.local/phase1/milestone6/context-20261114T183632Z-53aba023/report.json`）来自脚本把 60 条约束写进 `quests.metadata`（`tests/live_context_probe.py:166,180-183`），再用子串包含判断（`:208-210`）——**透传校验，不是抽取校验**。

### 2.3 Recall 检索实现

- **纯词项索引，无语义向量**：`_terms`（`memory.py:12-17`）做 ASCII 词 + 中文 bigram，上限 128；排序=候选集合字典序（`:372` `sorted(candidate_set)[:513]`）；无 TF-IDF/相似度/embedding（`backend/src` 全量无 embedding/vector/cosine/faiss/numpy 命中）。
- 候选边界：每词 513（`:359`）、按 quest 索引 513（`:367`）、`refs` 直并（`:371`），总候选 513，消费前 512（`:372-374`）；`limit`/`max_bytes` 双限，超限计 `omitted` 并给 `cursor`（`:584-600`）。
- 来源可靠性：每项带 `trust`（`core_workspace|core_record|core_event|verified_evidence`）、`source_hash`、`plan_binding`（`bound|unbound`）、`trust_scope`（`memory.py:564-581`，明确"仅证明来源记录，不证明领域真值"）；召回时逐项重算快照哈希并与当前 Core 行比对（`:446-563`），不一致即丢弃（`test_memory_m6.py:231-232`）。
- 反幻觉硬约束：`status="confirmed"` 一律拒绝（`memory.py:76-77`），召回项恒 `hypothesis`（`:475,569`；`test_memory_m6.py:136,191,304`）。
- 冲突：仅 `memory_key` 维度（第 2.2 节），派生源无冲突合并。
- 过期过滤：`valid_until`（`memory.py:401`）；撤销源 `revoked_memory_sources` 逐项过滤（`:403-409,450-457`；`test_memory_m6.py:192-196,360-382`）。
- 事实层缺口：capsule 顶层 `facts` 永为 `[]`（`context_service.py:308`；`test_context_m6.py:84` 明确断言）。可信证据只在 `tasks[].facts`/`evidence_refs`（`context_service.py:136-145`），未上卷到会话级事实。

### 2.4 Agent 间通信协议

- 消息类型是**常量集合**，不是 enum 类型系统：`WORKER_COMMANDS`（6）与 `WORKER_FACTS`（7）为 `frozenset`（`event_domain.py:16-36`），`URGENT_EVENTS`（`:37-44`）；payload 自由 JSON（`events.payload TEXT`，`migrations.py:69-72`），无 per-type schema。
- **持久化消息 + 状态机是真实的**：`events`+`outbox` 同事务（`store.py:141-158`）；`event_deliveries.state CHECK ('pending','leased','delivered','dead','skipped')`（`dispatcher_schema.py:13-20`）；`event_inbox` 带 `notice_attempts/notice_next_attempt/notice_dead_at/notice_token`（`:23-31`）；`worker_inbox`（`worker_schema.py:5-8`）在 `worker_runtime.py:1071-1096` 转成 user 消息并注明"untrusted, not authority"。
- 命令→状态迁移真实：`dispatcher.py:305-342` 把 `worker.command.pause/resume/cancel` 映射到 `paused/queued/cancelled`，校验前置状态（`:314-320`）与 Quest 授权（`:321-326`）。
- 缺口：①`worker.command.assign` 只在 `event_domain.py:18` 定义，全仓无生产点；worker 实际由 `WorkerScheduler.tick` → `manager.start` 启动（`worker_runtime.py:1886-1893`）。②无"agent→agent 直接消息"类型；`worker.help_requested` 只进 composer（`main.py:354`），限 2 次（`worker_runtime.py:763-768`）。③路由白名单硬编码在 `_routable`（`dispatcher.py:144-161`），新增消费者需改代码。

### 2.5 治理：风险分级、审批绑定、预算熔断

- **风险分级：真实且失败关闭。** `ACTION_RISKS` 固定映射 6 个动作（`governance.py:16-25`）；未知名 `DomainError("Unknown action is denied")`（`:38-42`）；R3 在申请与授权两侧恒拒（`:191-192`、`:353-354`）；R0/R1 要求 `parameters["path"]` 落在 `resource_scope` 内（`:361-367`），R1 还要匹配当前 plan_revision 的 `task_grants`（`:370-379`）。
- **审批绑定：真实且强。** 7 元组绑定（quest_id、plan_revision、action_type、parameter_digest、resource_scope、risk、policy_version，`:387-395`）；不匹配即置 `REVOKED`/`EXPIRED` 并抛错（`:396-417`）；`consumed_at IS NULL` 单次消费（`:403-406`）；过期在读取与决策两处检查（`:254-268`、`:307-311`）；完成门要求 `decided <= consumed < expires`（`evidence.py:36-52`）。工具侧有等价检查并原子消费（`tool_engine.py:369-399`）。
- **预算熔断：真实，双层次。** ①模型层：`admit` 逐次 HTTP 预留（`model_call_budget.py:145-455`），`settle` 发现超用置 `breached=1`（`:468-482`），此后 `admit` 直接 `BudgetExceeded("ledger is fenced")`（`:170-173`）；429 冷却共享（`:116-133`，`tests/test_model_call_budget.py:280`）。②Worker 层：token/cost 预留失败即 `worker.blocked`（`worker_runtime.py:1396-1447`，`reason_code=token_budget|cost_budget`），叠加 `steps/tool_spent` 上限（`:1301-1303,1643-1645`）。
- 运维缺口：`breached=1` 之后只有"重新对账"路径（`model_call_budget.py:182-193` 要求 `reconciled_cost`），**没有运营解封接口**；触发后需手改库。
- 漂移风险：风险表有两份 —— `governance.ACTION_RISKS`（`governance.py:16-25`）与各工具 `risk` 字段（`tool_domain.py:97-191`），靠"工具名 == action_type"对齐（R2 仅 `browser_get`/`mcp_call` 两表都有，`tool_domain.py:178,191`）。新 R2 工具若忘加名，审批会因 "Unknown action is denied" 失败（失败关闭，但会卡死功能）。

"""Task-centric, integrity-checked context archives backed by SQLite."""

import hashlib
import json

from .domain import DomainError, now_iso


def _json(value):
    return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))


def _hash(value):
    return hashlib.sha256(_json(value).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def _merge_messages(previous, rows):
    merged = [item for item in previous if item.get("role") == "user"]
    highlights = [item for item in previous if item.get("role") != "user"]
    positions = {(item["text"], item["status"]): item for item in merged}
    for row in rows:
        if row["role"] != "user":
            highlights.append(
                {
                    "text": row["content"][:256],
                    "source_refs": [row["id"]],
                    "status": "unverified",
                    "role": row["role"],
                    "omitted": len(row["content"]) > 256,
                }
            )
            continue
        key = (row["content"], "unverified")
        if key not in positions:
            item = {
                "text": row["content"],
                "source_refs": [],
                "status": "unverified",
                "role": "user",
                "omitted": False,
            }
            positions[key] = item
            merged.append(item)
        positions[key]["source_refs"].append(row["id"])
    return merged + highlights[-16:]


def _task_context(connection):
    quests = connection.execute(
        "SELECT * FROM quests WHERE conversation_id='main' AND status NOT IN ('completed','cancelled','failed') ORDER BY id LIMIT 101"
    ).fetchall()
    if len(quests) > 100:
        raise DomainError("Too many active Quests for safe compaction")
    result = []
    for quest in quests:
        qid = quest["id"]
        requirement = connection.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM quest_requirements WHERE quest_id=?", (qid,)
        ).fetchone()
        current_plan = connection.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM quest_plans WHERE quest_id=? AND revision=?",
            (qid, quest["plan_revision"]),
        ).fetchone()
        plan = (
            current_plan
            if current_plan
            and current_plan["approved_at"] is not None
            and current_plan["status"] in ("approved", "paused")
            else None
        )
        plan_state = "approved" if plan else "pending" if quest["plan_revision"] else "none"
        nodes = (
            connection.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM task_nodes WHERE plan_id=? ORDER BY node_key", (plan["id"],)
            ).fetchall()
            if plan
            else []
        )
        evidence = connection.execute(
            "SELECT id,kind,trusted,payload,created_at FROM evidence WHERE quest_id=? ORDER BY id",
            (qid,),
        ).fetchall()
        receipts = connection.execute(
            "SELECT r.id,r.execution_mode,r.result_digest,i.tool_name,i.resource_scope,i.plan_revision FROM action_receipts r JOIN action_intents i ON i.id=r.intent_id WHERE i.quest_id=? ORDER BY r.id",
            (qid,),
        ).fetchall()
        tasks = [
            {
                "key": node["node_key"],
                "objective": node["objective"],
                "success_criteria": json.loads(node["criteria_json"]),
                "status": node["status"],
                "expected_artifact": node["expected_artifact"],
                "allowed_tools": json.loads(node["allowed_tools"]),
                "evidence_refs": json.loads(node["evidence_refs"]),
            }
            for node in nodes
        ]
        result.append(
            {
                "quest_id": qid,
                "goal": quest["goal"],
                "status": quest["status"],
                "version": quest["version"],
                "source_refs": [f"quest:{qid}"],
                "success_criteria": json.loads(requirement["criteria_json"]) if requirement else [],
                "constraints": json.loads(quest["metadata"]),
                "plan_id": plan["id"] if plan else None,
                "plan_state": plan_state,
                "plan_revision": quest["plan_revision"],
                "pending_plan_id": current_plan["id"]
                if current_plan and not plan and current_plan["status"] == "proposed"
                else None,
                "decisions": [
                    {
                        "type": "approved_plan",
                        "source_refs": [f"plan:{plan['id']}"],
                        "digest": plan["digest"],
                    }
                ]
                if plan
                else [],
                "completed_steps": [node for node in tasks if node["status"] == "succeeded"],
                "pending_steps": [
                    node for node in tasks if node["status"] not in ("succeeded", "skipped")
                ],
                "blockers": [node for node in tasks if node["status"] == "blocked"],
                "artifacts": [
                    node["expected_artifact"] for node in tasks if node["expected_artifact"]
                ],
                "paths": [
                    receipt["resource_scope"]
                    for receipt in receipts
                    if receipt["plan_revision"] == quest["plan_revision"]
                ],
                "evidence_refs": [row["id"] for row in evidence if row["trusted"]],
                "facts": [
                    {
                        "statement": "Trusted evidence recorded",
                        "kind": row["kind"],
                        "source_refs": [f"evidence:{row['id']}"],
                    }
                    for row in evidence
                    if row["trusted"]
                ],
                "hypotheses": [
                    {
                        "statement": row["payload"],
                        "source_refs": [f"evidence:{row['id']}"],
                        "status": "unverified",
                    }
                    for row in evidence
                    if not row["trusted"]
                ],
                "receipts": [
                    {**dict(row), "historical": row["plan_revision"] != quest["plan_revision"]}
                    for row in receipts
                ],
            }
        )
    return result


class ContextService:
    def __init__(self, store):
        self.store = store

    @staticmethod
    def _through(connection, scope, scope_id):
        row = connection.execute(
            "SELECT through FROM context_archive_heads WHERE scope=? AND scope_id=?",
            (scope, scope_id),
        ).fetchone()
        return row["through"] if row else -1

    def _record_archive(self, connection, scope, scope_id, sources, capsule, through):
        inserted = connection.execute(
            "INSERT INTO context_archives(scope,scope_id,source_json,source_hash,capsule_json,capsule_hash,created_at) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
            (
                scope,
                scope_id,
                _json(sources),
                _hash(sources),
                _json(capsule),
                _hash(capsule),
                now_iso(),
            ),
        )
        archive_id = inserted.lastrowid
        connection.executemany(
            "INSERT INTO context_archive_sources VALUES (?,?,?,?)",
            [(scope, scope_id, str(source["id"]), archive_id) for source in sources],
        )
        connection.execute(
            "INSERT INTO context_archive_heads VALUES (?,?,?,?) ON CONFLICT(scope,scope_id) DO UPDATE SET through=excluded.through,archive_id=excluded.archive_id",
            (scope, scope_id, through, archive_id),
        )

    def _verify_source(self, connection, scope, scope_id, source_id):
        index = connection.execute(
            "SELECT a.source_json,a.source_hash FROM context_archive_sources s JOIN context_archives a ON a.id=s.archive_id WHERE s.scope=? AND s.scope_id=? AND s.source_id=?",
            (scope, scope_id, str(source_id)),
        ).fetchone()
        if index is None:
            raise DomainError("Context source integrity failure")
        sources = json.loads(index["source_json"])
        if _hash(sources) != index["source_hash"]:
            raise DomainError("Context archive integrity failure")
        entry = next((item for item in sources if str(item["id"]) == str(source_id)), None)
        if scope == "router":
            current = connection.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM messages WHERE conversation_id=? AND id=?", (scope_id, source_id)
            ).fetchone()
        else:
            current = connection.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM worker_messages WHERE run_id=? AND ordinal=?", (scope_id, source_id)
            ).fetchone()
        if entry is None or current is None or _hash(dict(current)) != entry["hash"]:
            raise DomainError("Context source integrity failure")
        return current

    def router_snapshot(self):
        with self.store.connection() as connection:
            connection.execute("BEGIN")
            state = dict(
                connection.execute(
                    "SELECT * FROM router_state WHERE conversation_id='main'"
                ).fetchone()
            )
            through = self._through(connection, "router", "main")
            messages = [
                dict(row)
                for row in connection.execute(
                    "SELECT * FROM messages WHERE conversation_id='main' AND rowid>? ORDER BY rowid LIMIT 510",
                    (through,),
                )
            ]
            connection.commit()
        return {"state": state, "messages": messages}

    def _archives(self, connection, scope, scope_id):
        rows = connection.execute(
            "SELECT a.* FROM context_archive_heads h JOIN context_archives a ON a.id=h.archive_id WHERE h.scope=? AND h.scope_id=?",
            (scope, scope_id),
        ).fetchall()
        for row in rows:
            sources, capsule = json.loads(row["source_json"]), json.loads(row["capsule_json"])
            if _hash(sources) != row["source_hash"] or _hash(capsule) != row["capsule_hash"]:
                raise DomainError("Context archive integrity failure")
            refs = [
                ref for item in capsule.get("hypotheses", []) for ref in item.get("source_refs", [])
            ]
            refs += [
                ref
                for item in capsule.get("completed_steps", [])
                if isinstance(item, dict)
                for ref in item.get("source_refs", [])
            ]
            for ref in refs:
                self._verify_source(connection, scope, scope_id, ref)
