# ADR 009: Source-bound planning, independent review and durable coordination

Status: Phase 2 implementation in progress; local and live acceptance are recorded separately.
Date: 2026-11-15.

## Context

ADRs [007](ADR-007-native-worker-and-execution-evidence.md) and
[008](ADR-008-context-recall-budget.md) establish approved native execution, trusted
receipts, bounded context and Gateway admission. Phase 2 needs stronger planning,
revision and collaboration without replacing those controls or adding user chats.

## Decision

1. Keep the persistent Router as the only user-facing Agent. A separate Planner
   consumes the original request, source hashes, constraints and offered tools to
   propose a bounded DAG. A proposal never grants execution authority; plan and
   team approval continue to require the authenticated local user.
2. Store literal user clauses, pending model extractions and separately confirmed
   clauses with distinct provenance. Bound context highlights and retain original
   source readback paths. Conflicts, omissions, expiry and revocation remain visible;
   extracted instructions never substitute for action approval.
3. Review a delivery in a fresh context containing the original contract, criteria,
   bounded actual artifacts and verified receipts. Do not copy the Worker's private
   conversation. Bind the verdict to its input hash and admitted model attempt.
   `NEEDS_REVISION` requires concrete goals and consumes the existing bounded budget.
   A fresh PASS is necessary for review criteria but remains subject to NodeVerifier
   and CompletionGate checks. The current reviewer uses the approved Worker's model;
   separate context does not establish independent model identity.
4. Project typed Agent messages from the existing durable event/outbox transport.
   Preserve task identity, lease fencing, Inbox deduplication and Router-mediated
   control. Agent messages confer no right to mutate another Worker's assignment.
5. Reuse observed model performance as a sourced, sample-counted input to new team
   proposals. Preserve explicit user scores, approved profile hashes, completed
   nodes and historical contracts. Replacement never resets cumulative budgets.

## Consequences and limits

The implementation adds focused services and schema changes rather than a parallel
runtime. Default Review autonomy, policy, exact approvals, receipts and Gateway
reservations remain authoritative. Unknown remote effects stay unresolved until
trusted recovery conditions permit settlement; a client timeout permits no replay.

Schema repair, review rounds, Agent counts, context packets and replanning are
bounded. General automatic remaining-DAG replanning, arbitrary hierarchical Agent
expansion, exhaustive per-message payload schemas and learned semantic retrieval
remain incomplete. The legacy summary-only delivery contract stays compatible;
`delivery_review` explicitly requires all eight delivery fields. Local/Mock tests
and synthetic benchmarks do not establish complex live-task acceptance. See the
[Phase 2 report](../PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md) for the current evidence.

The current execution boundary remains the fixed Core toolset: bounded numeric
AST, syntax checks and diagnostics, with create-only file writes. General program
execution, arbitrary test runners, artifact patching and running-DAG revision are
not supplied by introducing fresh review or typed coordination.
# Phase 2 — Actual Agent Execution Chain Audit

Date: 2026-11-15 (Asia/Shanghai). Branch: `codex/phase1-continuous`.
This is a source/retained-evidence audit of the evolving Phase 2 working tree, not a
frozen acceptance result. Root is the unique integration owner. Phase 1 M1–M7 reports,
the M7 backend-hardening report, required architecture/protocol documents, and the
named Router/Worker/team/graph/dispatcher/context/memory/provider/tool/evidence/
governance modules were read. Earlier audits under `_audit/` describe the pre-change
state; conclusions below include the current Phase 2 changes.

## Executable chain

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    U[One main user conversation] --> R[Persistent Router: observe, recall, strict decision]
    R -->|chat| A[One user-facing response]
    R -->|create Quest and durable quest.proposed| D[Dispatcher: outbox, leases, inbox, dedup]
    D --> P[Separate Planner: original request, constraints, strict bounded DAG]
    P --> PA[Pending plan: digest, revision, criteria, dependencies]
    PA -->|authenticated local user approves| C[Composer: model profiles, online observations, hard budgets]
    C --> TA[Pending team: roles and models decoupled]
    TA -->|authenticated local user approves| S[WorkerScheduler: ready nodes and concurrency]
    S --> W[Native Worker: private context, model/tool loop, checkpoints]
    W --> T[ToolEngine: policy, grants, exact approvals, intent and receipt]
    T --> W
    W -->|structured worker.result| V[Fresh independent review context]
    V -->|NEEDS_REVISION with concrete goals| RW[Bounded revision of same approved assignment]
    RW --> W
    V -->|PASS| N[NodeVerifier: current provenance and fixed criteria checks]
    N --> G[CompletionGate: recheck approved plan, receipts and evidence]
    G --> Q[Verified task and Quest transitions]
    Q --> D
    D --> RN[Router notice: silent or user progress/result update]
    RN --> A
    W -->|help or blocker event| D
    D -->|help: pending approved replacement proposal| C
    X[ProviderGateway and durable admission ledger] -. all model calls .-> R
    X -.-> P
    X -.-> C
    X -.-> W
    X -.-> V
    M[Task capsules, constraints, source archives and memory] -. bounded context .-> R
    M -. original source recovery .-> W
```

`forge_api.main._core_lifespan` starts six background loops: Dispatcher, Router notices,
Planner, Composer, WorkerScheduler, and review/verification. Provider latency runs
outside SQLite write transactions. A proposal is not an approved plan, an approved
team, a running Worker or a completed task.

1. `RouterService.handle_user_message` synchronizes memory, observes a bounded snapshot,
   calls the configured Gateway, validates `RouterDecision`, and permits one bounded
   schema-repair request. The final user/assistant messages, Quest, source constraints,
   events and idempotent turn record commit atomically. Chat creates no Quest/Worker.
2. `process_pending_plan` consumes the durable creation event. `QuestGraphService.generate`
   receives the original user-message ID/content with its hash, sourced constraints,
   offered tool catalogue and capability names. Generated plans are limited to eight
   nodes/sixteen edges; invalid names/graphs receive one repair opportunity. `propose`
   persists the DAG; `approve` binds authenticated actor, revision, digest and version.
3. `process_pending_team` proposes bounded role contracts. `TeamComposerEngine.compose`
   filters tool/context/cost/budget incompatibilities and offers single-model, greedy,
   coverage and complementarity search. `performance_snapshot` supplies separate,
   source-digested live/Mock observations with sample counts and Wilson intervals for
   rates; it does not rewrite manually supplied capability scores or infer task success
   from transport success. Team approval binds the plan and selected profile hashes.
4. `WorkerScheduler.tick` launches only approved, ready assignments. `WorkerManager.start`
   checks dependencies, effective tool scope, model identity and token/tool/time/agent/
   depth/concurrency limits. `_run` owns a native checkpointed model/tool loop. `_repair`
   preserves failed diagnostics and bounded repair history; provider, contract, budget,
   dependency, authorization, code and tool failures have distinct classifications.
5. `ToolEngine.prepare/execute` enforces current permissions before action, persists an
   exact intent and records its receipt. R1 writes require a Workspace grant; R2 requires
   exact action approval and operator allowlists; unknown/R3 actions fail closed.
   Uncertain external effects are not silently repeated after restart or reassignment.
6. `IndependentReviewService` constructs a fresh packet from the original contract,
   criteria, structured delivery, actual bounded artifacts and trustworthy receipts.
   It does not copy the Worker's private conversation. It currently uses the same
   approved underlying model in a separate context: independent context is not model
   diversity. PASS/NEEDS_REVISION/REJECT/BLOCKED are schema-checked; revision requires
   concrete goals and has a default two-round limit. Budget and source bindings persist.
7. `NodeVerifier` requires the applicable fresh PASS, then performs fixed JSON or numeric
   semantic verification. `CompletionGate` revalidates approved historical/current
   bindings, original execution mode, actual tool results and artifact hashes before
   completion. Model self-report or Mock evidence alone cannot establish live completion.
8. `Dispatcher` delivers typed event facts at least once with Inbox deduplication and
   fencing. `AgentMessage.from_event` projects task identity and structured coordination
   kinds. Workers cannot directly edit another Worker's task. Only Router appends the
   selected user-facing update to `main`.

## Evidence classification

| Capability | Current implementation | Verification category and limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Persistent single Router/conversation, SQLite UoW/CAS, migrations | Real code and durable records | Local restart/transaction tests; Phase 1 M1–M7 retained evidence |
| Strict Router/Planner decisions and bounded repair | Real Gateway-backed production paths | Current B/F 53-test focused suite; reasoning/orchestration assertions are Mock |
| Planner from original request and source constraints | Separate production component | Mock strict-wire, integrity, catalogue and node-limit regressions |
| Dynamic role/model selection and approved replacement | Real bounded composer/scheduler | Offline/synthetic comparisons and Mock integration; no general live superiority claim |
| Model online statistics | Actual bounded Core observations | Provenance/sample counts retained; sparse priors are not measured abilities |
| Native Worker tools/checkpoints | Real runtime and governed local tools | Phase 1 M5 live numeric/JSON demonstrations; current new recovery branches tested locally/Mock |
| Independent fresh-context review and revision | Real production service and evidence binding | New Mock/adversarial coverage; current complex live review/rework E2E still unverified here |
| Task capsules, constraints, source readback | Real hash-checked archives and index | 39 context/memory tests; M6 retained narrow live continuation; no infinite-capacity claim |
| Recall | Keyword/source/Quest/time/type filters and bilingual aliases | 9/9 exploratory synthetic source-ID/hash cases; learned semantic/embedding recall absent |
| Agent communication | Durable existing event bus with typed projection | Core identity checks and bounded event flow; exhaustive per-type payload contracts remain partial |
| Full autonomous remaining-DAG replanning | Existing proposal/control/replacement interfaces | General automatic safe replanning and hierarchical expansion remain incomplete |
| Independent Reviewer model selection | Same approved model with fresh context | Separate Reviewer model diversity remains an extension, not implemented evidence |
| Complex multi-domain autonomous completion after failure/rework/restart | Components now connected | Must be judged by retained L1/L2/L3 live runs; unverified at this audit snapshot |

The old narrow output-schema compatibility contract still permits summary-only results;
`delivery_review` explicitly requires all eight delivery fields. Do not state that every
legacy Worker contract enforces all eight fields. Default autonomy remains Review:
model-generated plans, teams and replacements remain pending until authenticated approval.

## Actual live Provider evidence

The new retained probe is
`.local/phase2/provider/20261114T233125Z-d07064/report.json`: **11/11 small protocol cases**,
26.712 seconds, `wb-local`, self-reported `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, Gateway through loopback
`127.0.0.1:8788/v1`. It covers minimal dialogue, three Router-schema responses, three tool
call responses, bounded context recall, two concurrent calls and streaming. Discovery
returned eleven IDs and included the requested model. The 300,000-token admission ceiling
and concurrency two were finite configuration, not consumed tokens or service maxima.

These records distinguish proxy response, returned model response and case correctness.
Upstream identity remains **unverified_proxy_reported_identity**. Actual maximum context,
output, rate limits and cost remain unknown; the 65,536 context and 1,024 probe-output
ceilings are operator bounds. Protocol success is not an autonomous task-completion result.
Phase 1 M5 additionally retains a real numeric tool run and one JSON-syntax completion;
M6 retains one narrow continuation success after five preserved diagnostic failures.

## Continuity and open boundaries

`ConstraintService` separates literal user clauses, pending model extracts and separately
confirmed records, with original IDs/hashes, potential conflicts, expiry and revocation.
Router/Worker highlights are bounded; omitted originals remain in archives and can be
re-read with source checks. L0 recent interaction, L1 Quest, L2 project/history and L3
failure-experience paths exist. Active Quest counts, indexing batches, candidate pages,
artifact/receipt snapshots and model windows remain finite; learned semantic retrieval,
general source relevance and arbitrary-scale continuity are not established.

Recovery uses durable Worker/model/tool state and lease generations. Unknown remote
outcomes retain reservations until trusted recovery conditions permit action. The current
live driver tests storage compaction/readback and restart at the approved-plan boundary;
that alone would not prove safe recovery from an arbitrary in-flight external action.
The independent driver's five offline tests verify missing DB handling, actual budget
inspection, genuine archive/readback, no-op truthfulness and visible integrity failure.
Desktop packaging/UI acceptance is deferred; no new desktop-release claim follows.

The fixed tool contracts do not provide arbitrary shell, unrestricted Python,
arbitrary test commands or a general patch operation. `python_compile` proves
syntax only, `numeric_ast` executes a bounded pure numeric subset and
`shell_inspect` permits only `python_version`. `file_write` creates files with
exclusive-create semantics. A review revision cannot generally edit an existing
artifact in place. Team replacement keeps the approved DAG; Router goal updates
and new DAG proposals remain limited to proposed/awaiting-approval Quests, so
general running-DAG replanning is still absent. Source retrieval remains lexical.
# Sprint F — Source-linked Constraints and Bounded Context

Date: 2026-11-15 (Asia/Shanghai). Integration owner: root agent. Scope: backend context,
memory, source-linked user constraints and offline retrieval evaluation. No Provider or
credential files were read by this subtask; no live model call was made.

## Audit result and changes

The M6 archive stored every distinct user message verbatim in the next capsule. It
preserved originals but increased every subsequent model input indefinitely. The early
Phase 2 Router stored extracted constraints in `memories` as hypotheses; a key derived
from the full statement did not associate different budget statements for conflict
detection, and those rows lacked source-content hashes or confirmation provenance.

The existing SQLite archive, source-integrity checks, transaction boundaries, Gateway,
and Worker tool-pair protection are retained. The Phase 2 v10 migration also installs
`constraint_records`, `constraint_message_index` and an incremental source cursor.

- `ConstraintService.index_message` associates the current original user message with
  the Router-selected Quest. Reindexing is idempotent; changed source content and an
  attempted conflicting reassignment fail closed. Message metadata supplied by a caller
  does not establish Quest association.
- A bounded literal extractor copies at most eight short clauses per user message.
  Its origin is `explicit_user`; model-derived paraphrases remain `pending_model`.
  A separate confirmation operation requires another user message containing both a
  confirmation expression and the exact clause. Confirmations have their own source ID
  and hash. These labels describe instruction provenance, not domain facts or approval.
- Records retain original message IDs, SHA-256, Quest association, dimension, origin,
  optional timezone-aware expiry and revocation state. Budget/deadline/language/retention/
  scope/model dimensions allow **potential** conflicts to remain visible. A changed,
  missing, expired or revoked source is excluded. Conflicting statements are not resolved
  by silently choosing the newest one.
- Router archives retain at most 64 user highlights within 12,288 encoded bytes and 16
  other highlights within 4,096 bytes. Individual user highlights are bounded UTF-8
  excerpts. Initial anchors and recent items are favored; omissions and source-recall
  entry points are recorded. Duplicate messages have at most four source references in
  a highlight. Originals remain in `messages` and source archives.
- Worker archives bound claims and completed-tool highlights, retain the initial task
  contract and live tool-call/result pair, and trim archived highlights to the actual
  input budget before committing. Trusted receipts and original worker messages remain
  in their durable stores. Bounded sourced constraints are included in Worker context;
  archived Router rebuilds refresh constraint records from the current source store.
- Per-Quest evidence and receipt snapshots are capped at 64 entries each and explicitly
  indicate omissions. The independent evidence gate continues to use authoritative
  execution records; a context snapshot is not completion authority.
- Memory indexing processes at most 128 source messages per batch. It stores source
  hashes, terms and bounded clauses rather than another copy of the full corpus.
  Archived original messages are therefore retrievable after their highlights leave
  the capsule. L0 labels current interactions; archived sources use L1 for an associated
  Quest or L2 for unassociated history. Existing Quest, project and failure indexing
  retains the L1/L2/L3 paths.
- Recall supports bounded keyword/source/Quest lookup, a small bilingual alias expansion,
  timezone-aware time filters and source-type filters. The alias dictionary helps with
  cases such as `spending` → `预算`, but this is **lexical retrieval**, not embedding or
  learned semantic retrieval.

## Verification

Commands run from `backend`, using its existing virtual environment:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/test_constraints_phase2.py tests/test_context_m6.py tests/test_memory_m6.py -q --junitxml=../docs/audit/phase2/sprint-f-tests.xml
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/phase2/retrieval_evaluation.py --output ../docs/audit/phase2/retrieval-evaluation-v2.json
```

The focused source/context/memory run passed **39 tests in 15.42 seconds** (8 new tests
plus the 31 existing M6 context/memory tests). These are offline deterministic/Mock
tests. They cover pending versus confirmed provenance, exact original-source IDs,
confirmation tampering, conflict visibility, expiry, revocation, Quest isolation,
transaction rollback, duplicate-reference bounds, UTF-8 budgets, and recall/readback of
an omitted message after three compactions and a storage reopen. The raw history in
that continuity test contains 240 messages; every original remains available.

Ruff check and format checks passed for this subtask's seven Python files. The root
agent runs the complete integration checks and records their frozen-source results.

The fixed `phase2-retrieval-v1` evaluation passed **9/9 exploratory synthetic cases**.
Dataset SHA-256:
`6d4dd52492b4bb9e55db3dcbff5f5bd49ddfa260665504356097eeede92a533b`.
The evaluator checks expected source identities and independently recomputed source
hashes after reopening storage. It covers bilingual budget/retention/deadline queries,
language, a file-path reference, a recorded decision, historical Quest identity,
Quest-associated constraints, and a time-exclusion query. The v1 diagnostic output is
preserved; v2 additionally records and validates actual source hashes. Neither output
contains model calls, external tool execution, model quality measurements or live
domain-task success evidence.

`tests/test_router_intelligence_phase2.py` adds separate Mock Router/Planner regressions
for bounded repair, atomic failure, constraint provenance, original-request integrity,
planning contract names, node limits and single-Router recovery. Their final integrated
focused run passed **14/14 in 1.68 seconds**. An initial run identified a missing
autonomous-Planner capability-name check; root integrated the fix and also checks generated
tools against the actual offered catalogue. Known-but-unavailable R2 tools, repeated invalid
plans, missing original requests and overlarge autonomous DAGs are covered.

The final combined B/F focused run passed **53 tests in 18.36 seconds**:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/test_constraints_phase2.py tests/test_context_m6.py tests/test_memory_m6.py tests/test_router_intelligence_phase2.py -q --junitxml=../docs/audit/phase2/sprint-bf-integrated-tests.xml
```

The complete backend suite remains root's integration responsibility. None of these
53 tests is a live-provider validation.

## Limits

The literal extractor is deliberately small and cannot establish the semantics of every
quoted, conditional or implied user instruction. Pending model extracts require source
review; a literal user clause is not automatically an authenticated action approval.
Potential-conflict dimensions may require user clarification. Confirmation/revocation
are Core service operations; this subtask does not add a public user interface for them.

The fixed retrieval corpus is small and exploratory. It does not measure unconstrained
semantic retrieval, learned relevance, Router task understanding, or model correctness.
Candidate pages, active-Quest snapshots and per-call indexing remain bounded. Long
histories can require multiple indexing batches or source reads; arbitrary-scale memory
and unbounded storage are not claimed. Omitted context never implies that the underlying
record, requirement, receipt or artifact does not exist.

# Sprint D / E / G — Worker recovery, independent review and communication

Date: 2026-11-15, Asia/Shanghai. This subreport records local engineering
verification. No Provider network call was performed by this implementation
subtask. Root integration owns the live experiments and final acceptance.

## Audit and preserved implementation

Phase 1 already supplied native model/tool loops, hidden Worker contexts,
approved model/role contracts, durable leases, cumulative allocations, governed
tools, intent/receipt evidence, upstream receipt reads and independent fixed
JSON/numeric verifiers. Those mechanisms are reused. Existing uncommitted Phase
2 delivery-schema and repair-counter changes were preserved and corrected.

The initial repair implementation could leave a failed call `running` and repeat
it before asking the model to repair. Invalid-schema/help responses also left
their pessimistic local reservation charged despite known usage. Expanding the
fallback output schema for old schema-less contracts could exhaust a small
context before tests reached the model, causing a waiting concurrency fixture to
hang. These defects were reproduced or identified in source and fixed.

## Worker execution and recovery

New roles retain the eight-field delivery schema. Explicit `delivery_review`
and `json_review:@delivery` criteria require all eight fields and a finite
confidence in [0,1]. Historical schema-less contracts keep their original narrow
summary schema; their permissions/context reservation are not silently expanded.
Result events record which delivery fields were actually supplied.

Known model responses settle actual token/cost usage before output validation.
Schema failures receive bounded structured feedback. Repair has a cumulative
counter (default two; hard configurable range zero through four), and also
consumes the original step/token/tool/time budgets. Resource, task-contract,
provider, authorization, dependency, code and tool failures remain distinguishable.

A Provider `truncated` response can enter that same bounded repair loop only
with valid known usage. Live provenance additionally requires the exact current
call/provider/model/Worker usage to match a settled Gateway attempt. Its actual
charge is retained before requesting a compact complete delivery. Partial
content and tool calls are discarded without creating tool intents or receipts;
the rejection event records usage and zero executed calls. Timeout, transport
errors and unsettled live outcomes retain their original reservations and do
not enter truncation repair. Concise delivery instructions keep findings brief
and cite exact evidence/path references instead of duplicating source excerpts.

An active Worker now renews its current lease between completed model/tool
steps, after rechecking its token, generation, approved plan/team and running
Quest. Renewal cannot revive an expired/stale claim and is capped by the
original task deadline. Each individual call remains bounded by the current
lease (normally 60 seconds) and task deadline; there is no in-flight heartbeat
or increased task allocation. A sent timeout keeps the unknown Gateway attempt
and local reservation, with no replay. Failure events record only fixed
exception-type labels; an outer built-in `TimeoutError` is classified as
`timeout` without writing exception text or arbitrary class names.

The retained live L1 workspace `ws-20261115T001324Z-L1-70d6a4` was inspected
read-only: creation at 00:14:28.284 UTC and blocking at 00:15:28.353 UTC match
the original 60-second lease. Its fourth attempt began at 00:15:05.349 UTC,
remains reserved with no usage, and no truncation repair ran. A read-only
SQLite backup of that database supplied the original Worker messages, tools,
model and output limit to the real Gateway with a delayed HTTP MockTransport;
the outer timeout reproduced a built-in `TimeoutError` and reserved attempt.
This diagnostic made zero network calls and did not alter the live workspace.

`file_write` retains create-only semantics. The new, separately approved R1
`file_revise` requires `path`, `prior_receipt_id`, `expected_sha256` and complete
new `content`. Its source must be this same Worker's latest successful produced
version, backed by an intact `file_write` / `file_revise` receipt chain. A shared
read-only helper validates every version's run/worker/plan/mode, successful
call/intent/receipt, parameter/result/content hashes and unchanged path. Earlier
full bytes remain in immutable intent parameters; immutable receipts link the
versions. The tool rechecks active generation, plan/team, workspace grant,
current hash and file identity under the Core write lock immediately before
atomic replacement. Unknown replacement results retain uncertain state and
block replay. User files and predecessor artifacts cannot establish ownership.
Existing contracts gain no tool authority. Only an explicitly approved
`file_revise` scope receives bounded Core artifact receipt references in model
context; these references consume the same context/token budget.

Failed fixed R0 diagnostics and local reads may inform a new model-selected
call only after validating their genuine failed receipt. Failed local
`file_read` / `directory_list` operations now produce a real failure receipt for
bounded OS/encoding/policy errors; stale authorization still produces uncertain
state. A Core pre-execution R0 denial can be repaired only after proving there
is no action intent for the call, persisting the rejection/parameter digest and
the actual diagnostic tool reply. This produces no fictional success receipt.
External or uncertain effects retain the original fail-closed behavior.

The failed call remains in history, and is never replayed by the repair loop.
`settled_read_failure` validates the provenance both for restart and for the
completion gate. Batched tool replies stay contiguous; repair instructions are
inside the failing tool feedback rather than inserted between pending replies.

## Independent review and revision

`IndependentReviewService` is an explicitly approved validation stage of the
same node contract. It uses that node's approved Provider/model through the
native Gateway. It is **independent context with the same model**, not evidence
of model diversity or a separate specialist model. Supported criteria are:

- `delivery_review` / `json_review:@delivery`: eight-field delivery plus at least
  one successful authorized tool receipt; no file write is required.
- `json_review:<workspace path>`: actual produced JSON artifact, matching live
  receipt/hash and deterministic JSON verification before model judgment.

The review packet contains the original user message ID/hash where recorded,
the latest goal-update message where recorded, source-linked constraints,
original task/node contract, final delivery and validated receipts/artifacts.
It does not contain the Worker conversation or private reasoning. Packet size
is bounded at 64 KiB and oversized input blocks review rather than truncating
evidence silently. Registered structured-output support enables native JSON
schema requests; unsupported Providers use prompt formatting and strict local
validation.

Review returns only `PASS`, `NEEDS_REVISION`, `REJECT` or `BLOCKED`, findings,
explicit revision goals and bounded confidence. A PASS is rechecked against the
current source packet and a settled Gateway attempt. Mock review cannot prove
live completion. Deterministic artifact/receipt checks remain necessary; a model
review is a domain-quality assessment, not a mathematical correctness proof.

`NEEDS_REVISION` resumes only the same `review_pending` Worker after validating
the current result/review event. It preserves the original approved model,
tools, completed sibling nodes, cumulative budgets and historical receipts.
The old delivery remains recorded. There is no reopening of completed nodes,
no permission expansion and no budget reset. A committed revision verdict is replayed idempotently after restart if Core stopped before requeue. The service defaults to two review
rounds, with a hard upper bound of four.

The review stage charges the same Worker token/step/currency counters and the
Gateway's existing global/quest/team/worker admission ledger. Approval budgets
must include review and possible revision. Capacity pressure proved unsent
refunds its reservation, queues with bounded backoff and consumes no semantic
review round. Started claims have durable leases. After restart, a settled or
rejected attempt, or a trusted expired remote isolation bound, permits bounded
recovery. Unknown remote outcomes keep their reservation and emit one explicit
recovery-blocked event; they are never blindly retried. The Gateway atomically
fences stale/refunded reviewer claims before HTTP admission. Defensive late
response accounting cannot subtract an already refunded reservation, and stale
results cannot replace a current review.

Malformed produced JSON now yields bounded `NEEDS_REVISION` feedback labelled
`deterministic_artifact_validation` from the Core JSON parser. It creates no
fictional Provider attempt or PASS; a corrected artifact still needs independent
model review. This consumes the same repair and review-round limits. A normally
settled truncated model review reconciles actual usage before requesting a new
compact verdict in fresh context, retaining the same source packet and counting
the next round. The output ceiling is at most 8192 and still respects the
approved output/model allowance. Unknown outcomes never enter that repair path.
Oversized packets or model-context overflow produce controlled input-limit
diagnostics, without silently dropping evidence. Reviewer calls also respect
the configured Provider timeout. A 60-second review claim can remain safely
reserved during a longer authorized call: expiry alone cannot release or refund
an admitted unknown remote attempt.

## Durable communication

`AgentMessage` projects persisted Core events into all ten requested protocol
types: assignment, accepted, completed, help, review, revision, dependency block,
model unavailable, budget warning and agent failure. Existing events/outbox/inbox
remain the transport, with Router coordination; no free-text group chat or
Worker-to-Worker mutation channel was introduced.

Workers emit accepted and routine progress facts. Dispatcher validates native
message identity against the durable Worker assignment. Malformed native
envelopes follow the existing bounded retry/dead-letter path. Legacy events
without native run/plan/node identity are explicitly labelled
`legacy_nonexecution`. Planner delivery also accepts `quest.proposal_updated`.

## Local verification

Commands below were run from `backend` with `.venv/Scripts/python.exe`:

- Worker/runtime/tool/receipt/fixed-verifier group: **95 passed in 30.82 s**.
- Phase 2 recovery/protocol plus M4 integration/adversarial group:
  **58 passed, one existing Starlette/httpx deprecation warning in 21.17 s**;
  XML: `worker-review-protocol-tests.xml`. This run caught a subsequent format
  check requirement, which was fixed. The XML records tests, not a static pass.
- Updated Phase 2 recovery/reviewer/Gateway guard plus ToolEngine group:
  **49 passed in 22.73 s**; XML: `worker-review-recovery-tests.xml`.
- Combined updated Worker, review lifecycle, Gateway guard, Dispatcher,
  ToolEngine, upstream receipt and fixed-verifier regression group:
  **128 passed in 46.34 s**; XML: `worker-review-final-tests.xml`.
- Settled truncation, bounded retries, unknown-timeout/unsettled-live rejection,
  Worker/tool integration and reviewer Gateway guards: **81 passed in 48.91 s**;
  XML: `worker-truncation-recovery-tests.xml`. An initial run had one small-budget
  archive-context regression; shortening the Worker prompt fixed it, and the
  six archive cases passed before this complete rerun. Truncation responses use
  HTTP MockTransport; the unsettled-live case is an explicitly labelled stub.
- Dispatcher, workspace backup/restore and migration regressions: **65 passed,
  one existing Starlette/httpx deprecation warning in 18.25 s**; XML:
  `dispatcher-backup-migration-tests.xml`. Dispatcher fixtures now drain their
  finite backlog with a 32-tick bound instead of assuming three 50 ms slices
  finish every delivery under load. The v7 snapshot fixture removes the Phase 2
  repair column and constraint tables before invoking the unchanged migration
  path; restored schema version is checked against `SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- Worker lease renewal, fixed exception labels, actual Gateway timeout,
  truncation and reviewer integration regressions: **90 passed in 32.30 s**;
  XML: `worker-lease-recovery-tests.xml`. The new cases cover a 110-second
  simulated multi-step task under successive 60-second leases, deadline caps,
  expired claims, competing owners, pause and changed-plan rejection. Real local
  file receipts remain present; MockTransport timeout preserves an unknown
  reservation. Ruff check/format passed for the three changed Python files.
- Owned artifact revision, parser feedback, bounded Reviewer truncation repair,
  Worker/ToolEngine and publish-evidence integration: **153 passed in 40.63 s**;
  XML: `worker-revision-final-tests.xml`. Dedicated revision/configuration cases
  include immutable version chains, rejected old contracts, user-file and stale
  hash protection, unknown replacement results, and grant/pause/content races.
  After adding the explicit raw-JSON/no-Markdown initial instruction, the six
  archive-budget cases plus the full bad-JSON/revision/review path passed again:
  **7 passed in 2.89 s**. Ruff check and format were rerun on all seven changed
  Python source/test files after the final prompt wording change and passed.
- Independent auditor's additional review lifecycle tests are retained in
  `test_phase2_integration_security.py`; they cover unsent capacity, settled and
  isolated restart recovery, unknown remote outcomes, and stale late responses.
- Four initial Gateway claim guard tests passed in 1.88 s; the later group adds
  cancellation/pause/stale-plan guard tests.
- Provider diagnostics persist only Core-controlled error codes; raw Provider
  exception messages are not written to failure/review events. Allowlisted
  `budget_exhausted` can distinguish admission failure from a sent timeout.

The tests use explicitly labelled scripted Mock models or HTTP MockTransport,
real SQLite transactions, real governed local reads/writes and real numeric
subprocesses. Synthetic ledger fixtures exercise failure ordering; they are not
live Provider results. Earlier failures were diagnosed in tool output rather
than relabelled as passes. Final combined-suite and source-integrity results
belong in the root verification record.

## Remaining limits

Review is same-model context independence and can share model biases. The fixed
execution toolset still does not implement arbitrary shell, unrestricted Python
or a general-purpose code patch tool. The explicit revision tool only replaces
the current Worker's own proven artifact; it does not edit arbitrary existing
user code or predecessor files. Contracts lacking that explicit tool still
require an approved fresh-path strategy or a reviewed plan/team change. Worker
code correction is bounded tool/contract repair;
this report does not claim unconstrained autonomous software development.

Unknown remote execution without a trusted isolation bound remains an explicit
manual/resource blocker. Recovery after arbitrary database corruption, unlimited
history, or unlimited team expansion is outside the verified scope. Real
multi-role task correctness and real model rework/restart acceptance require the
root live experiments; none is inferred from these offline results.

A final focused pass after the revision-commit/requeue recovery fix reported **28 passed in 13.95 s** (worker-review-restart-tests.xml). Ruff check and format were rerun on the changed review and test files.

## Complex live acceptance and unfinished work

L1 source analysis, L2 multi-Agent architecture comparison and L3 scheduler research,
implementation and experimentation have reproducible input descriptors in
`backend/scripts/phase2/acceptance_scenarios.py`. Descriptors contain actual bounded
repository inputs, source hashes and goals, with no seeded plan/team/approval/receipt
or hidden solution. Final L1/L2/L3 results, review rounds, tool evidence, artifact
hashes, compaction and restart observations remain pending integration-owner records.
The final machine-readable record is `docs/audit/phase2/verification.json`.

One retained L1 diagnostic, `20261114T235101Z-L1-3318e2`, ended after 146.716 seconds
with `composer_did_not_propose_team`: Composer hit the default 30-second Provider
timeout, and two unknown-outcome attempts remained reserved. This is a failed live
attempt. The subsequent fix exposes validated process settings
`FORGE_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 30, finite range greater than 0 through 600)
and `FORGE_PROVIDER_MAX_RETRIES` (default 1, integers 0–3), aligns the HTTP timeout
with the request, and sizes Planner/Composer leases for their bounded repair stage.
The live harness uses 120 seconds and zero additional retries. A later rerun remains
subject to its own recorded result; the failed attempt is preserved.

The requested full success condition requires a complex live task to retain its
goal across real failure, autonomous repair, independent revision, compaction and
Core restart with independently verified artifacts. Storage readback or restart at
the approved-plan boundary alone cannot establish that condition. Current component
connectivity, local tests and protocol success therefore do not justify declaring
Phase 2 complete.

Remaining material limits include general remaining-DAG replanning; exhaustive
coordination payload schemas; learned semantic recall; independent reviewer model
selection; sparse online capability evidence; same-budget live algorithm comparisons;
and safe arbitrary in-flight recovery. Default Review mode still requires authenticated
plan/team/replacement approval. Desktop packaging remains deferred.

| Requested capability | Current boundary and remaining gap |
| --- | --- |
| Semantic memory retrieval | Retrieval is lexical with limited bilingual aliases and source/Quest/time/type filters. No embedding or learned semantic retrieval is implemented. Fixed semantic artifact verification is a separate mechanism. |

These mechanisms do not establish general autonomous software development. |
| Artifact correction after review | `file_write` uses create-only semantics and never overwrites an existing file. A revision can change structured delivery or create an allowed fresh artifact when the original criteria accept that path; it cannot generally patch a previously written artifact in place. |
| Replanning during execution | Router goal updates and new DAG proposals accept only proposed/awaiting-approval Quests. Team replacement retains the current DAG and completed history. Automatic revision of the remaining running DAG is incomplete. |
| Uniform Worker delivery | Review criteria enforce eight fields, while legacy/default compatibility schemas require only `summary`. The eight-field requirement is not universal across all existing contracts. |
| Long autonomous task continuity | Archives, source checks and bounded recovery exist. Final complex live failure/rework/compaction/restart acceptance remains pending; arbitrary in-flight external-effect recovery is unproven. |

## Remaining limits

Review is same-model context independence and can share model biases. The fixed
execution toolset still does not implement arbitrary shell, unrestricted Python
or a general-purpose code patch tool. The explicit revision tool only replaces
the current Worker's own proven artifact; it does not edit arbitrary existing
user code or predecessor files. Contracts lacking that explicit tool still
require an approved fresh-path strategy or a reviewed plan/team change. Worker
code correction is bounded tool/contract repair;
this report does not claim unconstrained autonomous software development.

Unknown remote execution without a trusted isolation bound remains an explicit
manual/resource blocker. Recovery after arbitrary database corruption, unlimited
history, or unlimited team expansion is outside the verified scope. Real
multi-role task correctness and real model rework/restart acceptance require the
root live experiments; none is inferred from these offline results.

# Phase 2 — Actual Agent Execution Chain Audit

Date: 2026-11-15 (Asia/Shanghai). Branch: `codex/phase1-continuous`.
This is a source/retained-evidence audit of the evolving Phase 2 working tree, not a
frozen acceptance result. Root is the unique integration owner. Phase 1 M1–M7 reports,
the M7 backend-hardening report, required architecture/protocol documents, and the
named Router/Worker/team/graph/dispatcher/context/memory/provider/tool/evidence/
governance modules were read. Earlier audits under `_audit/` describe the pre-change
state; conclusions below include the current Phase 2 changes.

## Executable chain

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    U[One main user conversation] --> R[Persistent Router: observe, recall, strict decision]
    R -->|chat| A[One user-facing response]
    R -->|create Quest and durable quest.proposed| D[Dispatcher: outbox, leases, inbox, dedup]
    D --> P[Separate Planner: original request, constraints, strict bounded DAG]
    P --> PA[Pending plan: digest, revision, criteria, dependencies]
    PA -->|authenticated local user approves| C[Composer: model profiles, online observations, hard budgets]
    C --> TA[Pending team: roles and models decoupled]
    TA -->|authenticated local user approves| S[WorkerScheduler: ready nodes and concurrency]
    S --> W[Native Worker: private context, model/tool loop, checkpoints]
    W --> T[ToolEngine: policy, grants, exact approvals, intent and receipt]
    T --> W
    W -->|structured worker.result| V[Fresh independent review context]
    V -->|NEEDS_REVISION with concrete goals| RW[Bounded revision of same approved assignment]
    RW --> W
    V -->|PASS| N[NodeVerifier: current provenance and fixed criteria checks]
    N --> G[CompletionGate: recheck approved plan, receipts and evidence]
    G --> Q[Verified task and Quest transitions]
    Q --> D
    D --> RN[Router notice: silent or user progress/result update]
    RN --> A
    W -->|help or blocker event| D
    D -->|help: pending approved replacement proposal| C
    X[ProviderGateway and durable admission ledger] -. all model calls .-> R
    X -.-> P
    X -.-> C
    X -.-> W
    X -.-> V
    M[Task capsules, constraints, source archives and memory] -. bounded context .-> R
    M -. original source recovery .-> W
```

`forge_api.main._core_lifespan` starts six background loops: Dispatcher, Router notices,
Planner, Composer, WorkerScheduler, and review/verification. Provider latency runs
outside SQLite write transactions. A proposal is not an approved plan, an approved
team, a running Worker or a completed task.

1. `RouterService.handle_user_message` synchronizes memory, observes a bounded snapshot,
   calls the configured Gateway, validates `RouterDecision`, and permits one bounded
   schema-repair request. The final user/assistant messages, Quest, source constraints,
   events and idempotent turn record commit atomically. Chat creates no Quest/Worker.
2. `process_pending_plan` consumes the durable creation event. `QuestGraphService.generate`
   receives the original user-message ID/content with its hash, sourced constraints,
   offered tool catalogue and capability names. Generated plans are limited to eight
   nodes/sixteen edges; invalid names/graphs receive one repair opportunity. `propose`
   persists the DAG; `approve` binds authenticated actor, revision, digest and version.
3. `process_pending_team` proposes bounded role contracts. `TeamComposerEngine.compose`
   filters tool/context/cost/budget incompatibilities and offers single-model, greedy,
   coverage and complementarity search. `performance_snapshot` supplies separate,
   source-digested live/Mock observations with sample counts and Wilson intervals for
   rates; it does not rewrite manually supplied capability scores or infer task success
   from transport success. Team approval binds the plan and selected profile hashes.
4. `WorkerScheduler.tick` launches only approved, ready assignments. `WorkerManager.start`
   checks dependencies, effective tool scope, model identity and token/tool/time/agent/
   depth/concurrency limits. `_run` owns a native checkpointed model/tool loop. `_repair`
   preserves failed diagnostics and bounded repair history; provider, contract, budget,
   dependency, authorization, code and tool failures have distinct classifications.
5. `ToolEngine.prepare/execute` enforces current permissions before action, persists an
   exact intent and records its receipt. R1 writes require a Workspace grant; R2 requires
   exact action approval and operator allowlists; unknown/R3 actions fail closed.
   Uncertain external effects are not silently repeated after restart or reassignment.
6. `IndependentReviewService` constructs a fresh packet from the original contract,
   criteria, structured delivery, actual bounded artifacts and trustworthy receipts.
   It does not copy the Worker's private conversation. It currently uses the same
   approved underlying model in a separate context: independent context is not model
   diversity. PASS/NEEDS_REVISION/REJECT/BLOCKED are schema-checked; revision requires
   concrete goals and has a default two-round limit. Budget and source bindings persist.
7. `NodeVerifier` requires the applicable fresh PASS, then performs fixed JSON or numeric
   semantic verification. `CompletionGate` revalidates approved historical/current
   bindings, original execution mode, actual tool results and artifact hashes before
   completion. Model self-report or Mock evidence alone cannot establish live completion.
8. `Dispatcher` delivers typed event facts at least once with Inbox deduplication and
   fencing. `AgentMessage.from_event` projects task identity and structured coordination
   kinds. Workers cannot directly edit another Worker's task. Only Router appends the
   selected user-facing update to `main`.

## Evidence classification

| Capability | Current implementation | Verification category and limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Persistent single Router/conversation, SQLite UoW/CAS, migrations | Real code and durable records | Local restart/transaction tests; Phase 1 M1–M7 retained evidence |
| Strict Router/Planner decisions and bounded repair | Real Gateway-backed production paths | Current B/F 53-test focused suite; reasoning/orchestration assertions are Mock |
| Planner from original request and source constraints | Separate production component | Mock strict-wire, integrity, catalogue and node-limit regressions |
| Dynamic role/model selection and approved replacement | Real bounded composer/scheduler | Offline/synthetic comparisons and Mock integration; no general live superiority claim |
| Model online statistics | Actual bounded Core observations | Provenance/sample counts retained; sparse priors are not measured abilities |
| Native Worker tools/checkpoints | Real runtime and governed local tools | Phase 1 M5 live numeric/JSON demonstrations; current new recovery branches tested locally/Mock |
| Independent fresh-context review and revision | Real production service and evidence binding | New Mock/adversarial coverage; current complex live review/rework E2E still unverified here |
| Task capsules, constraints, source readback | Real hash-checked archives and index | 39 context/memory tests; M6 retained narrow live continuation; no infinite-capacity claim |
| Recall | Keyword/source/Quest/time/type filters and bilingual aliases | 9/9 exploratory synthetic source-ID/hash cases; learned semantic/embedding recall absent |
| Agent communication | Durable existing event bus with typed projection | Core identity checks and bounded event flow; exhaustive per-type payload contracts remain partial |
| Full autonomous remaining-DAG replanning | Existing proposal/control/replacement interfaces | General automatic safe replanning and hierarchical expansion remain incomplete |
| Independent Reviewer model selection | Same approved model with fresh context | Separate Reviewer model diversity remains an extension, not implemented evidence |
| Complex multi-domain autonomous completion after failure/rework/restart | Components now connected | Must be judged by retained L1/L2/L3 live runs; unverified at this audit snapshot |

The old narrow output-schema compatibility contract still permits summary-only results;
`delivery_review` explicitly requires all eight delivery fields. Do not state that every
legacy Worker contract enforces all eight fields. Default autonomy remains Review:
model-generated plans, teams and replacements remain pending until authenticated approval.

## Actual live Provider evidence

The new retained probe is
`.local/phase2/provider/20261114T233125Z-d07064/report.json`: **11/11 small protocol cases**,
26.712 seconds, `wb-local`, self-reported `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, Gateway through loopback
`127.0.0.1:8788/v1`. It covers minimal dialogue, three Router-schema responses, three tool
call responses, bounded context recall, two concurrent calls and streaming. Discovery
returned eleven IDs and included the requested model. The 300,000-token admission ceiling
and concurrency two were finite configuration, not consumed tokens or service maxima.

These records distinguish proxy response, returned model response and case correctness.
Upstream identity remains **unverified_proxy_reported_identity**. Actual maximum context,
output, rate limits and cost remain unknown; the 65,536 context and 1,024 probe-output
ceilings are operator bounds. Protocol success is not an autonomous task-completion result.
Phase 1 M5 additionally retains a real numeric tool run and one JSON-syntax completion;
M6 retains one narrow continuation success after five preserved diagnostic failures.

## Continuity and open boundaries

`ConstraintService` separates literal user clauses, pending model extracts and separately
confirmed records, with original IDs/hashes, potential conflicts, expiry and revocation.
Router/Worker highlights are bounded; omitted originals remain in archives and can be
re-read with source checks. L0 recent interaction, L1 Quest, L2 project/history and L3
failure-experience paths exist. Active Quest counts, indexing batches, candidate pages,
artifact/receipt snapshots and model windows remain finite; learned semantic retrieval,
general source relevance and arbitrary-scale continuity are not established.

Recovery uses durable Worker/model/tool state and lease generations. Unknown remote
outcomes retain reservations until trusted recovery conditions permit action. The current
live driver tests storage compaction/readback and restart at the approved-plan boundary;
that alone would not prove safe recovery from an arbitrary in-flight external action.
The independent driver's five offline tests verify missing DB handling, actual budget
inspection, genuine archive/readback, no-op truthfulness and visible integrity failure.
Desktop packaging/UI acceptance is deferred; no new desktop-release claim follows.

The fixed tool contracts do not provide arbitrary shell, unrestricted Python,
arbitrary test commands or a general patch operation. `python_compile` proves
syntax only, `numeric_ast` executes a bounded pure numeric subset and
`shell_inspect` permits only `python_version`. `file_write` creates files with
exclusive-create semantics. A review revision cannot generally edit an existing
artifact in place. Team replacement keeps the approved DAG; Router goal updates
and new DAG proposals remain limited to proposed/awaiting-approval Quests, so
general running-DAG replanning is still absent. Source retrieval remains lexical.
# Sprint F — Source-linked Constraints and Bounded Context

Date: 2026-11-15 (Asia/Shanghai). Integration owner: root agent. Scope: backend context,
memory, source-linked user constraints and offline retrieval evaluation. No Provider or
credential files were read by this subtask; no live model call was made.

## Audit result and changes

The M6 archive stored every distinct user message verbatim in the next capsule. It
preserved originals but increased every subsequent model input indefinitely. The early
Phase 2 Router stored extracted constraints in `memories` as hypotheses; a key derived
from the full statement did not associate different budget statements for conflict
detection, and those rows lacked source-content hashes or confirmation provenance.

The existing SQLite archive, source-integrity checks, transaction boundaries, Gateway,
and Worker tool-pair protection are retained. The Phase 2 v10 migration also installs
`constraint_records`, `constraint_message_index` and an incremental source cursor.

- `ConstraintService.index_message` associates the current original user message with
  the Router-selected Quest. Reindexing is idempotent; changed source content and an
  attempted conflicting reassignment fail closed. Message metadata supplied by a caller
  does not establish Quest association.
- A bounded literal extractor copies at most eight short clauses per user message.
  Its origin is `explicit_user`; model-derived paraphrases remain `pending_model`.
  A separate confirmation operation requires another user message containing both a
  confirmation expression and the exact clause. Confirmations have their own source ID
  and hash. These labels describe instruction provenance, not domain facts or approval.
- Records retain original message IDs, SHA-256, Quest association, dimension, origin,
  optional timezone-aware expiry and revocation state. Budget/deadline/language/retention/
  scope/model dimensions allow **potential** conflicts to remain visible. A changed,
  missing, expired or revoked source is excluded. Conflicting statements are not resolved
  by silently choosing the newest one.
- Router archives retain at most 64 user highlights within 12,288 encoded bytes and 16
  other highlights within 4,096 bytes. Individual user highlights are bounded UTF-8
  excerpts. Initial anchors and recent items are favored; omissions and source-recall
  entry points are recorded. Duplicate messages have at most four source references in
  a highlight. Originals remain in `messages` and source archives.
- Worker archives bound claims and completed-tool highlights, retain the initial task
  contract and live tool-call/result pair, and trim archived highlights to the actual
  input budget before committing. Trusted receipts and original worker messages remain
  in their durable stores. Bounded sourced constraints are included in Worker context;
  archived Router rebuilds refresh constraint records from the current source store.
- Per-Quest evidence and receipt snapshots are capped at 64 entries each and explicitly
  indicate omissions. The independent evidence gate continues to use authoritative
  execution records; a context snapshot is not completion authority.
- Memory indexing processes at most 128 source messages per batch. It stores source
  hashes, terms and bounded clauses rather than another copy of the full corpus.
  Archived original messages are therefore retrievable after their highlights leave
  the capsule. L0 labels current interactions; archived sources use L1 for an associated
  Quest or L2 for unassociated history. Existing Quest, project and failure indexing
  retains the L1/L2/L3 paths.
- Recall supports bounded keyword/source/Quest lookup, a small bilingual alias expansion,
  timezone-aware time filters and source-type filters. The alias dictionary helps with
  cases such as `spending` → `预算`, but this is **lexical retrieval**, not embedding or
  learned semantic retrieval.

## Verification

Commands run from `backend`, using its existing virtual environment:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/test_constraints_phase2.py tests/test_context_m6.py tests/test_memory_m6.py -q --junitxml=../docs/audit/phase2/sprint-f-tests.xml
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/phase2/retrieval_evaluation.py --output ../docs/audit/phase2/retrieval-evaluation-v2.json
```

The focused source/context/memory run passed **39 tests in 15.42 seconds** (8 new tests
plus the 31 existing M6 context/memory tests). These are offline deterministic/Mock
tests. They cover pending versus confirmed provenance, exact original-source IDs,
confirmation tampering, conflict visibility, expiry, revocation, Quest isolation,
transaction rollback, duplicate-reference bounds, UTF-8 budgets, and recall/readback of
an omitted message after three compactions and a storage reopen. The raw history in
that continuity test contains 240 messages; every original remains available.

Ruff check and format checks passed for this subtask's seven Python files. The root
agent runs the complete integration checks and records their frozen-source results.

The fixed `phase2-retrieval-v1` evaluation passed **9/9 exploratory synthetic cases**.
Dataset SHA-256:
`6d4dd52492b4bb9e55db3dcbff5f5bd49ddfa260665504356097eeede92a533b`.
The evaluator checks expected source identities and independently recomputed source
hashes after reopening storage. It covers bilingual budget/retention/deadline queries,
language, a file-path reference, a recorded decision, historical Quest identity,
Quest-associated constraints, and a time-exclusion query. The v1 diagnostic output is
preserved; v2 additionally records and validates actual source hashes. Neither output
contains model calls, external tool execution, model quality measurements or live
domain-task success evidence.

`tests/test_router_intelligence_phase2.py` adds separate Mock Router/Planner regressions
for bounded repair, atomic failure, constraint provenance, original-request integrity,
planning contract names, node limits and single-Router recovery. Their final integrated
focused run passed **14/14 in 1.68 seconds**. An initial run identified a missing
autonomous-Planner capability-name check; root integrated the fix and also checks generated
tools against the actual offered catalogue. Known-but-unavailable R2 tools, repeated invalid
plans, missing original requests and overlarge autonomous DAGs are covered.

The final combined B/F focused run passed **53 tests in 18.36 seconds**:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/test_constraints_phase2.py tests/test_context_m6.py tests/test_memory_m6.py tests/test_router_intelligence_phase2.py -q --junitxml=../docs/audit/phase2/sprint-bf-integrated-tests.xml
```

The complete backend suite remains root's integration responsibility. None of these
53 tests is a live-provider validation.

## Limits

The literal extractor is deliberately small and cannot establish the semantics of every
quoted, conditional or implied user instruction. Pending model extracts require source
review; a literal user clause is not automatically an authenticated action approval.
Potential-conflict dimensions may require user clarification. Confirmation/revocation
are Core service operations; this subtask does not add a public user interface for them.

The fixed retrieval corpus is small and exploratory. It does not measure unconstrained
semantic retrieval, learned relevance, Router task understanding, or model correctness.
Candidate pages, active-Quest snapshots and per-call indexing remain bounded. Long
histories can require multiple indexing batches or source reads; arbitrary-scale memory
and unbounded storage are not claimed. Omitted context never implies that the underlying
record, requirement, receipt or artifact does not exist.
# ADR 009: Source-bound planning, independent review and durable coordination

Status: Phase 2 implementation in progress; local and live acceptance are recorded separately.
Date: 2026-11-15.

## Context

ADRs [007](ADR-007-native-worker-and-execution-evidence.md) and
[008](ADR-008-context-recall-budget.md) establish approved native execution, trusted
receipts, bounded context and Gateway admission. Phase 2 needs stronger planning,
revision and collaboration without replacing those controls or adding user chats.

## Decision

1. Keep the persistent Router as the only user-facing Agent. A separate Planner
   consumes the original request, source hashes, constraints and offered tools to
   propose a bounded DAG. A proposal never grants execution authority; plan and
   team approval continue to require the authenticated local user.
2. Store literal user clauses, pending model extractions and separately confirmed
   clauses with distinct provenance. Bound context highlights and retain original
   source readback paths. Conflicts, omissions, expiry and revocation remain visible;
   extracted instructions never substitute for action approval.
3. Review a delivery in a fresh context containing the original contract, criteria,
   bounded actual artifacts and verified receipts. Do not copy the Worker's private
   conversation. Bind the verdict to its input hash and admitted model attempt.
   `NEEDS_REVISION` requires concrete goals and consumes the existing bounded budget.
   A fresh PASS is necessary for review criteria but remains subject to NodeVerifier
   and CompletionGate checks. The current reviewer uses the approved Worker's model;
   separate context does not establish independent model identity.
4. Project typed Agent messages from the existing durable event/outbox transport.
   Preserve task identity, lease fencing, Inbox deduplication and Router-mediated
   control. Agent messages confer no right to mutate another Worker's assignment.
5. Reuse observed model performance as a sourced, sample-counted input to new team
   proposals. Preserve explicit user scores, approved profile hashes, completed
   nodes and historical contracts. Replacement never resets cumulative budgets.

## Consequences and limits

The implementation adds focused services and schema changes rather than a parallel
runtime. Default Review autonomy, policy, exact approvals, receipts and Gateway
reservations remain authoritative. Unknown remote effects stay unresolved until
trusted recovery conditions permit settlement; a client timeout permits no replay.

Schema repair, review rounds, Agent counts, context packets and replanning are
bounded. General automatic remaining-DAG replanning, arbitrary hierarchical Agent
expansion, exhaustive per-message payload schemas and learned semantic retrieval
remain incomplete. The legacy summary-only delivery contract stays compatible;
`delivery_review` explicitly requires all eight delivery fields. Local/Mock tests
and synthetic benchmarks do not establish complex live-task acceptance. See the
[Phase 2 report](../PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md) for the current evidence.

The current execution boundary remains the fixed Core toolset: bounded numeric
AST, syntax checks and diagnostics, with create-only file writes. General program
execution, arbitrary test runners, artifact patching and running-DAG revision are
not supplied by introducing fresh review or typed coordination.

# Phase 2 — Experiments and Reproduction

Updated: 2026-11-15 (Asia/Shanghai). Real Provider protocols, local/Mock execution,
synthetic algorithm measurements and pending acceptance are reported separately.
Failures and earlier diagnostics remain preserved; a later success does not erase them.

## Recorded runs

| Record | Mode | Result | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `20261114T233125Z-d07064` | Live protocol | 11/11 cases, 26.712 seconds | Gateway → local proxy → self-reported model; no complex task result |
| `20261114T235101Z-L1-3318e2` | Live L1 diagnostic | Failed, 146.716 seconds, `composer_did_not_propose_team` | Provider timeout; two unknown attempts retain reservations; no completed artifact claim |
| `benchmark_c51c77ee97c8` / [offline v2](audit/phase2/benchmarks/offline-intelligence-v2.json) | Offline synthetic plus actual local tools | Complete, 9.48 seconds, zero Provider calls | Six fixed team/context scenarios, governance matrix, source retrieval |
| [Retrieval v2](audit/phase2/retrieval-evaluation-v2.json) | Synthetic, persisted/reopened Core | 9/9 source-ID/hash cases, 1.369 seconds | Source identity and provenance; no domain correctness measurement |
| L1/L2/L3 live acceptance | Live E2E required | Pending integration-owner results | Must include original requests, native tools, review, artifacts, failure/rework/continuity evidence |

The protocol record is stored at
`.local/phase2/provider/20261114T233125Z-d07064/report.json`. Provider: `wb-local`;
requested model: `deepseek-v4.1-flash`; route: local workbuddy-api/wb-in via
`http://127.0.0.1:8788/v1`. Upstream identity remains
`unverified_proxy_reported_identity`. Eleven discovered IDs included the target.
Token admission ceiling 300,000, concurrency two, context operator ceiling 65,536
and output probe ceiling 1,024 are configured bounds, not service maxima or usage.
Actual maximum context/output, rate limit and cost are unknown.

The protocol ledger contains 11 settled attempts reporting 5,444 input and 637 output
tokens. These are usage measurements separate from the reservation ceiling. The L1
diagnostic retains its original `run.json` under `.local/phase2/runs/`; failed runs
remain part of the denominator when final live results are summarized.

The 11 cases cover minimal dialogue, three Router-schema responses, three tool-call
responses, bounded-context recall, two simultaneous requests and streaming. A
returned tool-call structure is protocol evidence; it is not by itself evidence that
the requested tool action executed. Proxy response, returned model response and
the explicit case check remain separate observations.

## Fixed offline benchmark

Dataset SHA-256: `99cdfeeae6df2635f03c768ec7290230452e31e15ae65bee74d885aaf1ef8cec`.
The data are fixed, deterministic and exploratory. A separate hard-constraint scorer
checks proposals; no model call contributes an answer. Earlier
[v1](audit/phase2/benchmarks/offline-intelligence-v1.json) is retained as a diagnostic.

### Capability-aware team composition

Six difficulty/domain scenarios compare eight variants under the same synthetic
model profiles, capability targets and resource limits. All 48 proposals passed
the independent contract checks. These metrics describe selected model identities,
not task quality, real token usage or cost.

| Variant | Scenarios | Contract pass rate | Specialist-target fraction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Single model | 6 | 1.00 | 0.125 |
| Static team | 6 | 1.00 | 0.00 |
| Greedy selection | 6 | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| Capability coverage | 6 | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| Complementarity | 6 | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| Dynamic recomposition | 6 | 1.00 | 0.75 |
| No coordination penalty | 6 | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| No confidence weighting | 6 | 1.00 | 1.00 |

No-confidence and no-coordination did not change this proxy on these cases; these
results do not establish their benefit. Completed-node/history preservation is
covered by separate service regression tests. Real selection quality, latency,
coordination burden and adaptive task success require live comparison.

### Task-centric context compression

Six scenarios each contain two original obligations. Every variant receives a
6,144 serialized UTF-8 byte input ceiling. Actual ContextService archives are
created, the database is reopened, and source IDs/hashes are independently checked.

| Variant | Admitted cases | Obligations retained | Obligations with checked sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Full context | 0/6 | 0/12 admitted | 0/12 admitted |
| Recency truncation | 6/6 | 0/12 | 0/12 |
| Conventional summary | 6/6 | 6/12 | 0/12 |
| Task-centric | 6/6 | 6/12 | 6/12 |
| Task-centric + source recall | 6/6 | 12/12 | 12/12 |

Full context exceeds the shared input ceiling and is refused; the original text
still contains its obligations. Conventional summary is a fixed extractive baseline,
not a generated model summary. Byte admission is not actual provider token savings.
This result measures retained source obligations, not downstream model compliance.

### Evidence-driven governance

The 15-case matrix uses the actual ToolEngine and local file tools with a clearly
labelled Mock Worker fixture. Three execution requests produced two unique receipts,
including receipt replay. Eleven expected denials and four expected allows matched;
false-allow rate 0/11 and false-deny rate 0/4. Cases cover missing/revoked grants,
parameter substitution, protected/outside paths, exact R2 approvals and a forged
receipt rejected by NodeVerifier/CompletionGate. R2 cases stop at intent preparation;
no external requests execute.

The model-claim-only counterfactual permits 11/11 expected denials; removing binding
permits 4/11; removing revocation rechecks permits 2/11. These ablations simulate
omitted checks and never authorize an action. Actual receipt verification and fixed
independent verifier/evidence gate paths are exercised. Independent LLM Reviewer
quality and a four-way same-budget live governance comparison remain unmeasured.

### Source retrieval

Dataset: `phase2-retrieval-v1`;
SHA-256: `6d4dd52492b4bb9e55db3dcbff5f5bd49ddfa260665504356097eeede92a533b`.
Nine fixed cases check bilingual budget/retention/deadline terms, language, file path,
decision, Quest identity, Quest-associated constraint and time exclusion. All expected
source identities and independently recomputed original-row hashes match after
storage reopen. Limited bilingual aliases extend lexical retrieval; learned semantic
or embedding recall, held-out generalization and task truth are not measured.

## Local regression records

| Test group | Result | Record |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Router/Planner/constraints/context/memory | 53 passed, 18.36 seconds | [Combined JUnit](audit/phase2/sprint-bf-integrated-tests.xml) |
| Live driver offline checks | 5 passed, 0.57 seconds | [Driver JUnit](audit/phase2/driver-tests.xml) |
| Team/registry/recomposition/benchmark provenance | 42 passed, 14.61 seconds | [Sprint C/I](audit/phase2/sprint-ci.md) |
| Worker/review/Gateway/Dispatcher/tools/receipts/fixed verifiers | 128 passed, 46.34 seconds | [D/E/G report](audit/phase2/sprint-deg.md), [JUnit](audit/phase2/worker-review-final-tests.xml) |
| Provider configuration/timeout and Router/Planner source binding | 42 passed, 4.56 seconds | [Focused report](audit/phase2/provider-source-regressions.md), [JUnit](audit/phase2/provider-source-tests.xml) |
| Cumulative allowance and existing team contracts | 40 passed, 3.61 seconds | [Report](audit/phase2/cumulative-budget-and-quest-identity.md), [JUnit](audit/phase2/cumulative-budget-tests.xml) |
| Quest identity, context/memory, Router/Planner and offline probe | 67 passed, 32.53 seconds | [Report](audit/phase2/cumulative-budget-and-quest-identity.md), [JUnit](audit/phase2/quest-identity-probe-tests.xml) |
| Frozen full backend suite | Pending integration owner | Final `docs/audit/phase2/verification.json` |

Groups overlap; their counts do not form an aggregate full-suite total. Tests using
Mock providers are never counted as live task executions. Historical Phase 1 test
counts and demonstrations remain in their original reports.

## Reproduction and live acceptance contract

From `backend`, using the existing virtual environment, write to a new output path:

environment variable is introduced by the offline benchmark. Live scripts require a
protected process credential reference and finite budget; credentials must not appear
in arguments, output records or source. `verify_provider.py` accepts `--credential-env`;
`live_e2e.py` reads the process-only `FORGE_PROVIDER_KEY_LIVE_TEST` variable. Supply its
value through a protected process input method. Do not place a value in shell history.

Process-only `FORGE_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` defaults to 30 seconds and accepts a
finite value greater than 0 through 600. `FORGE_PROVIDER_MAX_RETRIES` defaults to 1
and accepts integers 0–3. The current live harness selects 120 seconds and zero
additional retries after the retained Composer timeout diagnostic. Every actual
attempt still requires Gateway admission; an unknown remote result stays reserved.

experiments; it supplies no unrestricted Python/test runner, arbitrary shell or

execution mechanism used, and cannot be generalized to arbitrary repository repair.

artifact hashes, final status and failure diagnostics. Price stays unknown when no
trusted price is configured. Report success denominator, evidence completeness,
compaction source readback and observed restart boundary explicitly. L1/L2/L3 final
metrics remain pending; run directories and proposed tasks are not acceptance evidence.

`ConstraintService` separates literal user clauses, pending model extracts and separately
confirmed records, with original IDs/hashes, potential conflicts, expiry and revocation.
