# Quality Gates and Known Limitations

Updated: 2026-11-15. Phase 2 Agent Intelligence is in progress; desktop acceptance is deferred.

## Current evidence

- Phase 2 local/Mock focused records: B/F 53 passed in 18.36 seconds, driver 5 passed in 0.57 seconds, C/I 42 passed in 14.61 seconds, D/E/G 128 passed in 46.34 seconds, Provider/source binding 42 passed in 4.56 seconds. Groups overlap and are not a full-suite count. Final frozen-source integration remains pending.
- Later focused local/Mock records: own-artifact revision and Reviewer repair 153 passed in 40.63 seconds, Worker lease recovery 90 passed in 32.30 seconds, committed revision/requeue restart recovery 28 passed in 13.95 seconds. [D/E/G evidence](audit/phase2/sprint-deg.md) retains earlier results; these overlapping groups are not live quality measurements.
- Fixed numeric-suite revision group: 119 passed in 44.14 seconds, including 21 new cases, with actual local numeric subprocesses and scripted model fixtures; no Provider call. [C/I evidence](audit/phase2/sprint-ci.md) records the fail-closed authorization, budget, unresolved-outcome and callback checks.
- Later [semantic revision recovery group](audit/phase2/semantic-recovery-20261115T090801.xml): 74 passed in 34.65 seconds; the semantic test file now contains 30 cases. Persisted feedback before callback recovers idempotently after reopen without model review, while current source/authority/budget and unresolved-outcome guards remain enforced. This is local/Mock evidence.
- [Lossless review-input / round-limit group](audit/phase2/review-context-20261115T091955.xml): 118 passed in 36.18 seconds, including 15 new cases. Complete sources and exact constraint spans reconstruct the unchanged original packet/PASS binding. The retained L2 fixture's native Gateway payload reserves 64,245 under the unchanged 65,536 ceiling; local construction made no network call and proves no larger-packet capacity or live acceptance.
- Real Gateway protocol probes through local workbuddy-api/wb-in, requested `deepseek-v4.1-flash`: the proxy-default run passed 11/11 small cases in 26.712 seconds; the [explicit `reasoning_effort=none` probe](audit/phase2/provider-probe-reasoning-none.json) passed 10/11 in 20.210 seconds, retaining the failed exact-text minimal dialogue check. The request parameter does not prove internal upstream reasoning behavior. Upstream identity remains proxy-reported and unverified; actual service capacity and price are unknown. Protocol checks do not establish task completion.
- Offline v2: six fixed domains/difficulties, 48 team proposals satisfying hard constraints, 12/12 obligations recovered by compaction plus source recall, governance 0/11 false allows and 0/4 false denials, retrieval 9/9 source-ID/hash checks. These are exploratory synthetic/local mechanism measurements with zero Provider calls.
- Historical M6 verification passed 372 tests; one bounded live continuation succeeded after five retained failures. M7 backend hardening passed 488 tests. Their reports retain exact scope; they are not current Phase 2 full-suite or packaged-desktop acceptance.

Detailed evidence and reproducible commands are in the [Phase 2 report](PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md),
[experiments](PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md) and [execution-chain audit](audit/phase2/execution-chain-audit.md).
The final integration owner records the frozen result in `docs/audit/phase2/verification.json`.

## Required Phase 2 acceptance

1. Preserve one persistent user-facing Router/conversation and private native Workers.
2. Require valid original-request/constraint sources, bounded schemas and explicit authenticated plan/team/replacement approval. Default Review remains enabled.
3. Admit every model attempt through the durable Gateway token/concurrency ledger; retain unknown usage/effects and never infer remote cancellation from a timeout.
4. Enforce tool policy, current grants, exact approvals, durable intents, receipts and execution-mode provenance. Mock records cannot prove live completion.
5. Bind fresh review verdicts to original criteria, actual artifacts/receipts and the latest delivery. `NEEDS_REVISION` must contain actionable goals and stay within cumulative budgets and round limits.
6. Recheck approval history/current bindings, artifact hashes, tool results and applicable fixed semantic verifiers at completion. A model PASS or JSON syntax alone does not establish domain correctness.
7. Record L1/L2/L3 live metrics and independently inspect artifacts. Demonstrate observed failure/repair, review revision, actual archive/readback and Core restart boundaries rather than inferring them from records or directory names.
8. Run checks against the final source snapshot and preserve failed attempts and historical evidence. A complex live task must satisfy the intended continuity condition before Phase 2 is declared complete.
9. Permit artifact replacement only with explicitly approved `file_revise`, the same current Worker's latest successful receipt chain, unchanged file hash and current workspace grant. Recheck the chain and latest bytes at review/completion; retain immutable prior versions. Existing create-only contracts gain no permission.
10. Keep parser/fixed-suite revision feedback distinguishable from LLM review or PASS. Bind semantic failure to the actual suite/report/source/receipt and latest delivery, require explicit revision authority and remaining original budgets with no unresolved actions/calls, and rerun the real suite after repair. Charge settled truncated reviews before bounded retry; never reset cumulative budgets or replay unknown remote outcomes. Lease renewal must retain fencing, current authority and the original task deadline.

## Known limits

- Router/Planner repair is bounded once; autonomous plans cap at eight nodes/sixteen edges. General remaining-DAG replanning and arbitrary hierarchical Agent expansion are incomplete.
- Goal updates/new DAG proposals accept only proposed/awaiting-approval Quests. Team replacement preserves the current DAG; it does not implement autonomous replanning of a running DAG.
- Cumulative Worker/review token allowance is distinct from the per-request context/output bound; both remain enforced, along with approved node/team limits. Bounded Quest identity recall is separate from ordinary fact/constraint recall; true identity omissions/cursors and multiple candidates still require clarification.
- Dynamic team changes retain completed nodes and require approval. Performance snapshots are bounded, sourced and sample-counted; the current five-observation eligibility threshold does not establish statistical sufficiency or automatically learned general capability.
- Independent review uses the same approved underlying model in a fresh context. Independent model diversity is not implemented. `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` defaults to two and accepts integers one through four; the live harness selects three within its scenario's three-round cap, without changing historical runs. Output is capped by 8192, role output and model output limits. Labelled Core JSON-parser revision feedback supplies no LLM review or PASS. Legacy/default delivery compatibility requires only `summary`, while `delivery_review` requires all eight fields.
- A lossless review envelope can remove duplicate escaping/schema/constraint metadata while preserving full source text, exact source spans and the original packet/PASS hash. It changes representation, not context or evidence limits. Oversized packets, model-context overflow and exhausted budgets still block. Published runtime settings use an explicit whitelist; missing legacy values remain null.
- Router/Worker archives have bounded highlights, preserve original-source recovery and signal omissions. Active-Quest snapshots, indexing batches, evidence/receipt pages and model windows remain finite. Long histories can require multiple reads or fail closed.
- Constraint literal extraction and potential-conflict dimensions are bounded heuristics. User/model provenance does not prove domain facts or grant action approval. Confirmation/revocation have Core operations but no new public interface in this sprint.
- Recall uses bounded lexical terms, bilingual aliases and source/Quest/time/type filters. Learned semantic retrieval, general relevance and arbitrary-scale memory are not established.
- Worker execution tools are fixed: `python_compile` checks syntax, `numeric_ast` runs a bounded pure numeric subset and `shell_inspect` permits `python_version`. Arbitrary shell, unrestricted Python, arbitrary test runners and a general code patch tool are absent.
- `file_write` remains exclusive-create. Explicitly approved `file_revise` only replaces the current Worker's own latest produced artifact with receipt-chain/hash checks and immutable version history; user files, predecessor artifacts, stale versions and uncertain outcomes are excluded. General repository patch/test loops remain incomplete, and all revision must preserve the original approved criteria.
- Worker leases renew only between settled steps for a valid current owner, bounded by the task deadline. Expired/stale claims, changed plans, competing owners and paused/cancelled assignments cannot be revived; calls remain capped by the current lease/deadline and unknown outcomes retain reservations.
- Fixed semantic-suite feedback is deterministic Core validation, not independent LLM review. Persisted feedback before callback can recover once after restart, including semantic-only nodes, only after current result/semantic/source/receipt, scope/grant and original-budget checks with no unsettled actions or model attempts. It issues no model-review request; stale sources, revoked authority, exhausted budgets, unknown actions and callback errors remain blocked. This does not establish arbitrary in-flight recovery.
- ACP is a typed projection of durable events with task identities and fenced ownership; exhaustive payload contracts remain partial. Unknown external effects and unresolved model attempts may conservatively block progress until trusted settlement is possible.
- Team/context/governance benchmarks use small deterministic cases, synthetic profiles, fixed extractive summaries and byte budgets. Same-budget real task quality, measured token/cost savings, independent LLM governance quality and statistical generalization remain open.
- SQLite migration/restart tests do not establish production durability under every failure mode. Packaged Windows Alpha, full native lifecycle, credential vault and backup/restore integration remain outside this sprint's completed evidence.

## Historical verification

Phase 1 reports retain their original results and limitations. In particular, the
[M3 report](PHASE1_MILESTONE3_REPORT.md) records 140 local/Mock tests at that stage;
later bounded real-provider observations are in M5/M6 and the Phase 2 protocol probe.
Earlier native/UI checks and dependency audits do not establish final packaging or
cross-platform safety. Never describe a proposed Worker as a running Worker.

# Phase 2 — Actual Agent Execution Chain Audit

Date: 2026-11-15 (Asia/Shanghai). Branch: `codex/phase1-continuous`.
This is a source/retained-evidence audit of the evolving Phase 2 working tree, not a
frozen acceptance result. Root is the unique integration owner. Phase 1 M1–M7 reports,
the M7 backend-hardening report, required architecture/protocol documents, and the
named Router/Worker/team/graph/dispatcher/context/memory/provider/tool/evidence/
governance modules were read. Earlier audits under `_audit/` describe the pre-change
state; conclusions below include the current Phase 2 changes.

## Executable chain

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    U[One main user conversation] --> R[Persistent Router: observe, recall, strict decision]
    R -->|chat| A[One user-facing response]
    R -->|create Quest and durable quest.proposed| D[Dispatcher: outbox, leases, inbox, dedup]
    D --> P[Separate Planner: original request, constraints, strict bounded DAG]
    P --> PA[Pending plan: digest, revision, criteria, dependencies]
    PA -->|authenticated local user approves| C[Composer: model profiles, online observations, hard budgets]
    C --> TA[Pending team: roles and models decoupled]
    TA -->|authenticated local user approves| S[WorkerScheduler: ready nodes and concurrency]
    S --> W[Native Worker: private context, model/tool loop, checkpoints]
    W --> T[ToolEngine: policy, grants, exact approvals, intent and receipt]
    T --> W
    W -->|structured worker.result| V[Fresh independent review context]
    V -->|NEEDS_REVISION with concrete goals| RW[Bounded revision of same approved assignment]
    RW --> W
    V -->|PASS| N[NodeVerifier: current provenance and fixed criteria checks]
    N --> G[CompletionGate: recheck approved plan, receipts and evidence]
    G --> Q[Verified task and Quest transitions]
    Q --> D
    D --> RN[Router notice: silent or user progress/result update]
    RN --> A
    W -->|help or blocker event| D
    D -->|help: pending approved replacement proposal| C
    X[ProviderGateway and durable admission ledger] -. all model calls .-> R
    X -.-> P
    X -.-> C
    X -.-> W
    X -.-> V
    M[Task capsules, constraints, source archives and memory] -. bounded context .-> R
    M -. original source recovery .-> W
```

`forge_api.main._core_lifespan` starts six background loops: Dispatcher, Router notices,
Planner, Composer, WorkerScheduler, and review/verification. Provider latency runs
outside SQLite write transactions. A proposal is not an approved plan, an approved
team, a running Worker or a completed task.

1. `RouterService.handle_user_message` synchronizes memory, observes a bounded snapshot,
   calls the configured Gateway, validates `RouterDecision`, and permits one bounded
   schema-repair request. The final user/assistant messages, Quest, source constraints,
   events and idempotent turn record commit atomically. Chat creates no Quest/Worker.
2. `process_pending_plan` consumes the durable creation event. `QuestGraphService.generate`
   receives the original user-message ID/content with its hash, sourced constraints,
   offered tool catalogue and capability names. Generated plans are limited to eight
   nodes/sixteen edges; invalid names/graphs receive one repair opportunity. `propose`
   persists the DAG; `approve` binds authenticated actor, revision, digest and version.
3. `process_pending_team` proposes bounded role contracts. `TeamComposerEngine.compose`
   filters tool/context/cost/budget incompatibilities and offers single-model, greedy,
   coverage and complementarity search. `performance_snapshot` supplies separate,
   source-digested live/Mock observations with sample counts and Wilson intervals for
   rates; it does not rewrite manually supplied capability scores or infer task success
   from transport success. Team approval binds the plan and selected profile hashes.
4. `WorkerScheduler.tick` launches only approved, ready assignments. `WorkerManager.start`
   checks dependencies, effective tool scope, model identity and token/tool/time/agent/
   depth/concurrency limits. `_run` owns a native checkpointed model/tool loop. `_repair`
   preserves failed diagnostics and bounded repair history; provider, contract, budget,
   dependency, authorization, code and tool failures have distinct classifications.
5. `ToolEngine.prepare/execute` enforces current permissions before action, persists an
   exact intent and records its receipt. R1 writes require a Workspace grant; R2 requires
   exact action approval and operator allowlists; unknown/R3 actions fail closed.
   Separately approved `file_revise` can atomically replace only the same Worker's
   own latest artifact after receipt-chain/hash and current authority checks; immutable
   intents and receipts preserve old content. Existing create-only contracts gain no tool.
   Uncertain external effects are not silently repeated after restart or reassignment.
6. `IndependentReviewService` constructs a fresh packet from the original contract,
   criteria, structured delivery, actual bounded artifacts and trustworthy receipts.
   It does not copy the Worker's private conversation. It currently uses the same
   approved underlying model in a separate context: independent context is not model
   diversity. PASS/NEEDS_REVISION/REJECT/BLOCKED are schema-checked; revision requires
   concrete goals and has a default two-round limit, hard maximum four.
   Large review inputs use a lossless envelope of complete untrusted source blocks,
   exact original-message constraint spans and shared repeated metadata; the original
   `_packet` and PASS hash bindings remain unchanged. Full source text and review
   criteria remain, with unchanged context limits; the [118-case input group](review-context-20261115T091955.xml)
   is local/Mock evidence, with larger over-limit packets still rejected.
   Labelled Core JSON-parser errors can request revision without claiming an LLM review or PASS.
   Settled truncated reviews retain actual charges before a bounded fresh verdict;
   output is capped by 8192, the role and the model. Budget/source bindings persist,
   and a committed revision verdict can requeue idempotently after restart.
7. `NodeVerifier` requires the applicable fresh PASS, then performs fixed JSON or numeric
   semantic verification. A genuine failed fixed numeric report may produce labelled
   `deterministic_semantic_validation` feedback for the same Worker's governed revision,
   with exact source/receipt/report/result identities, explicit revision permissions,
   current grant, original budget headroom and no unsettled actions/calls. This is
   neither LLM review nor PASS; the repaired delivery must run the real suite again.
   Persisted feedback before callback can recover once after restart, including
   semantic-only nodes, without a model-review request. Recovery rechecks current
   result/semantic/source/receipt bindings, revision availability, scopes/grants,
   original budgets and absence of unsettled actions/calls; callback errors, stale
   sources and lost authority remain blocked. The [74-case recovery group](semantic-recovery-20261115T090801.xml)
   is local/Mock evidence. `CompletionGate` revalidates approved historical/current
   bindings, original execution mode, actual tool results and artifact hashes before
   completion. Model self-report or Mock evidence alone cannot establish live completion.
8. `Dispatcher` delivers typed event facts at least once with Inbox deduplication and
   fencing. `AgentMessage.from_event` projects task identity and structured coordination
   kinds. Workers cannot directly edit another Worker's task. Only Router appends the
   selected user-facing update to `main`.

## Evidence classification

| Capability | Current implementation | Verification category and limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Persistent single Router/conversation, SQLite UoW/CAS, migrations | Real code and durable records | Local restart/transaction tests; Phase 1 M1–M7 retained evidence |
| Strict Router/Planner decisions and bounded repair | Real Gateway-backed production paths | Current B/F 53-test focused suite; reasoning/orchestration assertions are Mock |
| Planner from original request and source constraints | Separate production component | Mock strict-wire, integrity, catalogue and node-limit regressions |
| Dynamic role/model selection and approved replacement | Real bounded composer/scheduler | Offline/synthetic comparisons and Mock integration; no general live superiority claim |
| Model online statistics | Actual bounded Core observations | Provenance/sample counts retained; sparse priors are not measured abilities |
| Native Worker tools/checkpoints | Real runtime and governed local tools | Phase 1 M5 live numeric/JSON demonstrations; current new recovery branches tested locally/Mock |
| Independent fresh-context review and revision | Real production service and evidence binding | New Mock/adversarial coverage; current complex live review/rework E2E still unverified here |
| Task capsules, constraints, source readback | Real hash-checked archives and index | 39 context/memory tests; M6 retained narrow live continuation; no infinite-capacity claim |
| Recall | Keyword/source/Quest/time/type filters and bilingual aliases | 9/9 exploratory synthetic source-ID/hash cases; learned semantic/embedding recall absent |
| Agent communication | Durable existing event bus with typed projection | Core identity checks and bounded event flow; exhaustive per-type payload contracts remain partial |
| Full autonomous remaining-DAG replanning | Existing proposal/control/replacement interfaces | General automatic safe replanning and hierarchical expansion remain incomplete |
| Independent Reviewer model selection | Same approved model with fresh context | Separate Reviewer model diversity remains an extension, not implemented evidence |
| Complex multi-domain autonomous completion after failure/rework/restart | Components now connected | Must be judged by retained L1/L2/L3 live runs; unverified at this audit snapshot |

The old narrow output-schema compatibility contract still permits summary-only results;
`delivery_review` explicitly requires all eight delivery fields. Do not state that every
legacy Worker contract enforces all eight fields. Default autonomy remains Review:
model-generated plans, teams and replacements remain pending until authenticated approval.

## Actual live Provider evidence

The new retained probe is
`.local/phase2/provider/20261114T233125Z-d07064/report.json`: **11/11 small protocol cases**,
26.712 seconds, `wb-local`, self-reported `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, Gateway through loopback
`127.0.0.1:8788/v1`. It covers minimal dialogue, three Router-schema responses, three tool
call responses, bounded context recall, two concurrent calls and streaming. Discovery
returned eleven IDs and included the requested model. The 300,000-token admission ceiling
and concurrency two were finite configuration, not consumed tokens or service maxima.

These records distinguish proxy response, returned model response and case correctness.
Upstream identity remains **unverified_proxy_reported_identity**. Actual maximum context,
output, rate limits and cost remain unknown; the 65,536 context and 1,024 probe-output
ceilings are operator bounds. Protocol success is not an autonomous task-completion result.
The historical 11/11 run omitted `reasoning_effort` and used the proxy default.
The separate explicit-`none` run `20261115T005858Z-7ae2c8` passed 10/11 cases in
20.210 seconds, with a failed exact-text minimal dialogue check and retained
response hash; its three Router, three tool-call, recall, two concurrent-call and
streaming checks passed. The original 11/11 result and new failed case are retained
separately. A request parameter does not independently prove upstream internal
reasoning behavior; both runs retain unverified proxy-reported model identity.
The [explicit-none probe summary](provider-probe-reasoning-none.json) publishes only
allowlisted observations, including the failed case and its response hash.
Phase 1 M5 additionally retains a real numeric tool run and one JSON-syntax completion;
M6 retains one narrow continuation success after five preserved diagnostic failures.

## Continuity and open boundaries

`ConstraintService` separates literal user clauses, pending model extracts and separately
confirmed records, with original IDs/hashes, potential conflicts, expiry and revocation.
Router/Worker highlights are bounded; omitted originals remain in archives and can be
re-read with source checks. L0 recent interaction, L1 Quest, L2 project/history and L3
failure-experience paths exist. Active Quest counts, indexing batches, candidate pages,
artifact/receipt snapshots and model windows remain finite; learned semantic retrieval,
general source relevance and arbitrary-scale continuity are not established.

Recovery uses durable Worker/model/tool state and lease generations. Unknown remote
outcomes retain reservations until trusted recovery conditions permit action. The current
Worker renews only between settled steps while its token/generation, approved contract
and running Quest remain valid, capped by the task deadline. Expired/stale ownership
cannot be revived and no individual call exceeds its current lease/deadline. The live
driver supports storage compaction/readback, a plan-boundary restart and a restart after
partial node completion. Actual observed snapshots and successful continuation remain
required; a supported option or plan-boundary restart alone does not prove recovery
from an arbitrary in-flight external action.
The independent driver's five offline tests verify missing DB handling, actual budget
inspection, genuine archive/readback, no-op truthfulness and visible integrity failure.
Desktop packaging/UI acceptance is deferred; no new desktop-release claim follows.
New driver snapshots and the Publisher retain only whitelisted runtime settings:
reasoning effort, review-round limit, Worker lease seconds, Provider timeout seconds
and retry limit. Missing legacy fields remain null and do not inherit later configuration.

The fixed tool contracts do not provide arbitrary shell, unrestricted Python,
arbitrary test commands or a general patch operation. `python_compile` proves
syntax only, `numeric_ast` executes a bounded pure numeric subset and
`shell_inspect` permits only `python_version`. `file_write` creates files with
exclusive-create semantics. Explicitly approved `file_revise` only replaces the
same Worker's own latest proven artifact, preserving immutable prior versions;
user files, predecessor artifacts, stale hashes and uncertain outcomes remain
excluded. Review and acceptance compare current bytes with the verified latest
receipt chain rather than treating a legitimate historical hash as current.
Team replacement keeps the approved DAG; Router goal updates
and new DAG proposals remain limited to proposed/awaiting-approval Quests, so
general running-DAG replanning is still absent. Source retrieval remains lexical.

# ADR 009: Source-bound planning, independent review and durable coordination

Status: Phase 2 implementation in progress; local and live acceptance are recorded separately.
Date: 2026-11-15.

## Context

ADRs [007](ADR-007-native-worker-and-execution-evidence.md) and
[008](ADR-008-context-recall-budget.md) establish approved native execution, trusted
receipts, bounded context and Gateway admission. Phase 2 needs stronger planning,
revision and collaboration without replacing those controls or adding user chats.

## Decision

1. Keep the persistent Router as the only user-facing Agent. A separate Planner
   consumes the original request, source hashes, constraints and offered tools to
   propose a bounded DAG. A proposal never grants execution authority; plan and
   team approval continue to require the authenticated local user.
2. Store literal user clauses, pending model extractions and separately confirmed
   clauses with distinct provenance. Bound context highlights and retain original
   source readback paths. Conflicts, omissions, expiry and revocation remain visible;
   extracted instructions never substitute for action approval.
3. Review a delivery in a fresh context containing the original contract, criteria,
   bounded actual artifacts and verified receipts. Do not copy the Worker's private
   conversation. Bind the verdict to its input hash and admitted model attempt.
   `NEEDS_REVISION` requires concrete goals and consumes the existing bounded budget.
   A fresh PASS is necessary for review criteria but remains subject to NodeVerifier
   and CompletionGate checks. The current reviewer uses the approved Worker's model;
   separate context does not establish independent model identity.
   Large inputs may use a lossless wire envelope with full untrusted source blocks,
   receipt/text-hash/byte bindings, shared repeated constraint fields and exact
   original-message character spans. Keep the original `_packet` and PASS hash
   unchanged; omit no source or review criterion and retain all context/budget limits.
4. Project typed Agent messages from the existing durable event/outbox transport.
   Preserve task identity, lease fencing, Inbox deduplication and Router-mediated
   control. Agent messages confer no right to mutate another Worker's assignment.
5. Reuse observed model performance as a sourced, sample-counted input to new team
   proposals. Preserve explicit user scores, approved profile hashes, completed
   nodes and historical contracts. Replacement never resets cumulative budgets.
6. Keep `file_write` create-only. Add separately approved R1 `file_revise` only for
   the current Worker's own latest successfully produced artifact, with exact prior
   receipt/hash, current authority/grant checks and atomic replacement. Retain old
   content in immutable intent/receipt history; review and completion validate the
   bounded same-Worker chain and latest bytes. Do not extend old contracts or grant
   authority over user files, predecessor artifacts or unsettled outcomes.
7. Distinguish Core JSON-parser feedback (`deterministic_artifact_validation`,
   `core_json_parser`) from model review. Parser failures may request concrete
   bounded revision but create no model attempt or PASS. Reviewer output is capped
   at `min(8192, role output_limit, model_max_output_tokens)`; settled truncation
   charges exact actual usage before any bounded new verdict. Unknown remote
   outcomes retain reservations. Committed revision verdicts requeue idempotently.
8. Renew Worker ownership only between settled steps after current token/generation,
   plan/team and status checks, to `min(task deadline, now + lease_seconds)`. Do not
   revive expired claims or enlarge task allocations. Individual calls remain
   bounded by their current lease/deadline.
9. Treat a node's token allowance as cumulative input/output/review/repair usage,
   separate from each model context window. Align the node schema ceiling with the
   existing finite 1,000,000-token graph ceiling; keep the sum of node allowances
   within the approved graph total and retain all lower scenario, team and global
   limits. This does not change previously approved budgets or grant unlimited use.
10. Bind fixed numeric-suite failure feedback to the latest delivery, exact
    Quest/plan/revision/Worker/run, real semantic run/report, source and receipt.
    Label it `deterministic_semantic_validation` / `core_fixed_numeric_suite`, with
    at most ten failed-case diagnostics and no LLM verdict or PASS. Invoke the same
    Worker's revision handler only with explicit graph/node/Worker/member revision
    scopes, a current grant, remaining original budgets and no unresolved actions
    or model attempts; a new delivery must pass the real suite again.

## Consequences and limits

The implementation adds focused services and schema changes rather than a parallel
runtime. Default Review autonomy, policy, exact approvals, receipts and Gateway
reservations remain authoritative. Unknown remote effects stay unresolved until
trusted recovery conditions permit settlement; a client timeout permits no replay.
The [118-case review-input group](../audit/phase2/review-context-20261115T091955.xml)
records local/Mock reconstruction and admission checks. Its L2 fixture's native
Gateway construction reserves 64,245 under the same 65,536 ceiling; this made no
network call and establishes no general larger-packet capacity or live success.

Fixed-suite feedback rejects duplicate results, callback errors and fake success;
if a callback commits before raising, the exact queued revision is fenced blocked.
A crash after semantic feedback commit but before callback permits idempotent
recovery through `IndependentReviewService.tick()`, including semantic-only nodes,
without a model-review request. Recovery requires `revision_available=true`, the
current delivery and genuine semantic/source/receipt bindings, current tool
scopes/grants, remaining original budgets and no unsettled actions or Gateway
attempts. The Worker revision interface rechecks approved team, cumulative
repair/step/token/deadline limits and one-time event consumption. Stale or changed
sources, revoked grants, exhausted budgets and originally unavailable revisions
remain blocked. The [74-case recovery group](../audit/phase2/semantic-recovery-20261115T090801.xml)
provides local/Mock evidence; this does not authorize unknown-action replay or
establish live task correctness.

Schema repair, review rounds, Agent counts, context packets and replanning are
bounded. General automatic remaining-DAG replanning, arbitrary hierarchical Agent
expansion, exhaustive per-message payload schemas and learned semantic retrieval
remain incomplete. The legacy summary-only delivery contract stays compatible;
`delivery_review` explicitly requires all eight delivery fields. Local/Mock tests
and synthetic benchmarks do not establish complex live-task acceptance. See the
[Phase 2 report](../PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md) for the current evidence.

The current execution boundary remains the fixed Core toolset: bounded numeric
AST, syntax checks and diagnostics, with create-only writes and explicitly scoped
own-artifact revision. General program execution, arbitrary test runners, general
repository patching and running-DAG revision remain incomplete.

# FORGE 项目状态

更新：2026-11-15（Asia/Shanghai）

## 当前状态

**Phase 2 Agent Intelligence 进行中，复杂任务真实验收尚未完成。** 本轮重点为现有后端的 Router/Planner、动态团队、Native Worker、独立审查返工、有来源的上下文与记忆、Agent 协调和真实端到端实验。进度见 [Phase 2 状态](PHASE2_STATUS.md)、[完整报告](PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md)和[实验记录](PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md)；最小架构调整见 [ADR 009](adr/ADR-009-agent-intelligence-contracts-and-review.md)。

Explicitly approved `file_revise` only replaces the current Worker's own latest produced artifact with receipt-chain/hash checks and immutable version history; user files, predecessor artifacts, stale versions and uncertain outcomes are excluded. - Worker leases renew only between settled steps for a valid current owner, bounded by the task deadline. Expired/stale claims, changed plans, competing owners and paused/cancelled assignments cannot be revived; calls remain capped by the current lease/deadline and unknown outcomes retain reservations.

   preserves failed diagnostics and bounded repair history; provider, contract, budget,
   dependency, authorization, code and tool failures have distinct classifications.
5. `ToolEngine.prepare/execute` enforces current permissions before action, persists an
   exact intent and records its receipt. R1 writes require a Workspace grant; R2 requires
   exact action approval and operator allowlists; unknown/R3 actions fail closed.
   Separately approved `file_revise` can atomically replace only the same Worker's
   own latest artifact after receipt-chain/hash and current authority checks; immutable
   intents and receipts preserve old content. Existing create-only contracts gain no tool.
   Uncertain external effects are not silently repeated after restart or reassignment.
6. `IndependentReviewService` constructs a fresh packet from the original contract,
   criteria, structured delivery, actual bounded artifacts and trustworthy receipts.
   It does not copy the Worker's private conversation. It currently uses the same
   approved underlying model in a separate context: independent context is not model
   diversity. PASS/NEEDS_REVISION/REJECT/BLOCKED are schema-checked; revision requires
   concrete goals and has a default two-round limit, hard maximum four.
   Large review inputs use a lossless envelope of complete untrusted source blocks,
   exact original-message constraint spans and shared repeated metadata; the original
   `_packet` and PASS hash bindings remain unchanged. Full source text and review
   criteria remain, with unchanged context limits; the [118-case input group](review-context-20261115T091955.xml)
   is local/Mock evidence, with larger over-limit packets still rejected.
   Labelled Core JSON-parser errors can request revision without claiming an LLM review or PASS.
   Settled truncated reviews retain actual charges before a bounded fresh verdict;
   output is capped by 8192, the role and the model. Budget/source bindings persist,
   and a committed revision verdict can requeue idempotently after restart.
7. `NodeVerifier` requires the applicable fresh PASS, then performs fixed JSON or numeric
   semantic verification. A genuine failed fixed numeric report may produce labelled
   `deterministic_semantic_validation` feedback for the same Worker's governed revision,
   with exact source/receipt/report/result identities, explicit revision permissions,
   current grant, original budget headroom and no unsettled actions/calls. This is
   neither LLM review nor PASS; the repaired delivery must run the real suite again.
   Persisted feedback before callback can recover once after restart, including
   semantic-only nodes, without a model-review request. Recovery rechecks current
   result/semantic/source/receipt bindings, revision availability, scopes/grants,
   original budgets and absence of unsettled actions/calls; callback errors, stale
   sources and lost authority remain blocked. The [74-case recovery group](semantic-recovery-20261115T090801.xml)
   is local/Mock evidence. `CompletionGate` revalidates approved historical/current
   bindings, original execution mode, actual tool results and artifact hashes before
   completion. Model self-report or Mock evidence alone cannot establish live completion.
8. `Dispatcher` delivers typed event facts at least once with Inbox deduplication and
   fencing. `AgentMessage.from_event` projects task identity and structured coordination
   kinds. Workers cannot directly edit another Worker's task. Only Router appends the
   selected user-facing update to `main`.

## Evidence classification

| Capability | Current implementation | Verification category and limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Persistent single Router/conversation, SQLite UoW/CAS, migrations | Real code and durable records | Local restart/transaction tests; Phase 1 M1–M7 retained evidence |
| Strict Router/Planner decisions and bounded repair | Real Gateway-backed production paths | Current B/F 53-test focused suite; reasoning/orchestration assertions are Mock |
| Planner from original request and source constraints | Separate production component | Mock strict-wire, integrity, catalogue and node-limit regressions |
| Dynamic role/model selection and approved replacement | Real bounded composer/scheduler | Offline/synthetic comparisons and Mock integration; no general live superiority claim |
| Model online statistics | Actual bounded Core observations | Provenance/sample counts retained; sparse priors are not measured abilities |
| Native Worker tools/checkpoints | Real runtime and governed local tools | Phase 1 M5 live numeric/JSON demonstrations; current new recovery branches tested locally/Mock |
| Independent fresh-context review and revision | Real production service and evidence binding | New Mock/adversarial coverage; current complex live review/rework E2E still unverified here |
| Task capsules, constraints, source readback | Real hash-checked archives and index | 39 context/memory tests; M6 retained narrow live continuation; no infinite-capacity claim |
| Recall | Keyword/source/Quest/time/type filters and bilingual aliases | 9/9 exploratory synthetic source-ID/hash cases; learned semantic/embedding recall absent |
| Agent communication | Durable existing event bus with typed projection | Core identity checks and bounded event flow; exhaustive per-type payload contracts remain partial |
| Full autonomous remaining-DAG replanning | Existing proposal/control/replacement interfaces | General automatic safe replanning and hierarchical expansion remain incomplete |
| Independent Reviewer model selection | Same approved model with fresh context | Separate Reviewer model diversity remains an extension, not implemented evidence |
| Complex multi-domain autonomous completion after failure/rework/restart | Components now connected | Must be judged by retained L1/L2/L3 live runs; unverified at this audit snapshot |

The old narrow output-schema compatibility contract still permits summary-only results;
`delivery_review` explicitly requires all eight delivery fields. Do not state that every
legacy Worker contract enforces all eight fields. Default autonomy remains Review:
model-generated plans, teams and replacements remain pending until authenticated approval.

## Actual live Provider evidence

The new retained probe is
`.local/phase2/provider/20261114T233125Z-d07064/report.json`: **11/11 small protocol cases**,
26.712 seconds, `wb-local`, self-reported `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, Gateway through loopback
`127.0.0.1:8788/v1`. It covers minimal dialogue, three Router-schema responses, three tool
call responses, bounded context recall, two concurrent calls and streaming. Discovery
returned eleven IDs and included the requested model. The 300,000-token admission ceiling
and concurrency two were finite configuration, not consumed tokens or service maxima.

These records distinguish proxy response, returned model response and case correctness.
Upstream identity remains **unverified_proxy_reported_identity**. Actual maximum context,
output, rate limits and cost remain unknown; the 65,536 context and 1,024 probe-output
ceilings are operator bounds. Protocol success is not an autonomous task-completion result.
The historical 11/11 run omitted `reasoning_effort` and used the proxy default.
The separate explicit-`none` run `20261115T005858Z-7ae2c8` passed 10/11 cases in
20.210 seconds, with a failed exact-text minimal dialogue check and retained
response hash; its three Router, three tool-call, recall, two concurrent-call and
streaming checks passed. The original 11/11 result and new failed case are retained
separately. A request parameter does not independently prove upstream internal
reasoning behavior; both runs retain unverified proxy-reported model identity.
The [explicit-none probe summary](provider-probe-reasoning-none.json) publishes only
allowlisted observations, including the failed case and its response hash.
Phase 1 M5 additionally retains a real numeric tool run and one JSON-syntax completion;
M6 retains one narrow continuation success after five preserved diagnostic failures.

## Continuity and open boundaries

`ConstraintService` separates literal user clauses, pending model extracts and separately
confirmed records, with original IDs/hashes, potential conflicts, expiry and revocation.
Router/Worker highlights are bounded; omitted originals remain in archives and can be
re-read with source checks. L0 recent interaction, L1 Quest, L2 project/history and L3
failure-experience paths exist. Active Quest counts, indexing batches, candidate pages,
artifact/receipt snapshots and model windows remain finite; learned semantic retrieval,
general source relevance and arbitrary-scale continuity are not established.

Recovery uses durable Worker/model/tool state and lease generations. Unknown remote
outcomes retain reservations until trusted recovery conditions permit action. The current
Worker renews only between settled steps while its token/generation, approved contract
and running Quest remain valid, capped by the task deadline. Expired/stale ownership
cannot be revived and no individual call exceeds its current lease/deadline. The live
driver supports storage compaction/readback, a plan-boundary restart and a restart after
partial node completion. Actual observed snapshots and successful continuation remain
required; a supported option or plan-boundary restart alone does not prove recovery
from an arbitrary in-flight external action.
The independent driver's five offline tests verify missing DB handling, actual budget
inspection, genuine archive/readback, no-op truthfulness and visible integrity failure.
Desktop packaging/UI acceptance is deferred; no new desktop-release claim follows.
New driver snapshots and the Publisher retain only whitelisted runtime settings:
reasoning effort, review-round limit, Worker lease seconds, Provider timeout seconds
and retry limit. Missing legacy fields remain null and do not inherit later configuration.

The fixed tool contracts do not provide arbitrary shell, unrestricted Python,
arbitrary test commands or a general patch operation. `python_compile` proves
syntax only, `numeric_ast` executes a bounded pure numeric subset and
`shell_inspect` permits only `python_version`. `file_write` creates files with
exclusive-create semantics. Explicitly approved `file_revise` only replaces the
same Worker's own latest proven artifact, preserving immutable prior versions;
user files, predecessor artifacts, stale hashes and uncertain outcomes remain
excluded. Review and acceptance compare current bytes with the verified latest
receipt chain rather than treating a legitimate historical hash as current.
Team replacement keeps the approved DAG; Router goal updates
and new DAG proposals remain limited to proposed/awaiting-approval Quests, so
general running-DAG replanning is still absent. Source retrieval remains lexical.

# Detailed Implementation Roadmap

## Current Phase 2 Agent Intelligence sprint — 2026-11-15

Phase 2 is in progress; the requested complex live-task acceptance is pending.
This sprint's Phase 2 label is distinct from the original feature-phase numbering
retained below. See [Phase 2 status](PHASE2_STATUS.md), [report](PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md)
and [experiments](PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md).

- A: Audit the executable chain and probe the existing Provider/Gateway. Recorded: 11/11 small live protocol cases with the proxy default; 10/11 with explicit `reasoning_effort=none`, retaining a failed exact-text dialogue check. The setting does not prove upstream internal reasoning behavior; actual upstream identity, service maxima and price remain unknown.
- B: Separate Router/Planner, preserve original request/constraint sources and bound repair/DAG generation. Implemented with local/Mock coverage; complex live planning acceptance pending.
- C: Reuse bounded composition strategies and source online performance into new proposals. Local/Mock and synthetic comparisons recorded; general live-quality improvement unproven.
- D/E: Connect native repair, independent fresh-context review, concrete bounded revision and evidence-gated completion. Explicitly approved own-artifact `file_revise`, lossless full-source review inputs, labelled Core parser/fixed-suite feedback, idempotent persisted-feedback recovery, settled-truncation review retry and fenced between-step lease renewal now have local/Mock coverage. Original packet/PASS bindings, context limits and source/authority/budget/unresolved-outcome guards remain enforced. Final frozen integration and complex live failure/rework results pending.
- General code execution/editing remains open: current Workers have fixed diagnostics, syntax checks, numeric AST and create-only `file_write`; `file_revise` is limited to the same Worker's latest proven artifact with immutable history. General repository editing/test execution and safe running-DAG replanning require further work; current team replacement retains the existing DAG.
- F/G: Bound context highlights while retaining original-source recovery; project typed Agent messages over the existing durable transport and preserve conservative recovery. Semantic retrieval, exhaustive message payload schemas and arbitrary in-flight recovery remain open.
- H: Complete and record L1/L2/L3 native live tasks with actual tools/artifacts, independent checks, compaction and Core restart. Input descriptors and driver exist; final results pending.
- I: Preserve fixed team/context/governance baselines and ablations. Offline mechanism results exist; same-budget real model-quality and Reviewer comparisons remain open.

Completion requires independently evidenced complex-task continuity through failure,
repair, review revision, compaction and restart. Protocol success, local tests or
proposal creation alone do not satisfy it. Desktop packaging remains deferred.

## Historical continuous engineering milestones

- Milestone 1：数据可靠性本机验证完成，历史交付保留。
- Milestone 2：治理、Core 本地信任边界、证据门槛基础及依赖锁通过阶段审查；当时的范围见 [报告](PHASE1_MILESTONE2_REPORT.md)。
- Milestone 3：Provider Gateway、Persistent Router 和模型画像基础完成本机 Mock 协议测试；当时的范围见 [报告](PHASE1_MILESTONE3_REPORT.md)。后续有限真实供应商验证见 M5、M6 报告。
- Milestone 4：Quest Graph、事件投递和应用生命周期接线已完成本机 Mock/SQLite 验证，详见 [报告](PHASE1_MILESTONE4_REPORT.md)。
- Milestone 5：Native Worker、动态团队、固定工具治理与可信执行证据已完成本机冻结验收（282 项测试）；真实供应商通过有限的数值与 JSON 产物演示，范围见 [报告](PHASE1_MILESTONE5_REPORT.md)。
- Milestone 6：Context 归档、来源 Recall 与 Gateway 模型调用统一预算通过本机验证（372 passed）；真实供应商一次有界连续任务恢复成功，前五次诊断失败保留。容量和范围见 [报告](PHASE1_MILESTONE6_REPORT.md)。
- Milestone 7：桌面 Alpha 与 Tauri Core 生命周期正在集成；早期隔离原生启动已观察，最终原生联调、安装包和 Alpha 验收仍待完成。见 [报告草稿](PHASE1_MILESTONE7_REPORT.md)。

以下是原始目标清单，保留作为功能范围参考，而非当前完成状态的逐项核对；它的 Phase 编号与上述连续开发 Milestone 编号不同。具体已验证范围和剩余限制以上述报告及 [STATUS](STATUS.md) 为准。

## Phase 0 — Engineering audit
- [ ] Inspect Python/Node/Rust/Tauri toolchain and repository.
- [ ] Run tests and frontend build.
- [ ] Create ADRs and architecture guardrails.
- [ ] Confirm local startup scripts and deterministic DB location.
- [ ] Add CI workflow and static checks.
- [ ] Record real results in STATUS.
Acceptance: clean environment can start API/UI; tests pass.

## Phase 1 — Persistent Router
- [ ] Replace heuristic classifier with provider-backed Router Agent Loop.
- [ ] Define structured RouterAction schema.
- [ ] Implement intent and Quest reference resolution.
- [ ] Persist Router capsule and event cursor.
- [ ] Implement one unified conversation timeline.
- [ ] Ensure restart recovery.
Acceptance: multiple different topics and concurrent Quests remain in one user-visible conversation.

## Phase 2 — Quest Graph and event relay
- [ ] Add TaskNode, dependencies, cycle checks and DAG scheduler.
- [ ] Add worker event inbox/outbox and idempotent consumers.
- [ ] Add progress coalescing and important-event direct delivery.
- [ ] Add Quest pause/resume/cancel/update.
Acceptance: Worker progress/results appear in the same conversation; no separate user chat.

## Phase 3 — Model Registry
- [ ] Provider adapters for OpenAI-compatible and native APIs.
- [ ] Secure OS credential vault.
- [ ] Provider model discovery where supported.
- [ ] Benchmark task definitions and versioning.
- [ ] Benchmark runner and provenance.
- [ ] Online performance statistics and user override.
Acceptance: at least two real providers and auditable capability profiles.

## Phase 4 — Native Runtime and tools
- [ ] Streaming model gateway and retry/error mapping.
- [ ] Agent Loop and structured tool-call parser.
- [ ] Tool schemas and policy enforcement.
- [ ] Sandboxed file and command tools.
- [ ] Worker session persistence, cancellation and recovery.
Acceptance: a Worker performs a bounded multi-step task using native runtime.

## Phase 5 — Dynamic Team Composer
- [ ] Role templates and bounded dynamic role synthesis.
- [ ] Capability/confidence scoring.
- [ ] Cost/latency/context/concurrency constraints.
- [ ] Complementarity and coordination penalty.
- [ ] Explainable team proposals and approval.
- [ ] Dynamic re-composition on failure/blocker.
Acceptance: Router builds and explains a suitable team for distinct task types.

## Phase 6 — Context and Chain of Recall
- [ ] Task Capsule and compaction trigger.
- [ ] Archive and restore conversation context.
- [ ] Quest/project memory and evidence-linked retrieval.
- [ ] Memory freshness, contradiction and invalidation.
Acceptance: long task resumes after compaction/restart without losing constraints.

## Phase 7 — Governance and evidence
- [ ] Risk policy and exact-scope approvals.
- [ ] Budget ledger and circuit breakers.
- [ ] Evidence graph and artifact hashes.
- [ ] Independent verification.
Acceptance: unsafe actions blocked; completion supported by evidence.

## Phase 8 — Desktop release
- [ ] Tauri Rust bootstrap and Core lifecycle manager.
- [ ] Single chat with embedded Quest cards.
- [ ] Model Library, Agent activity, Memory and Approval views.
- [ ] OS credential storage, backup/restore and Windows installer.
Acceptance: end-to-end local desktop demo.

## Definition of Done
Every phase includes code, tests, docs, migration, error handling, logs, reproducible demo and STATUS update. No phase is complete based only on code generation.

# ADR 009: Source-bound planning, independent review and durable coordination

Status: Phase 2 implementation in progress; local and live acceptance are recorded separately.
Date: 2026-11-15.

## Context

ADRs [007](ADR-007-native-worker-and-execution-evidence.md) and
[008](ADR-008-context-recall-budget.md) establish approved native execution, trusted
receipts, bounded context and Gateway admission. Phase 2 needs stronger planning,
revision and collaboration without replacing those controls or adding user chats.

## Decision

1. Keep the persistent Router as the only user-facing Agent. A separate Planner
   consumes the original request, source hashes, constraints and offered tools to
   propose a bounded DAG. A proposal never grants execution authority; plan and
   team approval continue to require the authenticated local user.
2. Store literal user clauses, pending model extractions and separately confirmed
   clauses with distinct provenance. Bound context highlights and retain original
   source readback paths. Conflicts, omissions, expiry and revocation remain visible;
   extracted instructions never substitute for action approval.
3. Review a delivery in a fresh context containing the original contract, criteria,
   bounded actual artifacts and verified receipts. Do not copy the Worker's private
   conversation. Bind the verdict to its input hash and admitted model attempt.
   `NEEDS_REVISION` requires concrete goals and consumes the existing bounded budget.
   A fresh PASS is necessary for review criteria but remains subject to NodeVerifier
   and CompletionGate checks. The current reviewer uses the approved Worker's model;
   separate context does not establish independent model identity.
   Large inputs may use a lossless wire envelope with full untrusted source blocks,
   receipt/text-hash/byte bindings, shared repeated constraint fields and exact
   original-message character spans. Keep the original `_packet` and PASS hash
   unchanged; omit no source or review criterion and retain all context/budget limits.
4. Project typed Agent messages from the existing durable event/outbox transport.
   Preserve task identity, lease fencing, Inbox deduplication and Router-mediated
   control. Agent messages confer no right to mutate another Worker's assignment.
5. Reuse observed model performance as a sourced, sample-counted input to new team
   proposals. Preserve explicit user scores, approved profile hashes, completed
   nodes and historical contracts. Replacement never resets cumulative budgets.
6. Keep `file_write` create-only. Add separately approved R1 `file_revise` only for
   the current Worker's own latest successfully produced artifact, with exact prior
   receipt/hash, current authority/grant checks and atomic replacement. Retain old
   content in immutable intent/receipt history; review and completion validate the
   bounded same-Worker chain and latest bytes. Do not extend old contracts or grant
   authority over user files, predecessor artifacts or unsettled outcomes.
7. Distinguish Core JSON-parser feedback (`deterministic_artifact_validation`,
   `core_json_parser`) from model review. Parser failures may request concrete
   bounded revision but create no model attempt or PASS. Reviewer output is capped
   at `min(8192, role output_limit, model_max_output_tokens)`; settled truncation
   charges exact actual usage before any bounded new verdict. Unknown remote
   outcomes retain reservations. Committed revision verdicts requeue idempotently.
8. Renew Worker ownership only between settled steps after current token/generation,
   plan/team and status checks, to `min(task deadline, now + lease_seconds)`. Do not
   revive expired claims or enlarge task allocations. Individual calls remain
   bounded by their current lease/deadline.
9. Treat a node's token allowance as cumulative input/output/review/repair usage,
   separate from each model context window. Align the node schema ceiling with the
   existing finite 1,000,000-token graph ceiling; keep the sum of node allowances
   within the approved graph total and retain all lower scenario, team and global
   limits. This does not change previously approved budgets or grant unlimited use.
10. Bind fixed numeric-suite failure feedback to the latest delivery, exact
    Quest/plan/revision/Worker/run, real semantic run/report, source and receipt.
    Label it `deterministic_semantic_validation` / `core_fixed_numeric_suite`, with
    at most ten failed-case diagnostics and no LLM verdict or PASS. Invoke the same
    Worker's revision handler only with explicit graph/node/Worker/member revision
    scopes, a current grant, remaining original budgets and no unresolved actions
    or model attempts; a new delivery must pass the real suite again.

## Consequences and limits

The implementation adds focused services and schema changes rather than a parallel
runtime. Default Review autonomy, policy, exact approvals, receipts and Gateway
reservations remain authoritative. Unknown remote effects stay unresolved until
trusted recovery conditions permit settlement; a client timeout permits no replay.
The [118-case review-input group](../audit/phase2/review-context-20261115T091955.xml)
records local/Mock reconstruction and admission checks. Its L2 fixture's native
Gateway construction reserves 64,245 under the same 65,536 ceiling; this made no
network call and establishes no general larger-packet capacity or live success.

Fixed-suite feedback rejects duplicate results, callback errors and fake success;
if a callback commits before raising, the exact queued revision is fenced blocked.
A crash after semantic feedback commit but before callback permits idempotent
recovery through `IndependentReviewService.tick()`, including semantic-only nodes,
without a model-review request. Recovery requires `revision_available=true`, the
current delivery and genuine semantic/source/receipt bindings, current tool
scopes/grants, remaining original budgets and no unsettled actions or Gateway
attempts. The Worker revision interface rechecks approved team, cumulative
repair/step/token/deadline limits and one-time event consumption. Stale or changed
sources, revoked grants, exhausted budgets and originally unavailable revisions
remain blocked. The [74-case recovery group](../audit/phase2/semantic-recovery-20261115T090801.xml)
provides local/Mock evidence; this does not authorize unknown-action replay or
establish live task correctness.

Schema repair, review rounds, Agent counts, context packets and replanning are
bounded. General automatic remaining-DAG replanning, arbitrary hierarchical Agent
expansion, exhaustive per-message payload schemas and learned semantic retrieval
remain incomplete. The legacy summary-only delivery contract stays compatible;
`delivery_review` explicitly requires all eight delivery fields. Local/Mock tests
and synthetic benchmarks do not establish complex live-task acceptance. See the
[Phase 2 report](../PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md) for the current evidence.

The current execution boundary remains the fixed Core toolset: bounded numeric
AST, syntax checks and diagnostics, with create-only writes and explicitly scoped
own-artifact revision. General program execution, arbitrary test runners, general
repository patching and running-DAG revision remain incomplete.

# FORGE 项目状态

更新：2026-11-15（Asia/Shanghai）

## 当前状态

**Phase 2 Agent Intelligence 进行中，复杂任务真实验收尚未完成。** 本轮重点为现有后端的 Router/Planner、动态团队、Native Worker、独立审查返工、有来源的上下文与记忆、Agent 协调和真实端到端实验。进度见 [Phase 2 状态](PHASE2_STATUS.md)、[完整报告](PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md)和[实验记录](PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md)；最小架构调整见 [ADR 009](adr/ADR-009-agent-intelligence-contracts-and-review.md)。

当前已记录 B/F 局部合并 **53 passed / 18.36 秒**、驱动 **5 passed / 0.57 秒**、C/I **42 passed / 14.61 秒**、D/E/G **128 passed / 46.34 秒**、Provider/目标来源 **42 passed / 4.56 秒**；这些测试有重叠，不能相加作为完整套件数量。离线 v2 为小规模固定合成实验，零次 Provider 调用。本地 workbuddy-api/wb-in 的 `deepseek-v4.1-flash` 经 Gateway 的历史 proxy-default 探针为 **11/11 小协议案例 / 26.712 秒**；显式 `reasoning_effort=none` 探针为 **10/11 / 20.210 秒**，精确文本对话检查失败保留。参数不证明上游内部 reasoning 行为，上游身份仍是代理自报。L1/L2/L3 的最终任务、返工、产物和连续性结果及冻结完整套件待集成负责人汇总；协议通过不能代替复杂任务验收。

后续[自产物修订与 Reviewer 修复](audit/phase2/sprint-deg.md)局部组为 **153 passed / 40.63 秒**，租约恢复组 **90 passed / 32.30 秒**，返工 verdict 提交后重排队恢复组 **28 passed / 13.95 秒**。这些仍是有重叠的本地/Mock 工程验证，不构成新的 live 成功结论。

[固定数值套件失败到同 Worker 修订重验](audit/phase2/sprint-ci.md)扩大组为 **119 passed / 44.14 秒**，含首轮 21 个新增案例；后续[语义反馈恢复组](audit/phase2/semantic-recovery-20261115T090801.xml)为 **74 passed / 34.65 秒**，语义测试文件现有 30 个案例。本地真实数值子进程与脚本模型不算真实 Provider 验收。反馈需有来源、显式修订权限、有效 grant、原预算余量且无未结算动作/调用；修订后仍须真实套件通过。反馈提交后 callback 前崩溃可在重验当前结果、真实语义来源、权限/grant 和原预算后幂等恢复，无需发模型审查；旧结果、变化来源、撤权、预算耗尽、未知动作和回调异常仍阻断。

[审查输入无损表示组](audit/phase2/review-context-20261115T091955.xml)为 **118 passed / 36.18 秒**：完整 source、精确字符范围和共享元数据保留原 packet/PASS 哈希；确切 L2 fixture 的本地 native Gateway reserve 为 64,245，仍受 65,536 上限约束。未发网络请求、未追认旧运行，更大输入超界仍拒绝。新发布的运行配置只含白名单字段，旧记录缺失值保持 null。

用户已暂缓 M7 桌面验收；单一持久聊天的桌面联调、Core 生命周期、设置、审批范围、凭据、备份恢复及安装包仍须以最终实际结果为准。历史[后端加固](PHASE1_MILESTONE7_BACKEND_HARDENING.md)冻结快照为 **488 passed，1 warning，107.62 秒**，双工作目录 Ruff、格式及依赖检查通过，见[验证记录](audit/phase1/milestone7-backend-hardening-verification.json)。它不是当前 Phase 2 的完整套件或桌面发布验收。总体桌面待验项见 [M7 报告草稿](PHASE1_MILESTONE7_REPORT.md)。

Milestone 5 的 Native Worker、动态团队、工具治理与独立证据链已完成本机冻结验收：**282 passed，1 warning，44.99 秒**；真实供应商完成有限的 numeric AST 和 JSON 产物演示，范围见 [M5 报告](PHASE1_MILESTONE5_REPORT.md)。Milestone 6 的最终快照本机完整测试为 **372 passed，1 warning，77.78 秒**，静态、依赖与历史证据核验通过；一次有界真实供应商任务恢复成功，前五次诊断失败均保留。有限合成研究及容量边界见 [M6 报告](PHASE1_MILESTONE6_REPORT.md)。这些结果不能证明无限对话或通用任务正确性。

Router、Planner、Composer、benchmark、Worker 与独立 Reviewer 的模型请求沿用统一 Gateway 准入。价格未知时使用 token-only，不推算费用。当前默认 Review 审批保持启用；通用剩余 DAG 自主重规划、完整类型 payload 合同、学习式语义召回和独立 Reviewer 模型选择仍未完成。当前限制和质量门槛见 [QUALITY_GATES](QUALITY_GATES.md)，配置及恢复复核步骤见 [README](../README.md)。

当前 Worker 使用固定工具、语法检查和有界数值 AST，尚无任意代码/测试命令执行或通用代码补丁工具。`file_write` 仅新建；显式批准的 `file_revise` 可凭最新回执链和未变化哈希，原子修订当前 Worker 自己产出的文件并保留不可变版本，不能修改用户文件或前驱产物。Reviewer 的 Core JSON 解析反馈明确标记来源，不冒充模型审查；已结算截断重试消耗原预算与轮次。租约仅在已结算步骤间续期，仍受当前权限、代次围栏和任务截止约束。运行中团队替换保持同一 DAG；这不等于自主重规划。检索为有来源的词法召回，以上缺口不因局部测试通过而视为完成。

## 历史阶段与证据

各阶段报告和审计记录保留当时的测试结果、限制和待办，其历史描述不代表当前状态：

- [Phase 0 审计](PHASE0_AUDIT.md)及[验证证据](audit/phase0/verification.json)。
- [Milestone 1](PHASE1_MILESTONE1_REPORT.md)、[Milestone 2](PHASE1_MILESTONE2_REPORT.md)、[Milestone 3](PHASE1_MILESTONE3_REPORT.md) 和 [Milestone 4](PHASE1_MILESTONE4_REPORT.md) 报告。
- [Milestone 5](PHASE1_MILESTONE5_REPORT.md) 和 [Milestone 6](PHASE1_MILESTONE6_REPORT.md) 报告及各自审计证据。

历史审计脚本可能覆盖历史证据，重跑前应使用独立输出位置。阶段路线及尚未验证的验收目标见 [ROADMAP](ROADMAP.md)。

Status: Phase 2 implementation in progress; local and live acceptance are recorded separately.
Date: 2026-11-15.

## Context

ADRs [007](ADR-007-native-worker-and-execution-evidence.md) and
[008](ADR-008-context-recall-budget.md) establish approved native execution, trusted
receipts, bounded context and Gateway admission. Phase 2 needs stronger planning,
revision and collaboration without replacing those controls or adding user chats.

## Decision

1. Keep the persistent Router as the only user-facing Agent. A separate Planner
   consumes the original request, source hashes, constraints and offered tools to
   propose a bounded DAG. A proposal never grants execution authority; plan and
   team approval continue to require the authenticated local user.
2. Store literal user clauses, pending model extractions and separately confirmed
   clauses with distinct provenance. Bound context highlights and retain original
   source readback paths. Conflicts, omissions, expiry and revocation remain visible;
   extracted instructions never substitute for action approval.
3. Review a delivery in a fresh context containing the original contract, criteria,
   bounded actual artifacts and verified receipts. Do not copy the Worker's private
   conversation. Bind the verdict to its input hash and admitted model attempt.
   `NEEDS_REVISION` requires concrete goals and consumes the existing bounded budget.
   A fresh PASS is necessary for review criteria but remains subject to NodeVerifier
   and CompletionGate checks. The current reviewer uses the approved Worker's model;
   separate context does not establish independent model identity.
   Large inputs may use a lossless wire envelope with full untrusted source blocks,
   receipt/text-hash/byte bindings, shared repeated constraint fields and exact
   original-message character spans. Keep the original `_packet` and PASS hash
   unchanged; omit no source or review criterion and retain all context/budget limits.
4. Project typed Agent messages from the existing durable event/outbox transport.
   Preserve task identity, lease fencing, Inbox deduplication and Router-mediated
   control. Agent messages confer no right to mutate another Worker's assignment.
5. Reuse observed model performance as a sourced, sample-counted input to new team
   proposals. Preserve explicit user scores, approved profile hashes, completed
   nodes and historical contracts. Replacement never resets cumulative budgets.
6. Keep `file_write` create-only. Add separately approved R1 `file_revise` only for
   the current Worker's own latest successfully produced artifact, with exact prior
   receipt/hash, current authority/grant checks and atomic replacement. Retain old
   content in immutable intent/receipt history; review and completion validate the
   bounded same-Worker chain and latest bytes. Do not extend old contracts or grant
   authority over user files, predecessor artifacts or unsettled outcomes.
7. Distinguish Core JSON-parser feedback (`deterministic_artifact_validation`,
   `core_json_parser`) from model review. Parser failures may request concrete
   bounded revision but create no model attempt or PASS. Reviewer output is capped
   at `min(8192, role output_limit, model_max_output_tokens)`; settled truncation
   charges exact actual usage before any bounded new verdict. Unknown remote
   outcomes retain reservations. Committed revision verdicts requeue idempotently.
8. Renew Worker ownership only between settled steps after current token/generation,
   plan/team and status checks, to `min(task deadline, now + lease_seconds)`. Do not
   revive expired claims or enlarge task allocations. Individual calls remain
   bounded by their current lease/deadline.
9. Treat a node's token allowance as cumulative input/output/review/repair usage,
   separate from each model context window. Align the node schema ceiling with the
   existing finite 1,000,000-token graph ceiling; keep the sum of node allowances
   within the approved graph total and retain all lower scenario, team and global
   limits. This does not change previously approved budgets or grant unlimited use.
10. Bind fixed numeric-suite failure feedback to the latest delivery, exact
    Quest/plan/revision/Worker/run, real semantic run/report, source and receipt.
    Label it `deterministic_semantic_validation` / `core_fixed_numeric_suite`, with
    at most ten failed-case diagnostics and no LLM verdict or PASS. Invoke the same
    Worker's revision handler only with explicit graph/node/Worker/member revision
    scopes, a current grant, remaining original budgets and no unresolved actions
    or model attempts; a new delivery must pass the real suite again.

## Consequences and limits

The implementation adds focused services and schema changes rather than a parallel
runtime. Default Review autonomy, policy, exact approvals, receipts and Gateway
reservations remain authoritative. Unknown remote effects stay unresolved until
trusted recovery conditions permit settlement; a client timeout permits no replay.
The [118-case review-input group](../audit/phase2/review-context-20261115T091955.xml)
records local/Mock reconstruction and admission checks. Its L2 fixture's native
Gateway construction reserves 64,245 under the same 65,536 ceiling; this made no
network call and establishes no general larger-packet capacity or live success.

Fixed-suite feedback rejects duplicate results, callback errors and fake success;
if a callback commits before raising, the exact queued revision is fenced blocked.
A crash after semantic feedback commit but before callback permits idempotent
recovery through `IndependentReviewService.tick()`, including semantic-only nodes,
without a model-review request. Recovery requires `revision_available=true`, the
current delivery and genuine semantic/source/receipt bindings, current tool
scopes/grants, remaining original budgets and no unsettled actions or Gateway
attempts. The Worker revision interface rechecks approved team, cumulative
repair/step/token/deadline limits and one-time event consumption. Stale or changed
sources, revoked grants, exhausted budgets and originally unavailable revisions
remain blocked. The [74-case recovery group](../audit/phase2/semantic-recovery-20261115T090801.xml)
provides local/Mock evidence; this does not authorize unknown-action replay or
establish live task correctness.

Schema repair, review rounds, Agent counts, context packets and replanning are
bounded. General automatic remaining-DAG replanning, arbitrary hierarchical Agent
expansion, exhaustive per-message payload schemas and learned semantic retrieval
remain incomplete. The legacy summary-only delivery contract stays compatible;
`delivery_review` explicitly requires all eight delivery fields. Local/Mock tests
and synthetic benchmarks do not establish complex live-task acceptance. See the
[Phase 2 report](../PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md) for the current evidence.

The current execution boundary remains the fixed Core toolset: bounded numeric
AST, syntax checks and diagnostics, with create-only writes and explicitly scoped
own-artifact revision. General program execution, arbitrary test runners, general
repository patching and running-DAG revision remain incomplete.

# Phase 2 — Agent Intelligence Report

Updated: 2026-11-15 (Asia/Shanghai). Branch: `codex/phase1-continuous`.
Integration owner: root agent. **Phase 2 is in progress. One strict L1 run passed;
L2/L3 acceptance and final frozen-source verification remain incomplete.**

## Scope and architectural change

This sprint moves the existing backend toward autonomous task execution. Desktop
visual changes, packaging and the deferred M7 desktop Alpha are outside this sprint's
acceptance. Existing Phase 1 reports and failed experiments remain preserved.

The source audit and complete execution diagram are in the
[execution-chain audit](audit/phase2/execution-chain-audit.md). The minimum change is
recorded in [ADR 009](adr/ADR-009-agent-intelligence-contracts-and-review.md):

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    U[One user conversation] --> R[Persistent Router]
    R --> P[Separate Planner and proposed DAG]
    P --> A[Authenticated plan and team approval]
    A --> W[Native private Worker loops]
    W --> T[Governed tools and receipts]
    T --> V[Fresh independent review]
    V -->|concrete revision goals| W
    V --> N[NodeVerifier and CompletionGate]
    N --> R
```

All model requests use the existing Gateway and durable admission ledger. The
Router remains the only user-facing Agent. Workers, reviewers and durable events
do not create extra user conversations or use another Agent product as a backend.

## Implemented mechanisms

| Area | Current behavior | Verification boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Router and Planner | Strict decisions, one bounded repair, atomic turn commits, original and latest goal-update request IDs/hashes, offered-tool/capability checks, DAG limit of eight nodes/sixteen edges | Mock reasoning and local persistence regressions; live protocol coverage below |
| Team intelligence | Existing single-model/greedy/coverage/complementarity strategies consume sourced online observations with counts and Wilson intervals; proposals retain profile/source hashes | Synthetic selection proxies and local/Mock integration; no measured general model-quality gain |
| Team adaptation | Approved replacement may cover remaining nodes while retaining completed assignments and historical approvals | Local regression; general autonomous remaining-DAG replanning and hierarchical expansion incomplete |
| Native Worker | Private model/tool loop, checkpoints, fenced lease renewal between settled steps, bounded repair, distinct failure categories and structured delivery | Existing M5 live demonstrations; new branches covered locally/Mock pending complex live results |
| Artifact revision | Separately approved R1 `file_revise` atomically replaces the same Worker's own latest produced artifact using an intact receipt chain and unchanged hash | Local/Mock race, provenance and immutable-history checks; general repository editing remains absent |
| Independent review | Fresh packet from original goal, criteria, real artifacts and receipts; PASS/NEEDS_REVISION/REJECT/BLOCKED; concrete revision goals, default two-round limit, hard maximum four | Current same approved underlying model in a separate context; independent model diversity is absent |
| Evidence gate | Review provenance plus fixed semantic verifiers and final receipt/artifact/approval checks govern completion | Mock/adversarial regressions and actual local tool checks; self-report never establishes live completion |
| Context and constraints | Bounded Router/Worker highlights, original-source readback, sourced literal/pending/confirmed clauses, potential conflicts, expiry and revocation | 53 combined Router/Planner/context/memory tests; 9 exploratory synthetic source-identity cases |
| Memory | L0 current interaction, L1 Quest, L2 project/history and L3 failure observations; bounded keyword/alias/Quest/time/type filtering | Lexical retrieval; embeddings and learned semantic relevance absent |
| Agent protocol/recovery | Typed projection of existing event transport with task identities, fenced leases and deduplication; unresolved effects retain reservations | Per-type payload validation remains partial; arbitrary in-flight external-effect recovery is unproven |

The delivery vocabulary contains `summary`, `findings`, `decisions`, `artifacts`,
`evidence_references`, `unresolved_issues`, `confidence` and `next_actions`.
`delivery_review` enforces all eight. Legacy/default compatibility schemas still
require only `summary`; missing fields are not evidence of completed work.

`file_write` remains create-only. `file_revise` requires explicit plan/node and
team authority plus a workspace grant, with `path`, `prior_receipt_id`,
`expected_sha256` and full replacement `content`. It checks the latest successful
same-Worker receipt, current file bytes and authority immediately before atomic
replacement. Immutable intent parameters and receipts retain every prior version.
Review and read-only acceptance validate the bounded revision chain (at most 64
receipts) before comparing current bytes with the latest successful version.
Predecessor artifacts, user files, stale hashes and unsettled outcomes are excluded;
old create-only contracts acquire no additional authority.

Reviewer output is capped by 8192, the approved role/model caps, remaining model
context and original cumulative Worker tokens. Adaptive capacity keeps a floor of
`min(1024, original output cap)`; inability to fit that floor or original cost
limits fails closed. Native Gateway input reservation uses the actual serialized
payload, including schema/reasoning settings, and matches Core admission.
Review evaluates the current node's objective, criteria and approved role; an
intermediate read-only researcher is not asked to produce a downstream writer's
artifact. Nodes assigned final deliverables retain all original requirements.
`FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` defaults to two and accepts integers one through four;
the live harness explicitly selects three within its scenario's three-round cap.
Existing runs retain their original review limits and results.
Large packets can use a lossless wire envelope while the original `_packet` and
PASS `packet_sha256` stay unchanged. Full `file_read` source text appears once in
untrusted blocks bound to receipt references, text SHA256 and UTF-8 lengths.
Repeated constraint metadata uses shared fields; a statement already present
verbatim in an original/update message uses that same source's exact Unicode
`[start,end)` span, otherwise its full text remains. Native structured-output
requests retain the Gateway schema while avoiding a duplicate system-prompt copy.
The original L2 fixture packet was 56,755 bytes: its old conservative reserve was
73,065, the review-envelope estimate is 64,622 and actual local
`ProviderGateway._payload` construction reserves 64,245, within the same 65,536
context ceiling. All three source texts remain complete. This construction made
no network call, changed no historical run and establishes admission only for
that exact fixture; larger packets still fail closed when limits are exceeded.
Receipt-bound JSON syntax errors produce concrete line/column and receipt/hash
feedback labelled `deterministic_artifact_validation` / `core_json_parser`, with
`NEEDS_REVISION` only while repair/round/step/token/deadline limits permit, otherwise
