# Phase 2 — Actual Agent Execution Chain Audit

Date: 2026-11-15 (Asia/Shanghai). Branch: `codex/phase1-continuous`.
This is a source/retained-evidence audit of the evolving Phase 2 working tree, not a
frozen acceptance result. Root is the unique integration owner. Phase 1 M1–M7 reports,
the M7 backend-hardening report, required architecture/protocol documents, and the
named Router/Worker/team/graph/dispatcher/context/memory/provider/tool/evidence/
governance modules were read. Earlier audits under `_audit/` describe the pre-change
state; conclusions below include the current Phase 2 changes.

## Executable chain

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    U[One main user conversation] --> R[Persistent Router: observe, recall, strict decision]
    R -->|chat| A[One user-facing response]
    R -->|create Quest and durable quest.proposed| D[Dispatcher: outbox, leases, inbox, dedup]
    D --> P[Separate Planner: original request, constraints, strict bounded DAG]
    P --> PA[Pending plan: digest, revision, criteria, dependencies]
    PA -->|authenticated local user approves| C[Composer: model profiles, online observations, hard budgets]
    C --> TA[Pending team: roles and models decoupled]
    TA -->|authenticated local user approves| S[WorkerScheduler: ready nodes and concurrency]
    S --> W[Native Worker: private context, model/tool loop, checkpoints]
    W --> T[ToolEngine: policy, grants, exact approvals, intent and receipt]
    T --> W
    W -->|structured worker.result| V[Fresh independent review context]
    V -->|NEEDS_REVISION with concrete goals| RW[Bounded revision of same approved assignment]
    RW --> W
    V -->|PASS| N[NodeVerifier: current provenance and fixed criteria checks]
    N --> G[CompletionGate: recheck approved plan, receipts and evidence]
    G --> Q[Verified task and Quest transitions]
    Q --> D
    D --> RN[Router notice: silent or user progress/result update]
    RN --> A
    W -->|help or blocker event| D
    D -->|help: pending approved replacement proposal| C
    X[ProviderGateway and durable admission ledger] -. all model calls .-> R
    X -.-> P
    X -.-> C
    X -.-> W
    X -.-> V
    M[Task capsules, constraints, source archives and memory] -. bounded context .-> R
    M -. original source recovery .-> W
```

`forge_api.main._core_lifespan` starts six background loops: Dispatcher, Router notices,
Planner, Composer, WorkerScheduler, and review/verification. Provider latency runs
outside SQLite write transactions. A proposal is not an approved plan, an approved
team, a running Worker or a completed task.

1. `RouterService.handle_user_message` synchronizes memory, observes a bounded snapshot,
   calls the configured Gateway, validates `RouterDecision`, and permits one bounded
   schema-repair request. The final user/assistant messages, Quest, source constraints,
   events and idempotent turn record commit atomically. Chat creates no Quest/Worker.
2. `process_pending_plan` consumes the durable creation event. `QuestGraphService.generate`
   receives the original user-message ID/content with its hash, sourced constraints,
   offered tool catalogue and capability names. Generated plans are limited to eight
   nodes/sixteen edges; invalid names/graphs receive one repair opportunity. `propose`
   persists the DAG; `approve` binds authenticated actor, revision, digest and version.
3. `process_pending_team` proposes bounded role contracts. `TeamComposerEngine.compose`
   filters tool/context/cost/budget incompatibilities and offers single-model, greedy,
   coverage and complementarity search. `performance_snapshot` supplies separate,
   source-digested live/Mock observations with sample counts and Wilson intervals for
   rates; it does not rewrite manually supplied capability scores or infer task success
   from transport success. Team approval binds the plan and selected profile hashes.
4. `WorkerScheduler.tick` launches only approved, ready assignments. `WorkerManager.start`
   checks dependencies, effective tool scope, model identity and token/tool/time/agent/
   depth/concurrency limits. `_run` owns a native checkpointed model/tool loop. `_repair`
   preserves failed diagnostics and bounded repair history; provider, contract, budget,
   dependency, authorization, code and tool failures have distinct classifications.
5. `ToolEngine.prepare/execute` enforces current permissions before action, persists an
   exact intent and records its receipt. R1 writes require a Workspace grant; R2 requires
   exact action approval and operator allowlists; unknown/R3 actions fail closed.

do not create extra user conversations or use another Agent product as a backend.

## Implemented mechanisms

| Area | Current behavior | Verification boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Team adaptation | Approved replacement may cover remaining nodes while retaining completed assignments and historical approvals | Local regression; general autonomous remaining-DAG replanning and hierarchical expansion incomplete |
| Native Worker | Private model/tool loop, checkpoints, fenced lease renewal between settled steps, bounded repair, distinct failure categories and structured delivery | Existing M5 live demonstrations; new branches covered locally/Mock pending complex live results |
| Artifact revision | Separately approved R1 `file_revise` atomically replaces the same Worker's own latest produced artifact using an intact receipt chain and unchanged hash | Local/Mock race, provenance and immutable-history checks; general repository editing remains absent |

README.md:1:# FORGE v4 — Persistent Router Agent System
README.md:7:Phase 2 Agent Intelligence is in progress. The existing native runtime now connects a separate Planner, source-bound constraints and bounded memory, observation-informed team proposals, fresh-context independent review and typed durable Agent coordination. One retained strict L1 live run passed with review revision and Worker self-repair, without compaction or restart; the concurrent L2 and later L3 attempts failed. New L2/L3 reruns, complex-task continuity and final frozen-source verification remain pending. The local Provider's small live protocol probes passed [11/11 with the proxy default](docs/audit/phase2/provider-probe.json) and [10/11 with explicit `reasoning_effort=none`](docs/audit/phase2/provider-probe-reasoning-none.json); the latter retained a failed exact-text dialogue check. Focused local/Mock suites and exploratory synthetic benchmarks are recorded separately. See the [Phase 2 report](docs/PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md), [status](docs/PHASE2_STATUS.md), [experiments](docs/PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md) and [architecture decision](docs/adr/ADR-009-agent-intelligence-contracts-and-review.md).
README.md:145:Legacy databases are **not discovered or moved automatically**. If an earlier version used `backend/data/forge.sqlite3` or another CWD-relative location, stop its Core process, back up the database with SQLite's backup API (or copy the database and WAL files together while stopped), and set `FORGE_DB_PATH` to its absolute path. The first successful open migrates it in place to the current schema without changing the Router ID or existing records. Migration failure rolls back the entire pending chain; unknown future versions and ambiguous version metadata are rejected. Downgrades are unsupported.
README.md:147:Events and pending Outbox rows commit in the same transaction as their associated business changes. Durable per-consumer delivery uses leases, fencing, bounded retries, Inbox deduplication and dead-letter/replay records. Historical events migrate as pending. External tool effects require their own durable intents and receipts; event delivery alone does not make external effects exactly once.
README.md:151:Workers consume an approved Quest DAG and a separately approved team. Tool scopes, provider/model identity and token/tool/time/concurrency budgets are bound to those contracts. File writes additionally require a workspace grant; HTTPS/MCP actions require exact action approval and an operator allowlist. `FORGE_TOOL_NETWORK_HOSTS_JSON` is a JSON host list (at most 64); `FORGE_MCP_SERVERS_JSON` maps server names to `{"url":"https://example.invalid/mcp","tools":["example_tool"]}` (at most 16 servers), with the HTTPS host included in the allowlist. Defaults are empty and deny network access. These values are operator configuration, never model output. `jsonschema` validates Worker result contracts; it does not judge domain correctness. Help/reassignment produces a pending team proposal for authenticated approval. An uncertain action cannot be silently retried or discarded during replacement. Unsupported or failed fixed JSON criteria require manual review; infrastructure verification retries are bounded to three attempts.

# Independent review scope and bounded verdict capacity

Date: 2026-11-15 (Asia/Shanghai). This is a local/Mock regression and read-only
diagnostic record, not a successful live rerun.

## Retained live failure

`20261115T012115Z-L2-8e64f5` stopped after 96.416 seconds. A SQLite connection
opened with `mode=ro` confirmed 19 settled Gateway attempts, 92,916 input and
10,436 output tokens, six successful live read/list tool calls, and no unknown
remote outcomes. No report artifact was produced. The first read-only
`source-research` node was still `review_pending`; its two dependent nodes had
not executed.

The first independent review requested creation of the final report from this
read-only research node. Its approved objective and role contract instead
required source analysis; the final report belonged to the later writing node.
The Worker retained its scope and explicitly declined to claim a write. Review
of the expanded revision then stopped at `review_context_limit` before a second
Reviewer model call. The run's earlier stop reason mentioning unsettled attempts
is a boundary observation; the final durable ledger contains no unknown attempts.

## Changes

The Reviewer system instruction now evaluates the current node objective,
success criteria and approved role contract. The original user request remains
available in full, supplies applicable constraints, and still governs a node
assigned the corresponding final deliverable. Missing assigned artifacts continue
to fail provenance checks before model judgment. Revision instructions grant no
additional authority.

The original `_packet` and PASS hash binding are unchanged. No source, receipt,
delivery or constraint is removed. Single-response output remains bounded by
8,192, the role cap and the model cap; it additionally fits the remaining model
context and original cumulative Worker token allowance. Adaptive capacity below
1,024 is refused, while an existing role/model cap below 1,024 remains valid.
Insufficient original cost authority still fails closed. Original step, time,
review-round, reservation and unknown-outcome rules remain in force.

For the native Gateway, the Core computes input reservation from the actual
Gateway payload using the same serialized-byte accounting as admission. This
includes schema instructions, response format and configured reasoning options.
The final output cap is reflected in that exact payload before admission.

## Exact retained L2 construction

Reconstruction used the existing database in read-only mode and made no network
call. Its unchanged packet is 59,601 UTF-8 bytes, SHA-256
`1b5e7f48459f751f9a79ca309762cb97da7c4e5ae38095f265d3c915aad04e4a`.
The six receipt entries contain no identical full source contents to deduplicate.
With the clarified scope instruction, fixed output 8,192 would reserve 67,953.
The adaptive native request reserves input 59,761 plus output 5,775 = 65,536,
within the unchanged context ceiling. Prior cumulative Worker usage is 61,083
against the original 130,000 allocation. This construction establishes capacity,
not Reviewer verdict quality or live task completion.

## Validation

The focused group covers source/constraint reconstruction, current-node scope,

README.md:7:Phase 2 Agent Intelligence is in progress. The existing native runtime now connects a separate Planner, source-bound constraints and bounded memory, observation-informed team proposals, fresh-context independent review and typed durable Agent coordination. One retained strict L1 live run passed with review revision and Worker self-repair, without compaction or restart; the concurrent L2 and later L3 attempts failed. New L2/L3 reruns, complex-task continuity and final frozen-source verification remain pending. The local Provider's small live protocol probes passed [11/11 with the proxy default](docs/audit/phase2/provider-probe.json) and [10/11 with explicit `reasoning_effort=none`](docs/audit/phase2/provider-probe-reasoning-none.json); the latter retained a failed exact-text dialogue check. Focused local/Mock suites and exploratory synthetic benchmarks are recorded separately. See the [Phase 2 report](docs/PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md), [status](docs/PHASE2_STATUS.md), [experiments](docs/PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md) and [architecture decision](docs/adr/ADR-009-agent-intelligence-contracts-and-review.md).
README.md:145:Legacy databases are **not discovered or moved automatically**. If an earlier version used `backend/data/forge.sqlite3` or another CWD-relative location, stop its Core process, back up the database with SQLite's backup API (or copy the database and WAL files together while stopped), and set `FORGE_DB_PATH` to its absolute path. The first successful open migrates it in place to the current schema without changing the Router ID or existing records. Migration failure rolls back the entire pending chain; unknown future versions and ambiguous version metadata are rejected. Downgrades are unsupported.
README.md:147:Events and pending Outbox rows commit in the same transaction as their associated business changes. Durable per-consumer delivery uses leases, fencing, bounded retries, Inbox deduplication and dead-letter/replay records. Historical events migrate as pending. External tool effects require their own durable intents and receipts; event delivery alone does not make external effects exactly once.
README.md:151:Workers consume an approved Quest DAG and a separately approved team. Tool scopes, provider/model identity and token/tool/time/concurrency budgets are bound to those contracts. File writes additionally require a workspace grant; HTTPS/MCP actions require exact action approval and an operator allowlist. `FORGE_TOOL_NETWORK_HOSTS_JSON` is a JSON host list (at most 64); `FORGE_MCP_SERVERS_JSON` maps server names to `{"url":"https://example.invalid/mcp","tools":["example_tool"]}` (at most 16 servers), with the HTTPS host included in the allowlist. Defaults are empty and deny network access. These values are operator configuration, never model output. `jsonschema` validates Worker result contracts; it does not judge domain correctness. Help/reassignment produces a pending team proposal for authenticated approval. An uncertain action cannot be silently retried or discarded during replacement. Unsupported or failed fixed JSON criteria require manual review; infrastructure verification retries are bounded to three attempts.

## 检查记录

首次 focused run 为 37 passed / 1 failed：失败是已有 `TeamRoleWire.output_schema_json` 兼容改动导致生成 schema 不满足 strict required 约束；已保留解析兼容性并修正 schema。最终团队/重组/注册表及新增 benchmark/provenance 测试为 **42 passed，14.61 秒**。本子任务七个修改或新建 Python 文件的 Ruff 检查及格式通过；历史测试和审计未删除。

没有数据库迁移、运行依赖或环境变量新增。主要剩余限制：没有自动学习通用能力分数、没有凭一次调用评分、没有声称实现任意 Agent 层级/无限动态扩展；本轮的线上反馈是有界观察驱动的新提案排序。端到端真实性以主验收报告的独立 live 记录为准。

## 独立验收与历史证据发布

`backend/scripts/phase2/acceptance_checks.py` 提供 `evaluate_scenario(scenario, inspection, workspace, run_record=record)`。它只以 SQLite `mode=ro` 打开现有数据库，不创建 Store、不执行候选源码、不发 Provider 请求。逐项结果为 passed / failed / unknown，只有全部 passed 才通过。检查当前批准图与节点投影、历史批准团队、live Worker、精确 Gateway 调用、不可变工具回执、实际产物字节及哈希、八字段交付、输入来源完整性与读取回执。独立内容 PASS 通过 Core 的 `review_pass_matches` 在显式读取事务内重新构造来源包；L3 固定套件使用 `SemanticVerifier.validate_evidence` 重新验证源、回执与可信 provenance。

模型生成图要求 `quest.plan_proposed` 的 `planner_call_id / response_sha256 / graph_digest / source_event_id` 绑定到确切已结算 Planner 调用与当前图摘要；旧记录缺失该绑定为 unknown。L1 检查单 Worker、只读工具、排名发现或明确证据不足；L2 检查三至四个专业 Worker、真实引用和实际最终 JSON 的内容审查；L3 还要求不同有效输入的 numeric_ast 回执，其源码须与最终调度器逐字节相同。执行无关常数例子不能满足真实调度器实验要求。

L3 重启检查比较前后 Router identity 与当前数据库值，且要求已完成节点与剩余执行同时存在、实际 before/after_start 快照均无未结算远端调用或动作、成功节点及精确回执/调用/Worker 预算计数保留、最终数据库仍保留这些来源且计数不回退，并实际成功 resume。仅 approved-plan、尚未执行 Worker 的重启不满足 L3 验收。压缩需要实际 archive 和逐条原始来源 SHA256 回读。无法观测的用量、重启或压缩保持 unknown，费用未知保留 null。来源引用格式与范围可机械检查，引用与结论的语义相关性仍由独立 Reviewer 评估；模型判断不构成一般正确性证明。

`backend/scripts/phase2/publish_evidence.py` 只读取主驱动已经脱敏的 `run.json`，输出允许列表中的状态、失败码、用量、回执身份与哈希，不发布提示词、回复、日志、完整本地路径或产物正文。源快照与发布文件均以 SHA256/字节数索引，输出目录必须全新；后续实现不会追认历史失败为成功。首批 `docs/audit/phase2/live-runs/diagnostic-snapshot-v1/index.json` 包含 9 次主集成 live 诊断快照，其中旧记录未保存的状态保持 null；本子任务只发布已有记录，Provider 请求仍为 0。

```powershell

## Reproduction and live acceptance contract

From `backend`, using the existing virtual environment, write to a new output path:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/phase2/intelligence_benchmark.py --output 'D:\path\to\new-benchmark.json'
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/phase2/retrieval_evaluation.py --output 'D:\path\to\new-retrieval.json'
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/test_constraints_phase2.py tests/test_context_m6.py tests/test_memory_m6.py tests/test_router_intelligence_phase2.py -q
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/test_phase2_driver.py -q
```

model attempts. No synthetic feedback or model claim substitutes for rerunning the
real suite. Persisted feedback can recover once after a crash before callback,
including semantic-only nodes, without a model-review call. Recovery requires an
originally available revision, current result/semantic/source/receipt bindings,
current scopes/grants and remaining original budgets with no unsettled actions or
Gateway attempts. Changed or stale inputs, revoked authority, exhausted budgets,
callback errors and fake success remain fail closed. This bounded recovery is not
replay permission for an unknown external action.

Each final live record must retain Run ID, Provider/model, execution mode, model/tool
calls, charged/unknown token usage, duration, retries, review verdicts/revisions,
artifact hashes, final status and failure diagnostics. Price stays unknown when no
trusted price is configured. Report success denominator, evidence completeness,
compaction source readback and observed restart boundary explicitly. The retained
L1 pass and L2/L3 failures above are recorded; later reruns and final freeze remain
pending. Run directories and proposed tasks are not acceptance evidence.
The driver's `runtime_settings` and Publisher whitelist retain only reasoning
effort, review-round limit, Worker lease seconds, Provider timeout seconds and retry limit.
Missing values in older records remain null, with no retrospective inference or
approval/configuration change.

## Consequences and limits

The implementation adds focused services and schema changes rather than a parallel
runtime. Default Review autonomy, policy, exact approvals, receipts and Gateway
reservations remain authoritative. Unknown remote effects stay unresolved until
trusted recovery conditions permit settlement; a client timeout permits no replay.
The [118-case review-input group](../audit/phase2/review-context-20261115T091955.xml)
records local/Mock reconstruction and admission checks. Its L2 fixture's native
Gateway construction reserves 64,245 under the same 65,536 ceiling; this made no
network call and establishes no general larger-packet capacity or live success.

Recovery uses durable Worker/model/tool state and lease generations. Unknown remote
outcomes retain reservations until trusted recovery conditions permit action. The current
Worker renews only between settled steps while its token/generation, approved contract
and running Quest remain valid, capped by the task deadline. Expired/stale ownership
cannot be revived and no individual call exceeds its current lease/deadline. The live
driver supports storage compaction/readback, a plan-boundary restart and a restart after
partial node completion. Actual observed snapshots and successful continuation remain
required; a supported option or plan-boundary restart alone does not prove recovery
from an arbitrary in-flight external action.
The independent driver's five offline tests verify missing DB handling, actual budget
inspection, genuine archive/readback, no-op truthfulness and visible integrity failure.
Desktop packaging/UI acceptance is deferred; no new desktop-release claim follows.
New driver snapshots and the Publisher retain only whitelisted runtime settings:
reasoning effort, review-round limit, Worker lease seconds, Provider timeout seconds
retry limit and effective model token/concurrency limits. Missing legacy fields remain null and do not inherit later configuration.

The fixed tool contracts do not provide arbitrary shell, unrestricted Python,
arbitrary test commands or a general patch operation. `python_compile` proves
syntax only, `numeric_ast` executes a bounded pure numeric subset and
`shell_inspect` permits only `python_version`. `file_write` creates files with
exclusive-create semantics. Explicitly approved `file_revise` only replaces the
same Worker's own latest proven artifact, preserving immutable prior versions;
user files, predecessor artifacts, stale hashes and uncertain outcomes remain
excluded. Review and acceptance compare current bytes with the verified latest
receipt chain rather than treating a legitimate historical hash as current.
Team replacement keeps the approved DAG; Router goal updates
and new DAG proposals remain limited to proposed/awaiting-approval Quests, so
general running-DAG replanning is still absent. Source retrieval remains lexical.

## Consequences and limits

The implementation adds focused services and schema changes rather than a parallel
runtime. Default Review autonomy, policy, exact approvals, receipts and Gateway
reservations remain authoritative. Unknown remote effects stay unresolved until
trusted recovery conditions permit settlement; a client timeout permits no replay.
The [118-case review-input group](../audit/phase2/review-context-20261115T091955.xml)
records local/Mock reconstruction and admission checks. Its L2 fixture's native
Gateway construction reserves 64,245 under the same 65,536 ceiling; this made no
network call and establishes no general larger-packet capacity or live success.

Recovery uses durable Worker/model/tool state and lease generations. Unknown remote
outcomes retain reservations until trusted recovery conditions permit action. The current
Worker renews only between settled steps while its token/generation, approved contract
and running Quest remain valid, capped by the task deadline. Expired/stale ownership
cannot be revived and no individual call exceeds its current lease/deadline. The live
driver supports storage compaction/readback, a plan-boundary restart and a restart after
partial node completion. Actual observed snapshots and successful continuation remain
required; a supported option or plan-boundary restart alone does not prove recovery
from an arbitrary in-flight external action.
The independent driver's five offline tests verify missing DB handling, actual budget
inspection, genuine archive/readback, no-op truthfulness and visible integrity failure.
Desktop packaging/UI acceptance is deferred; no new desktop-release claim follows.
New driver snapshots and the Publisher retain only whitelisted runtime settings:
reasoning effort, review-round limit, Worker lease seconds, Provider timeout seconds
retry limit and effective model token/concurrency limits. Missing legacy fields remain null and do not inherit later configuration.

The fixed tool contracts do not provide arbitrary shell, unrestricted Python,
arbitrary test commands or a general patch operation. `python_compile` proves
syntax only, `numeric_ast` executes a bounded pure numeric subset and
`shell_inspect` permits only `python_version`. `file_write` creates files with
exclusive-create semantics. Explicitly approved `file_revise` only replaces the
same Worker's own latest proven artifact, preserving immutable prior versions;
user files, predecessor artifacts, stale hashes and uncertain outcomes remain
excluded. Review and acceptance compare current bytes with the verified latest
receipt chain rather than treating a legitimate historical hash as current.
Team replacement keeps the approved DAG; Router goal updates
and new DAG proposals remain limited to proposed/awaiting-approval Quests, so
general running-DAG replanning is still absent. Source retrieval remains lexical.

README.md:7:Phase 2 Agent Intelligence is in progress. The existing native runtime now connects a separate Planner, source-bound constraints and bounded memory, observation-informed team proposals, fresh-context independent review and typed durable Agent coordination. One retained strict L1 live run passed with review revision and Worker self-repair, without compaction or restart; the concurrent L2 and later L3 attempts failed. Later L2/L3 reruns also failed before review at packet/context and cumulative-budget limits. The [v5 full backend suite](docs/audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v5.xml) passed 820 tests with one warning in 219.96 seconds, before later v6 changes. New v6 full/live results, complex-task continuity and final frozen-source verification remain pending. The local Provider's small live protocol probes passed [11/11 with the proxy default](docs/audit/phase2/provider-probe.json) and [10/11 with explicit `reasoning_effort=none`](docs/audit/phase2/provider-probe-reasoning-none.json); the latter retained a failed exact-text dialogue check. Focused local/Mock suites and exploratory synthetic benchmarks are recorded separately. See the [Phase 2 report](docs/PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md), [status](docs/PHASE2_STATUS.md), [experiments](docs/PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md) and [architecture decision](docs/adr/ADR-009-agent-intelligence-contracts-and-review.md).

# FORGE v4 — Persistent Router Agent System

FORGE is a self-built, general-purpose autonomous Agent desktop application.

## Engineering status — 2026-11-15

Phase 2 Agent Intelligence is in progress. The existing native runtime now connects a separate Planner, source-bound constraints and bounded memory, observation-informed team proposals, fresh-context independent review and typed durable Agent coordination. One retained strict L1 live run passed with review revision and Worker self-repair, without compaction or restart; the concurrent L2 and later L3 attempts failed. Later L2/L3 reruns also failed before review at packet/context and cumulative-budget limits. The [v5 full backend suite](docs/audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v5.xml) passed 820 tests with one warning in 219.96 seconds, before later v6 changes. New v6 full/live results, complex-task continuity and final frozen-source verification remain pending. The local Provider's small live protocol probes passed [11/11 with the proxy default](docs/audit/phase2/provider-probe.json) and [10/11 with explicit `reasoning_effort=none`](docs/audit/phase2/provider-probe-reasoning-none.json); the latter retained a failed exact-text dialogue check. Focused local/Mock suites and exploratory synthetic benchmarks are recorded separately. See the [Phase 2 report](docs/PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md), [status](docs/PHASE2_STATUS.md), [experiments](docs/PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md) and [architecture decision](docs/adr/ADR-009-agent-intelligence-contracts-and-review.md).

Phase 1 Milestones 1–6 provide the persistence, governance, Registry, DAG, native Workers, tool/evidence and context/budget foundation. Historical M6 verification passed 372 tests; one bounded live continuation succeeded after five retained diagnostic failures. The [M7 backend hardening round](docs/PHASE1_MILESTONE7_BACKEND_HARDENING.md) passed 488 local tests. Desktop Alpha, final native integration and packaging are deferred; these historical backend results do not establish a desktop release.

See [current status](docs/STATUS.md), the [Phase 0 audit report](docs/PHASE0_AUDIT.md), and the report's dependency-ordered development plan. The release references `codex/MASTER_PROMPT.md`, but that file is missing from the supplied archive.

**The user has one persistent conversation.** A persistent Router Agent owns that conversation and coordinates multiple long-running Quests and hidden Worker Sessions. Workers have isolated execution contexts, but they are never presented as separate user conversations.

## Product invariants

1. One persistent user-facing conversation per workspace.

README.md:7:Phase 2 Agent Intelligence is in progress. The existing native runtime now connects a separate Planner, source-bound constraints and bounded memory, observation-informed team proposals, fresh-context independent review and typed durable Agent coordination. One retained strict L1 live run passed with review revision and Worker self-repair, without compaction or restart; the concurrent L2 and later L3 attempts failed. Later L2/L3 reruns also failed before review at packet/context and cumulative-budget limits. The [v5 full backend suite](docs/audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v5.xml) passed 820 tests with one warning in 219.96 seconds, before later v6 changes. The [v6 full suite](docs/audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v6.xml) retained 848 passed, one failed, one warning / 283.77 seconds; all three v6 live reruns failed. V7 corrects independent Worker/Gateway concurrency and extends bounded handoff/budget guidance. The [v7 full suite](docs/audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v7.xml) passed 849 tests / one warning / 216.87 seconds, while all three v7 live attempts failed. V8 strict-delivery, node-scope and bounded repair changes have focused coverage; new v8 full/live results, complex-task continuity and final frozen-source verification remain pending. # V8 continuity and live failure audit

This is a read-only inspection of frozen v8 source and retained live evidence. No source, runtime state, approval, receipt or historical run was changed; no provider request was made. The frozen manifest is `92bb6067ff7bc1dadfa6aa9b5994089969603b53b3980a9a5601d0a140e6b9e3` (156 files, `source-manifest-v8.json`). This audit does not add acceptance requirements.

## What the continuity harness actually checks

`backend/scripts/phase2/live_e2e.py:328` implements a real, quiescent restart during a Quest. The normal trigger at line 718 requires a completed node and remaining nodes. It pauses the Quest through authenticated plan control, waits until no model attempts, governed actions or Workers remain in flight, stops Core, compacts Router context, starts Core against the same workspace, observes Router identity, compares before/after durable anchors and resumes through authenticated control. It refuses a restart with unresolved execution. This establishes the intended scope of the experiment; it makes no claim about arbitrary crashes during unresolved external effects.

`continuity_snapshot` at line 201 reads SQLite in `mode=ro` within a transaction. Its anchors include node identities/status, action-receipt digests/mode, model-attempt states/charged usage and Worker token/step/tool counters. `compare_continuity` at line 315 requires an actual succeeded node rather than a vacuous empty set, and compares the retained anchors.

`backend/scripts/phase2/acceptance_checks.py:466` independently rechecks the recorded before/after snapshots against final durable rows. It requires both completed and remaining work, quiet snapshots, retained receipts and settled/rejected attempts, nondecreasing final Worker counters, matching plan/node identities and successful resume. `_continuity` at line 563 compares both recorded Router identities with the actual stored identity. Missing observations remain unknown; a pre-execution restart does not satisfy the mid-execution scope.

`compact_stopped_core` at `live_e2e.py:165` calls the actual `ContextService.compact_router(keep_recent=1)`, rebuilds Router context and reads every archived source through `read_source`. Each restored complete message row must equal its original database row. The final evaluator checks that a real archive and rebuilt capsule exist, rereads source hashes and requires this Quest's integrity-bound original user message among the verified sources. A no-op archive or invented source cannot pass. Existing driver/evaluator tests explicitly exercise these negative cases; they are test fixtures, not substitute live evidence.

`ContextService.compact_router` and `rebuild_router` at `backend/src/forge_core/context_service.py:328` and line 426 preserve source rows, verify archive/source integrity, update the cursor transactionally and refresh active task/constraint context. Worker context compaction is a separate path from the stopped-Core Router compaction experiment.

## Actual frozen-v8 live observations

The three retained records are `.local/phase2/runs/20261115T020604Z-L1-dceb58/run.json`, `20261115T020604Z-L2-7f6370/run.json` and `20261115T020604Z-L3-30acf0/run.json`. All three failed acceptance. No downstream Worker started in L2 or L3, and no required Core restart/stopped-Core Router compaction was reached.

No Core restart/Router compaction observation. |
| L2, 99.597 seconds | `worker.blocked` seq 61, `tool_budget`, on first `research-router-worker` node after independent `NEEDS_REVISION` | 11/16 steps, 15/16 tools, 83,018/110,000 Worker tokens, 1 repair | Four actual Worker archives, containing 9, 6, 6 and 4 source messages; task still failed. No successor or Core restart. |

### L2: actual revision loop, not a predecessor failure

The initial research node successfully read the manifest and Router/Worker excerpts and wrote `work/l2-router-worker.json` (10,521 bytes). Independent review requested factual/citation corrections and a more compact artifact consistent with the approved objective. After that review the Worker repeatedly reread its artifact and the two original excerpts, with one additional manifest read. It never called `file_revise` and emitted no revised delivery. The tool-budget guard at `backend/src/forge_core/worker_runtime.py:2267` rejects a response when its requested tool batch exceeds the remaining allowance; the exact rejected batch is not persisted, so this audit does not assign it an invented count.

Every later node remained `proposed`. The live evidence therefore cannot establish whether a successor would receive or use predecessor evidence. It also does not establish the cause of the repeated-read behavior merely from the existence of Worker archives.

### L3: approved deliverable/tool mismatch

The model-generated approved research node explicitly says to write `work/l3-research.json` and has `json_review:work/l3-research.json` plus that expected artifact. Its approved node tools are only `file_read` and `directory_list`. Six successful calls consist of manifest/excerpt reads and directory listings; the workspace `work/` directory contains no output file. Fresh read-only packet construction fails at actual artifact readback, before packet/context reservation is evaluated. This failure is not attributed to Reviewer context size or budget.

The unexecuted mathematics and architecture nodes also require writing intermediate JSON while their node tools contain only `file_read` and `worker_read_action_receipt`. The unexecuted review node asks to record `work/l3-review.json` without a writing tool. These are retained plan/tool-contract inconsistencies; this audit makes no change to them.

### Usage accounting remains incomplete where the records say so

L1 and L2 each retain one unresolved `router_notice` model-budget attempt when the driver stopped the blocked frontier. Their charged sums are respectively 128,890 input / 14,443 output and 109,862 input / 9,567 output, with `unknown_attempts=1` in each record. The unresolved reservations are L1 10,555 input + 4,096 output and L2 10,290 input + 4,096 output. These are reservations, not actual charged usage. Scenario total-token/accounted-usage checks correctly remain unknown; settled sums cannot prove total actual usage or cost. L3 retains 84,067 input / 12,506 output and zero unknown attempts.

# Retained intermediate context-capacity regression

The first v9 local focused run added an approximately 850-byte current-budget
message to every Worker request. Six legacy archived-context cases then failed
at `context_budget`; the original approved allowance could no longer fit its
task/tool context. An isolated `-x` reproduction failed
`test_worker_reads_only_archived_own_context_and_charges_tool[arguments0-review_pending-False]`
after 27 passing cases in 15.50 seconds. This was a local scripted-model test,
not a live Provider result.

The larger pre-fix groups were interrupted after the six failures when subsequent
event-barrier tests waited for the model request that the exhausted context had
prevented. Those interrupted groups did not produce a completed JUnit result and
are not counted as passes. Their tool outputs remain in the chat history.

The correction omits the additional budget hint when the effective per-request
allowance is below 8192. It preserves the original task/tool context and original
admission checks. Larger native requests still receive the hint, whose complete
serialized bytes participate in input admission.

The unchanged legacy Worker file then passed 48 cases in 15.81 seconds:
`budget-feedback-legacy-v9.xml`. Planner/publication tests passed 36 cases in
3.64 seconds: `planner-publication-final-v9.xml`. The frozen-source full suite
and live results are recorded separately; these focused results do not certify
them.

tools.name: exec

tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.
tools.name: wait

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.

        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

tools.description:
Control native apps or browsers on the user’s computer by reading or operating UI. Prefer purpose-built skills, connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available.

On the first invocation of `cua_repl`, or after resetting it, execute exactly one of the API calls shown below, optionally assigning its result to a variable. Do not add other API calls, waits, or snapshots to that invocation.
The tool result will include documentation and, when creating or selecting a tab or selecting an app, its initial UI state. Selecting a browser does not open a tab. Read that result before continuing.
Use only APIs described in the tool instructions or returned documentation.

When you need an inventory of available apps, browsers, and tabs, get a snapshot of all enabled surfaces. Otherwise, use the relevant entry point below:

```javascript
await cua.getState();
```

Use the first matching browser control option from the user's request:

For a tab @-mention (`mention=tab-v1`):
Pass the complete `plugin://...` URL to get the referenced tab.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ mention: tabMentionUrl });
```

For an existing tab identified by URL in browser context (including the current IAB tab):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ url }, { browser: browserId });
```

Known tab ID (`tabId` or `providerTabId`) and browser (name or browser @-mention):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: browserId });
```

To open a URL in the in-app browser (`@Browser`):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab("iab", url, { visible: boolean });
```

To open a URL in another named browser: pass its name directly; do not call `getBrowser` first.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab(browserName, url, browserOptions);
```

Known URL, only when the user has not specified a browser by name or @-mention:

```javascript
let browser = await cua.getBrowser({ url });
```

Browser IDs and options:

- `"mcpapps"`: use `cua.getBrowser({ id: "mcpapps" })` for existing full-screen MCP Apps in the task’s side panel.
- `"iab"` (in-app browser): in `createBrowserTab`, use `visible: true` to show the browser; `false` to keep it hidden.
- `"dot"` (Dot): use only when present in browser inventory. It accesses tabs on Dot's active main thread. `cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: "dot" })` selects an existing tab. `cua.createBrowserTab("dot", url, { visible: boolean })` creates one with the same visibility options as `"iab"`.
- `"chrome"` (@Chrome), `"edge"` (@Edge): pass a short, emoji-prefixed `sessionName` (e.g. `"🔎 Task"`) to `createBrowserTab` when starting a task.

On Windows, choose the requested window by app and title from the inventory. Pass the selected window's ID as returned.

```javascript
let app = await cua.getApp({ windowId: selected.id });
```

To add other content to the tool result, use `nodeRepl.write(value)` for text or other values and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(image)` for images. The APIs listed above already display their documentation or UI state; do not wrap their results in `write` or `emitImage`.

If your context begins with a summary of an existing computer use task, call `await cua.rewriteDocumentation()` before continuing the computer use task to ensure you have a complete view of the necessary documentation.

Several `cua_repl.js` calls may work toward the same goal. As soon as you observe the final outcome of the CUA part of the task, make your next tool call `cua_repl.js` with only `completion_summary`, exactly once. Do this before using another tool for the next part of the user’s request or sending your reply, even if the overall request continues. If you hand control to the user, wait to summarize until the handoff has ended and you’ve observed the final outcome of the CUA part of the task. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images, videos, and audio using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When an app or connector generates or edits media, prefer native media already displayed inline or a local output file already returned by the tool. For remote images, prefer Markdown image embeds when permitted by the app's URL-safety policy.
- When presenting media that cannot be displayed directly, including remote video and audio, use the app's preview or display tool when available. Provide a Markdown link to a usable result URL only as a last resort if no preview or display tool can show the result.
- Do not download remote media to bypass the app's restrictions on presenting it to the user.
- When sending or referencing a local image, video, or audio file, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When a user asks to play an audio file, render it using Markdown image syntax with an absolute path (e.g., ![audio](/absolute/path.mp3)).
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Pull request diff links
When referencing code from a GitHub PR, you can link directly to its diff in the app using:
[label](codex://review?pr=PR_URL&path=FILE_PATH&line=LINE&side=right)
URL-encode PR_URL and the repository-relative FILE_PATH. Use a verified one-based LINE from the current PR diff. Use side=left for the original code or side=right for the updated code. Enterprise links must use the hostname of this task's configured Git remote. Use ordinary file links for workspace code.

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, use the MCP server's `load_workspace_dependencies` tool (`mcp__codex_app__load_workspace_dependencies`) to find the bundled runtime and libraries.

### Automations
- When you write or rewrite an automation prompt, keep it within 10,000 estimated tokens.
- When the user asks to manage an app automation, set a reminder, or schedule a recurring task, use the relevant Automations action to help the user. Do not write raw automation directives by hand.
- Create an automation when the user wants a reminder, a recurring report, or a standing alert for future events.
- Do not create an automation to track a specific job or task through a milestone, failure, or completion. If the user asks you to watch a run or task to completion, keep checking in the current task and follow through when the requested condition is met.
- Unless the user asks for periodic updates, notify them only on a meaningful change, completion, failure, or required user action.
- When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.
- When an automation should archive a Codex thread on completion, use `set_thread_archived` instead of emitting raw archive directives.

### Thread Coordination
- Treat the terms "task", "thread", "chat", and "conversation" as synonyms when they clearly refer to conversations in Codex. Use "chat" when referring to conversations in the product. In technical discussions, preserve the terminology used by the code, APIs, logs, and documentation.
- When the user asks to create, fork, inspect, continue, hand off, pin, archive, unarchive, permanently delete, rename, or otherwise manage Codex threads, search for the relevant thread tool first: `create_thread`, `fork_thread`, `list_threads`, `list_archived_threads`, `read_thread`, `wait_threads`, `send_message_to_thread`, `handoff_thread`, `set_thread_pinned`, `set_thread_archived`, `delete_thread`, or `set_thread_title`.
- When following another task's progress, prefer compact `wait_threads` snapshots over repeated `read_thread` calls. Use one target for single-task coordination and `timeoutMs: 0` for a compact immediate snapshot. `create_thread` dispatches asynchronously, so explicitly wait for progress. Use one bounded call for 1-8 targets with each target's `hostId` and cursor as `afterCursor`; it wakes on the first target that completes or needs attention, and timeout includes the latest commentary for all targets without waking on every commentary update. An up-to-date cursor suppresses already-delivered final text. Separate waits from one task may run serially. Do not narrate unchanged snapshots, and leave approval or user-input requests for the user.
- Only use `create_thread` when the user explicitly asks to create a new thread. Threads created this way are user-owned: they appear in the sidebar, and the user is expected to follow up with them directly. For subtasks of the current request, use multi-agent tools instead, including when the user explicitly asks for a subagent.
- After a successful `create_thread` call, emit `::created-thread{threadId="..."}` for a created thread or `::created-thread{clientThreadId="..."}` for queued worktree setup on its own line in your final response.

### Inline Code Comments
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive when you need to attach feedback directly to specific code lines.
- Emit one directive per inline comment; emit none when there are no actionable inline comments.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3).
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.
</app-context>

# FORGE — Agent Intelligence Sprint
## Phase 2: From Agent Infrastructure to Autonomous Intelligence

你现在正式进入 FORGE 的下一阶段开发。

本轮不以桌面端发布为目标，而是以真正跑通自主多智能体系统为目标。

用户已经授权你使用本地配置的 Provider。你可以使用现有 Provider 进行真实模型调用、协议测试、Agent 实验和端到端任务验证。

本轮必须把重心从基础设施转移到 Agent Intelligence。

不要继续大规模开发 UI，不要优先处理安装包和 Tauri 外观问题。

核心任务是让 FORGE 真正成为一个能够长期自主工作的 Agent 系统。

---

# 一、首先重新审计当前代码

当前开发分支：

`codex/phase1-continuous`

先读取：

- docs/STATUS.md
- docs/ROADMAP.md
- docs/QUALITY_GATES.md
- docs/PRODUCT_ARCHITECTURE.md
- docs/ROUTER_AND_WORKER_PROTOCOL.md
- docs/MODEL_REGISTRY_AND_TEAM_COMPOSITION.md
- docs/CONTEXT_MEMORY_GOVERNANCE.md
- 所有 Phase 1 Milestone 报告

重点阅读源码：

- forge_core/router.py
- forge_core/worker_runtime.py
- forge_core/team_composition.py
- forge_core/quest_graph.py
- forge_core/dispatcher.py
- forge_core/context_service.py
- forge_core/memory.py
- forge_core/providers/
- forge_core/tool_engine.py
- forge_core/evidence.py
- forge_core/governance.py

先建立一份真正的 Agent 执行链路图。

区分：
1. 已经真实实现的功能。
2. 通过 Mock 验证的功能。
3. 已经通过真实 Provider 验证的功能。
4. 只有接口或数据模型的功能。
5. 目前无法端到端工作的功能。

不要重新实现已经完成的模块。

不要为了让报告好看而隐藏已有缺陷。

审计完成后直接进入开发，不需要等待用户再次批准。

# 二、本地 Provider：正式启用真实模型

用户已经允许使用本地 Provider。

要求：

1. 检查 FORGE 当前 Provider 配置。
2. 检查本地 Provider 服务是否可用。
3. 获取可用模型列表。
4. 检查模型的 Tool Calling、Structured Output、Streaming 能力。
5. 检查模型实际上下文和输出限制。
6. 检查 Token 预算和并发限制。
7. 运行真实模型的最小对话测试。
8. 运行真实模型的 Router 决策测试。
9. 运行真实 Worker 工具调用测试。

如果本地 Provider 是 OpenAI-compatible 服务，优先使用现有 Adapter。

不要新建一套绕过 Gateway 的 Provider 实现。

安全要求：

- 不要打印 API Key。
- 不要把凭据写入源码、日志、Git 或实验报告。
- 不要读取与 FORGE Provider 配置无关的个人文件。
- 不要修改用户原有 Provider 服务配置。
- 不要自动增加无限 Token 预算。
- 不要将 Mock 响应标记为真实模型结果。

如果某个模型不支持 Tool Calling，应该由 Router 选择兼容模型或采用安全的结构化调用适配方案，不要假设所有模型都具备相同能力。

本地 Provider 可能是代理服务，必须区分：
- FORGE 到本地代理的请求成功。
- 上游真实模型调用成功。
- 模型实际返回正确结果。

三者不能混为一谈。

# 三、核心任务：升级 Persistent Router

当前 Router 已经具备模型驱动决策基础，但还需要进一步增强。

目标：

Router 不应该只是一个分类器，而应该成为一个长期存在的自主 Agent。

## 3.1 Router Agent Loop

实现完整的循环：

Observe
→ Understand
→ Retrieve
→ Reason
→ Decide
→ Act
→ Observe Result
→ Reflect
→ Continue

Router 必须具备：

- 持续理解用户目标。
- 自动关联历史 Quest。
- 判断是否创建新 Quest。
- 判断是否继续现有 Quest。
- 识别用户约束。
- 识别任务优先级。
- 识别阻塞条件。
- 根据执行结果调整计划。
- 主动决定何时请求用户帮助。
- 在适当时机主动汇报进展。

不要把所有推理都写成固定 Prompt。

需要建立结构化决策协议，并对模型输出进行严格校验。

## 3.2 Router 与 Planner 分离

Router 负责：
- 用户意图理解。
- 任务生命周期管理。
- Quest 选择。
- 团队协调。
- 结果汇总。
- 用户交互。

Planner 负责：
- 目标分析。
- 子任务拆解。
- DAG 生成。
- 依赖关系推导。
- 成功标准定义。
- 任务执行顺序优化。

Planner 可以作为后台专用 Agent，但不能取代 Router。

## 3.3 复杂任务识别

支持：
- 普通聊天。
- 单步骤执行。
- 多步骤任务。
- 长期研究任务。
- 软件开发任务。
- 多模态任务。
- 多 Quest 并行任务。

不要为了增加 Agent 数量而把简单问题拆成复杂任务。

简单任务应该直接回答。

复杂任务才启动团队。

---

# 四、Dynamic Team Intelligence

这是 FORGE 最重要的创新方向之一。

目前已经具备模型注册、角色合同和基础组队算法。

接下来需要让团队真正根据任务需求动态形成。

## 4.1 Model Intelligence

完善模型画像：

- Coding
- Mathematics
- Research
- Architecture
- Planning
- Design
- Vision
- Writing
- Tool Calling
- Instruction Following

增加实际线上表现：

- Task Success Rate
- Tool Call Success Rate
- Retry Rate
- Schema Compliance
- Average Latency
- P95 Latency
- Token Consumption
- Cost
- Review Pass Rate

注意：

能力评分必须有来源、样本数、测试时间和置信度。

真实数据与用户手动评分分开保存。

不能把一次成功调用直接当成模型能力评分。

## 4.2 Dynamic Team Composer

Router 将 Quest 交给 Composer。

Composer 根据：

- Task Requirements
- Model Capabilities
- Model Reliability
- Tool Compatibility
- Token Budget
- Time Budget
- Coordination Overhead

选择团队。

支持：

- Single Agent
- Sequential Team
- Parallel Team
- Hierarchical Team
- Specialist Team
- Dynamic Expansion

要求模型与角色彻底解耦。

一个模型可以承担多个角色，一个角色也可以根据任务动态切换模型。

## 4.3 团队自适应

执行过程中：

- Worker 可以请求帮助。
- Router 可以增加专家。
- Router 可以替换表现不佳的模型。
- Router 可以重新分配未完成节点。
- Reviewer 可以要求返工。
- Planner 可以重新规划剩余 DAG。

但已完成节点、历史证据和已执行的外部动作不能因为重组而丢失。

团队规模、派生深度、预算和重试次数必须有界。

---

# 五、真正的 Native Worker Agent Loop

不要只把 Worker 当作任务执行函数。

Worker 必须拥有自己的推理循环和工作上下文。

完整过程：

接收任务
→ 理解任务合同
→ 检索必要上下文
→ 选择工具
→ 请求模型
→ 执行工具
→ 读取结果
→ 判断是否完成
→ 必要时修正
→ 输出结构化结果
→ 提交证据
→ 通知 Router

## 5.1 Worker 类型

完善以下角色：

Research Agent：
- 检索资料。
- 整理来源。
- 分析相关工作。
- 提供研究结论。

Math Agent：
- 数学推导。
- 公式验证。
- 数值计算。
- 检查推理漏洞。

Architect Agent：
- 设计系统架构。
- 定义接口。
- 分析依赖。
- 检查技术风险。

Coding Agent：
- 阅读代码。
- 编写代码。
- 修改代码。
- 运行测试。
- 修复错误。

Experiment Agent：
- 设计实验。
- 执行实验。
- 记录结果。
- 生成可复现报告。

Reviewer Agent：
- 检查成果。
- 对照成功标准。
- 检查证据。
- 给出通过或返工决定。

Planner Agent：
- 拆解任务。
- 更新 DAG。
- 管理依赖。
- 处理失败后的重新规划。

## 5.2 Worker 自我修正

Worker 不能遇到错误就直接失败。

应该能够：

1. 读取错误信息。
2. 判断错误类型。
3. 分析可能原因。
4. 选择修复策略。
5. 再次执行。
6. 对比修复前后的结果。
7. 判断是否需要求助。

区分：
- 代码错误。
- 工具错误。
- Provider 错误。
- 任务理解错误。
- 预算耗尽。
- 依赖阻塞。
- 外部资源不可用。

不同错误采用不同恢复策略。

禁止无限循环。

## 5.3 Worker 交付协议

每个 Worker 必须提交：

- Summary
- Findings
- Decisions
- Artifacts
- Evidence References
- Unresolved Issues
- Confidence
- Next Actions

不能只返回一段自由文本。

---

# 六、Reviewer：建立真正的独立审查机制

Reviewer 不应该只是让另一个模型重新总结一次结果。

它必须检查：

1. 是否完成原始目标。
2. 是否满足成功标准。
3. 是否存在未经验证的假设。
4. 产物是否真实存在。
5. 产物是否与执行记录对应。
6. 测试是否真实运行。
7. 是否存在逻辑错误。
8. 是否存在明显遗漏。
9. 是否存在安全问题。

Reviewer 应当拥有独立的上下文。

不要将 Coding Agent 的全部内部推理直接复制给 Reviewer。

Reviewer 应获得：
- 原始任务合同。
- 成功标准。
- 实际产物。
- 可信工具回执。
- 必要的研究来源。
- 测试结果。

审查结果：

PASS
NEEDS_REVISION
REJECT
BLOCKED

NEEDS_REVISION 必须能够创建有明确修改目标的返工任务。

设置最大审查轮次。

Reviewer 不能通过模型自述或 Mock 证据判定成功。

---

# 七、Context Compaction 与 Memory 深度增强

目前 M6 已经实现了有界 Context Archive、Recall 和预算管理。

但长期单一对话仍然有容量边界。

本轮重点解决这个问题。

## 7.1 Task-Centric Compaction

不要简单按时间截断历史。

采用多层上下文：

L0：Recent Interaction
L1：Active Quest Context
L2：Project Memory
L3：Long-term Experience

保留：
- 原始用户目标。
- 用户明确约束。
- 重要决策。
- 已完成节点。
- 当前阻塞。
- 产物路径。
- 证据来源。
- 失败经验。
- 后续行动。

每个压缩摘要必须保留来源引用。

压缩后必须能恢复到原始证据。

## 7.2 解决历史消息无限增长

不要为了保存所有用户约束而无限注入原始消息。

建立约束抽取和引用机制：

- 将用户约束单独索引。
- 保留原始消息 ID。
- 生成有来源的结构化 Constraint Record。
- 检测约束冲突。
- 检测约束是否过期。
- 必要时重新读取原始消息。

模型抽取出的约束先标记为待验证。

用户明确确认的约束与模型推测严格区分。

## 7.3 Memory Retrieval

改进 Recall：

- 语义检索。
- 关键词检索。
- Quest 关联检索。
- 时间检索。
- 来源可靠性过滤。
- 冲突检测。
- 过期过滤。

建立 Retrieval Evaluation Dataset。

测试 Router 是否能准确找到历史 Quest、决策、文件和用户约束。

不要只根据摘要文本相似度判断召回成功。

---

# 八、Agent 之间的协作机制

建立正式的 Agent Communication Protocol。

不允许把自由文本群聊作为主要协调机制。

支持：

TASK_ASSIGNMENT
TASK_ACCEPTED
TASK_COMPLETED
HELP_REQUEST
REVIEW_REQUEST
REVISION_REQUEST
DEPENDENCY_BLOCKED
MODEL_UNAVAILABLE
BUDGET_WARNING
AGENT_FAILED

重要消息持久化。

Router 负责协调。

Worker 不能绕过 Router 自行修改其他 Worker 的任务。

对于跨 Worker 共享的产物，必须通过有权限的 Artifact 和 Receipt 接口访问。

---

# 九、真正跑通复杂任务

本轮必须新增真实端到端实验。

不要只写单元测试。

建立三种任务难度：

## Level 1：简单任务

例如：

“分析这个 Python 项目，指出三个最值得优先修复的问题。”

验证：
- Router 判断。
- Quest 创建。
- 单 Worker 执行。
- 结果回传。

## Level 2：多 Agent 协作

例如：

“调研一个开源 Agent 框架，比较其架构，写一份技术分析报告。”

验证：
- Research Agent。
- Architect Agent。
- Coding/Writer Agent。
- Reviewer Agent。
- Router 汇总。

## Level 3：复杂自主开发

例如：

“研究一个新的 Agent 算法，提出技术方案，实现实验代码，运行实验，并分析结果。”

验证：
- Planner。
- Research Agent。
- Math Agent。
- Architect Agent。
- Coding Agent。
- Experiment Agent。
- Reviewer Agent。

复杂任务必须真实调用 Provider、真实执行工具、真实产生文件。

必须能在中途重启 Core 后继续执行。

## 实验数据

每次实验保存：

- Run ID
- Provider
- Model ID
- Execution Mode
- Model Calls
- Tool Calls
- Token Usage
- Duration
- Retry Count
- Review Results
- Artifact Hashes
- Final Status

真实模型实验与 Mock 实验分开统计。

失败实验必须保留。

---

# 十、算法研究：不要只做工程拼装

FORGE 有三个值得深入的自主研究方向：

1. Capability-Aware Dynamic Team Composition。
2. Evidence-Driven Autonomous Governance。
3. Task-Centric Context Compression。

本轮建立真正可复现的 Benchmark。

重点：

### Team Composition
比较：
- Single Model
- Static Team
- Greedy Selection
- Capability Coverage
- Complementarity
- Dynamic Recomposition

### Context Compression
比较：
- Full Context
- Recency Truncation
- Conventional Summary
- Task-Centric Compression
- Task-Centric Compression + Source Recall

### Agent Governance
比较：
- Model Claim Only
- Tool Receipt Verification
- Independent Reviewer
- Evidence-Gated Completion

至少建立多个不同难度和领域的任务。

使用固定测试集、统一预算和独立评分。

报告成功率、成本、延迟、Token、返工次数和证据完整率。

小样本结果必须明确标记为探索性实验，不允许夸大统计结论。

---

# 十一、本轮明确不做的事情

暂时不投入主要开发资源于：

- UI 视觉重构。
- Tauri 安装包优化。
- NSIS 发布。
- 动画效果。
- 桌面端页面扩展。
- 非必要的数据库重构。

现有桌面端保持可用即可。

如果发现会阻塞 Agent 运行的底层缺陷，可以修复，但不要将桌面测试变成主线。

---

# 十二、执行顺序

请连续执行以下阶段，不需要每个阶段都等待用户确认：

Sprint A：Provider 和 Agent Loop 深度审计及真实调用。

Sprint B：Persistent Router + Planner 智能化。

Sprint C：Dynamic Team Intelligence。

Sprint D：Native Worker 自主执行与自我修正。

Sprint E：Independent Reviewer 与返工闭环。

Sprint F：Context Compaction + Long-term Memory。

Sprint G：Agent Communication Protocol + 故障恢复。

Sprint H：真实复杂任务端到端验收。

Sprint I：三项核心算法 Benchmark 与消融实验。

每个阶段必须有独立测试和可复现报告。

如果发现现有架构不支持目标，应先提出最小必要架构调整，并通过 ADR 记录，不要推倒重写。

---

# 十三、工程约束

1. 保持一个长期用户对话入口。
2. Router 是唯一面向用户的 Agent。
3. Worker 是真正的后台执行 Agent。
4. 不允许通过创建多个用户 Conversation 规避上下文问题。
5. 不允许把 Codex、DSH 或 Claude Code 当作执行后端。
6. 不允许使用伪造的执行记录。
7. 不允许把 Mock 结果标记为 Live。
8. 不允许绕过 Approval、Policy 和 Evidence。
9. 不允许无限 Agent 派生。
10. 不允许无限重试。
11. 不允许无预算模型调用。
12. 保留历史测试和审计证据。
13. 不自动推送或合并 GitHub。
14. 不删除用户原有数据和实验记录。

可以使用多个 Codex 子任务并行分析和实现，但必须指定唯一集成负责人，避免多人同时修改相同核心文件。

---

# 十四、最终交付标准

最终必须让 FORGE 能够：

1. 长期与用户保持同一个对话。
2. 理解用户复杂目标。
3. 自动生成 Quest。
4. 自动规划 DAG。
5. 从模型库选择模型。
6. 动态组建 Agent 团队。
7. 后台并行执行任务。
8. Agent 之间结构化协作。
9. 自动发现错误并修复。
10. Reviewer 独立检查结果。
11. 不合格任务自动返工。
12. 上下文压缩后恢复工作。
13. 长期记忆跨任务复用。
14. Core 重启后继续执行。
15. 所有成果具备可信证据。

生成：

`docs/PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md`

`docs/PHASE2_STATUS.md`

`docs/PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md`

`docs/audit/phase2/verification.json`

最终报告必须明确区分真实模型验证、Mock 验证、合成实验和未完成项目。

现在开始执行。

本轮的成功标准不是增加了多少代码，而是 FORGE 是否真正能够自主完成一个复杂任务，并且在失败、返工、上下文压缩和 Core 重启后仍然保持任务连续性。要多开子代理并行，本地provider直接用本地workbuddy-api 的wb-in里面的deepseek-v4.1-flash

# FORGE v4 — Persistent Router Agent System

FORGE is a self-built, general-purpose autonomous Agent desktop application.

## Engineering status — 2026-11-15

Phase 2 Agent Intelligence is in progress. The existing native runtime now connects a separate Planner, source-bound constraints and bounded memory, observation-informed team proposals, fresh-context independent review and typed durable Agent coordination. One retained strict L1 live run passed with review revision and Worker self-repair, without compaction or restart; the concurrent L2 and later L3 attempts failed. Later L2/L3 reruns also failed before review at packet/context and cumulative-budget limits. The [v5 full backend suite](docs/audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v5.xml) passed 820 tests with one warning in 219.96 seconds, before later v6 changes. The [v6 full suite](docs/audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v6.xml) retained 848 passed, one failed, one warning / 283.77 seconds; all three v6 live reruns failed. V7 corrects independent Worker/Gateway concurrency and extends bounded handoff/budget guidance. The [v7 full suite](docs/audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v7.xml) passed 849 tests / one warning / 216.87 seconds, while all three v7 live attempts failed. The [v8 full suite](docs/audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v8.xml) passed 886 tests / one warning / 283.46 seconds; all three v8 live attempts failed, despite real review/revision and Worker archiving in L1/L2. L1/L2 each retain an unresolved Router-notice attempt and no mid-execution Core restart occurred. V9 generated-plan/tool-budget corrections await new full/live results; complex-task continuity and final verification remain pending. The local Provider's small live protocol probes passed [11/11 with the proxy default](docs/audit/phase2/provider-probe.json) and [10/11 with explicit `reasoning_effort=none`](docs/audit/phase2/provider-probe-reasoning-none.json); the latter retained a failed exact-text dialogue check. Focused local/Mock suites and exploratory synthetic benchmarks are recorded separately. See the [Phase 2 report](docs/PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md), [status](docs/PHASE2_STATUS.md), [experiments](docs/PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md) and [architecture decision](docs/adr/ADR-009-agent-intelligence-contracts-and-review.md).

Phase 1 Milestones 1–6 provide the persistence, governance, Registry, DAG, native Workers, tool/evidence and context/budget foundation. Historical M6 verification passed 372 tests; one bounded live continuation succeeded after five retained diagnostic failures. The [M7 backend hardening round](docs/PHASE1_MILESTONE7_BACKEND_HARDENING.md) passed 488 local tests. Desktop Alpha, final native integration and packaging are deferred; these historical backend results do not establish a desktop release.

See [current status](docs/STATUS.md), the [Phase 0 audit report](docs/PHASE0_AUDIT.md), and the report's dependency-ordered development plan. The release references `codex/MASTER_PROMPT.md`, but that file is missing from the supplied archive.

**The user has one persistent conversation.** A persistent Router Agent owns that conversation and coordinates multiple long-running Quests and hidden Worker Sessions. Workers have isolated execution contexts, but they are never presented as separate user conversations.

## Product invariants

1. One persistent user-facing conversation per workspace.
2. One persistent Router identity and resumable state per workspace.
3. Multiple durable Quests can run behind that conversation.
4. Worker Sessions are private execution contexts, not user-facing chats.
5. Worker events are selectively relayed into the single conversation timeline.
6. Model Provider, Model Profile, Role Template, Agent Instance, Quest and Session are separate domain entities.
7. Model Registry uses provider metadata, FORGE benchmark results, online performance and explicit user overrides.
8. Team composition combines reusable role templates with bounded dynamic role synthesis.
9. FORGE owns its Agent Loop, Router, Worker Runtime, Tool Engine, Memory, Governance and Evidence.
10. Codex, DSH and Claude Code are architectural references only, never execution backends.

## What this release contains

- Typed Python domain layer and repository interfaces.
- SQLite persistence with schema versioning and transaction boundaries.
- Persistent `main` conversation and Router identity.
- Quest lifecycle state machine and hidden Worker Session records.
- Durable event log with sequence cursor.
- Model Registry and explainable capability-fit team composition baseline.
- Provider gateway and explicit unconfigured provider; Mock protocol tests are labelled.
- FastAPI API with input validation and consistent error handling.
- React single-conversation UI with background Quest panel.
- Automated tests for persistence, lifecycle, router classification and team composition.
- Architecture, threat model, ADRs, detailed roadmap and Codex execution prompts.

## Important maturity statement

This is an engineering foundation with bounded context recovery, sourced lexical recall and evidence-gated execution. The Router uses a configured Provider or explicitly fails. Mock tests, synthetic experiments and real-provider observations are identified separately. The current independent reviewer uses the approved Worker's model in a fresh context. General autonomous replanning, learned semantic retrieval, arbitrary-scale continuity and complex-task correctness remain open. Plan/team/replacement approval stays authenticated and Review mode remains enabled. A proposal record alone never proves execution.

## Backend setup

The model-driven Router requires explicit provider configuration. Set the process environment
variables `FORGE_PROVIDER_ID`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_KIND` (for example `openai_compatible`),
`FORGE_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REF` (for example
`FORGE_PROVIDER_KEY_EXAMPLE`), `FORGE_ROUTER_MODEL_ID`, and
`FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` (an operator-supplied maximum context window). Put the actual
credential only in the process environment variable named by the credential reference. Set
`FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_TOOLS=true` and `FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_JSON_SCHEMA=true` only when
the provider supports them. Without configuration the Core starts but Router message calls fail
explicitly; no keyword or mock provider is selected automatically. The optional `request_id`
in a message request allows safe retry: reuse it only for the same input.
For live calls, register an enabled model with the same provider and model ID and explicitly set
both `tool_calling_support` and `structured_output_support` to supported. Unknown capabilities
are rejected. Values submitted through the model API are recorded as user overrides.

Provider timing, Worker ownership and review/output limits use the process environment:

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Per-attempt timeout in seconds; finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `30`. A timeout does not prove the upstream operation stopped. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_MAX_RETRIES` | Additional Gateway retries, integer `0`–`3`; defaults to `1`. Each HTTP attempt requires its own budget admission. |
| `FORGE_WORKER_LEASE_SECONDS` | Worker ownership lease, finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `60`. Valid current owners renew between steps, capped by the task deadline. The local call wait is bounded by the current lease; an upstream operation may remain unresolved after that wait ends. |
| `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` | Maximum review rounds; integer `1`–`4`, defaults to `2`. The live acceptance harness explicitly selects `3`, matching its scenario cap. This does not reset budgets or change historical runs. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_REASONING_EFFORT` | Optional explicit OpenAI-compatible/DeepSeek request setting: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`. Unset sends no setting. Configure only for a model that advertises support; Anthropic configuration rejects it. |
| `FORGE_ROUTER_OUTPUT_RESERVE` | Router response-token ceiling and reserved output allowance; integer `1`–`8192`, defaults to `2048`. `FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` must be greater than this value. A registered model's known output limit must also support it. |
| `FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` | Operator-supplied Router context ceiling, required when setting a Router model. Core startup requires an integer greater than `2048` and greater than the configured output reserve. |

The Phase 2 live acceptance harness uses a 120-second timeout, a 150-second Worker lease and zero additional
Gateway retries, with a Router output reserve of `4096` and `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS=3`
within the scenario's three-round cap. Router/Planner schema repair remains a separately bounded stage;
neither setting authorizes replay of an unresolved external action.

The current WorkBuddy acceptance harness explicitly requests `reasoning_effort=none`,
which the local proxy implementation advertises for the requested model. This is
an operator setting, not independent proof of the upstream model's internal behavior.
Earlier diagnostic runs used the proxy default and retain their separate results.

The Router reads a bounded snapshot and calls the provider outside the database write
transaction. A successful decision and its messages commit together; provider errors, invalid
decisions, or budget failures leave no messages or Quest changes for that turn. The caller can
retry with the same request ID. The context budget uses a conservative UTF-8 byte estimate,
reserves output and request overhead, and also respects a known registry context window. Tool
access is limited to read-only Core queries. Worker execution separately requires approved plan/team contracts and governed tool permissions.
