The v8 live runs share code snapshot
`8480f4f9c4f88a28d3d41047e5b1dbf90f424f9cc7892d0302c13758433c40ff`.
L1 `20261115T020604Z-L1-dceb58` failed in 136.466 seconds, 23 model/14 tool calls,
charged input/output 128,890/14,443 tokens. L2 `20261115T020604Z-L2-7f6370` failed
in 99.597 seconds, 25 model/15 tool calls, charged 109,862/9,567 tokens. Each record
retains one unresolved Router-notice attempt at stop; its reservation is respectively
10,555+4,096 and 10,290+4,096, not actual charged usage. Total actual usage and cost
remain unknown. Both Workers received real NEEDS_REVISION, then repeatedly reread
files and hit the original tool budget without revised delivery. L1 has two actual
Worker archives (17/6 source messages); L2 has four (9/6/6/4). These observations
establish Worker archiving, without a completed task or stopped-Core Router
compaction/mid-execution restart. L3 `20261115T020604Z-L3-30acf0` failed in 103.132
seconds, 18 model/six tool calls, 84,067/12,506 tokens, unknown zero. Its approved
research node required a file artifact while allowing only read tools; the actual
file was absent and packet construction failed before Reviewer/context admission.
No successor ran in L2/L3. The
[independent continuity/live audit](continuity-and-live-diagnosis-v8.md)
does not infer a repeated-read cause from archives or claim a predecessor handoff
failure/success where no successor executed. All three strict acceptances failed.

V9 rejects a generated node with a concrete artifact verifier unless that same
node already permits `file_write`; feedback uses the original bounded Planner
schema-repair path and inserts no tool authority. Worker requests show remaining
model steps, tool calls and cumulative tokens, and point to integrity-bound archived
source_refs/current artifact receipts. This guides reuse of evidence without
assuming the repeated-read cause is proved. A tool batch exceeding remaining calls
is rejected before any tool executes and may use the existing bounded repair path;
the settled model attempt stays charged. Original tool/step/token/cost/time and
repair/round limits remain unchanged. Publisher adds numeric retry totals/breakdown
and allowlisted review reason/context fields; prompt/reply/log/artifact bodies stay
excluded, and missing historical fields remain unknown/null. New v9 full/live
outcomes and final complex continuity remain pending.

The [v8 benchmark](benchmark-final-v8.json) completed in 17.598702 seconds with
zero Provider calls on the unchanged fixed dataset; earlier limitations remain.

## Continuity and open boundaries

`ConstraintService` separates literal user clauses, pending model extracts and separately
confirmed records, with original IDs/hashes, potential conflicts, expiry and revocation.
Router/Worker highlights are bounded; omitted originals remain in archives and can be
re-read with source checks. L0 recent interaction, L1 Quest, L2 project/history and L3
failure-experience paths exist. Active Quest counts, indexing batches, candidate pages,
artifact/receipt snapshots and model windows remain finite; learned semantic retrieval,
general source relevance and arbitrary-scale continuity are not established.

Recovery uses durable Worker/model/tool state and lease generations. Unknown remote
outcomes retain reservations until trusted recovery conditions permit action. The current
Worker renews only between settled steps while its token/generation, approved contract
and running Quest remain valid, capped by the task deadline. Expired/stale ownership
cannot be revived and no individual call exceeds its current lease/deadline. The live
driver supports storage compaction/readback, a plan-boundary restart and a restart after
partial node completion. Actual observed snapshots and successful continuation remain
required; a supported option or plan-boundary restart alone does not prove recovery
from an arbitrary in-flight external action.
The independent driver's five offline tests verify missing DB handling, actual budget
inspection, genuine archive/readback, no-op truthfulness and visible integrity failure.
Desktop packaging/UI acceptance is deferred; no new desktop-release claim follows.
New driver snapshots and the Publisher retain only whitelisted runtime settings:
reasoning effort, review-round limit, Worker lease seconds, Provider timeout seconds,
retry limit and effective model token/concurrency limits. Missing legacy fields remain null and do not inherit later configuration.

The fixed tool contracts do not provide arbitrary shell, unrestricted Python,
arbitrary test commands or a general patch operation. `python_compile` proves
syntax only, `numeric_ast` executes a bounded pure numeric subset and
`shell_inspect` permits only `python_version`. `file_write` creates files with
exclusive-create semantics. Explicitly approved `file_revise` only replaces the
same Worker's own latest proven artifact, preserving immutable prior versions;
user files, predecessor artifacts, stale hashes and uncertain outcomes remain
excluded. Review and acceptance compare current bytes with the verified latest
receipt chain rather than treating a legitimate historical hash as current.
Team replacement keeps the approved DAG; Router goal updates
and new DAG proposals remain limited to proposed/awaiting-approval Quests, so
general running-DAG replanning is still absent. Source retrieval remains lexical.

# FORGE 项目状态

更新：2026-11-15（Asia/Shanghai）

## 当前状态

**Phase 2 Agent Intelligence 进行中；一次 strict L1 已通过，L2/L3 及复杂连续性验收尚未完成。** 本轮重点为现有后端的 Router/Planner、动态团队、Native Worker、独立审查返工、有来源的上下文与记忆、Agent 协调和真实端到端实验。进度见 [Phase 2 状态](PHASE2_STATUS.md)、[完整报告](PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md)和[实验记录](PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md)；最小架构调整见 [ADR 009](adr/ADR-009-agent-intelligence-contracts-and-review.md)。

当前已记录 B/F 局部合并 **53 passed / 18.36 秒**、驱动 **5 passed / 0.57 秒**、C/I **42 passed / 14.61 秒**、D/E/G **128 passed / 46.34 秒**、Provider/目标来源 **42 passed / 4.56 秒**；这些测试有重叠，不能相加作为完整套件数量。离线 v2 为小规模固定合成实验，零次 Provider 调用；[v4 重跑](audit/phase2/benchmark-final-v4.json)为 6.3642 秒、0 Provider 调用，固定机制指标未变。本地 workbuddy-api/wb-in 的 `deepseek-v4.1-flash` 经 Gateway 的历史 proxy-default 探针为 **11/11 小协议案例 / 26.712 秒**；显式 `reasoning_effort=none` 探针为 **10/11 / 20.210 秒**，精确文本对话检查失败保留。参数不证明上游内部 reasoning 行为，上游身份仍是代理自报。协议通过不能代替复杂任务验收。

保留的 L1 `20261115T012115Z-L1-2a34ad` 在 **103.621 秒**通过 strict 验收，发生一次审查返工与一次 Worker 自修，但没有压缩或重启。同快照 L2 `20261115T012115Z-L2-8e64f5` 在 **96.416 秒**失败：中间只读研究被要求交付下游报告，后续审查受 context limit 阻断，最终调用账本无未知项。L3 `20261115T012340Z-L3-17c603` 在 **447.913 秒**失败，有效七节点图后未组队或执行 Worker；缺少原始模型回复，不能断言缺失字段。

后续 L2 `20261115T013328Z-L2-fed968` 在 80.711 秒失败：16 次模型、6 次工具、54,597/9,558 输入/输出 token、未知 0，raw/native 为 68,294/68,550，超过 65,536；声明并发 3 也超过场景 cap 2。L3 `20261115T013328Z-L3-4e61d3` 在 151.834 秒失败，最终为合法 7 角色/并发 2；研究产物 15,776 字节，raw/native 67,009/68,224，Worker 已用 38,989/70,000、剩余 31,011 不足审查。两次均无 `review.started` 或重启。

v6 的三次新 live 也失败，最终未知调用均为 0：L1 `20261115T014735Z-L1-b48614` 122.096 秒，两轮 `NEEDS_REVISION` 加前序自修耗尽原 Worker `max_repairs`；L2 `20261115T014735Z-L2-cd59cb` 84.678 秒，14,060 字节只读 delivery 未受 v6 JSON-artifact 指导，raw/native 60,371/60,425，已用 18,143/78,000、剩 59,857，单审查输入已差 568；L3 `20261115T014735Z-L3-4ce51e` 165.77 秒，产物 11,651 字节、raw/native 65,637/66,278，已用 57,093/90,000、剩 32,907，27 次调用、123,506/22,569 输入/输出。L2/L3 无审查或重启；复杂连续性仍未完成。

[全量 v4](audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v4.xml)为 **781 passed、6 failed、1 warning / 290.98 秒**；六个旧 M4 Mock Planner fixture 使用不可执行 criteria。仅改为 `delivery_review` 后，[原断言回归](audit/phase2/planner-legacy-fixture-regressions.xml)为 **21 passed / 12.89 秒**，不代替最终全量。[v5 快照](audit/phase2/source-manifest-v5.json)含 153 文件，Ruff、150 个 Python 文件格式和 diff 检查通过；[v5 全量](audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v5.xml)及[日志](audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v5.log)为 **820 passed、1 warning / 219.96 秒**，manifest 哈希 `a1f4646cb9acc810f3d35e8f9609a99ed553efd1ce4c2b3a0906d98c0333ed93`。v5 早于后续 v6 改动，不覆盖新修复；[v6 全量](audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v6.xml)及[日志](audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v6.log)保留 **848 passed、1 failed、1 warning / 283.77 秒**。`test_m5_lifespan_execution` 的实际并行 DAG 测试失败：Core 将 Gateway 模型并发 1 与 Worker 并发 2 混同，误把 team operator cap 降为 1；v7 恢复 Worker 并发 2，独立于 Gateway 资源，不修改原测试。[v7 全量](audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v7.xml)及[日志](audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v7.log)为 **849 passed、1 warning / 216.87 秒**；[155 文件 manifest](audit/phase2/source-manifest-v7.json)哈希 `58339132008a97956237ec38c2eb19eb7062f46b4ef2f5f946567ad52be26627`，Ruff 与 152 个 Python 文件格式通过。该快照早于 v8，不能覆盖新严格交付修复。[v8 全量](audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v8.xml)及[日志](audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v8.log)为 **886 passed、1 warning / 283.46 秒**；[156 文件 manifest](audit/phase2/source-manifest-v8.json)为 `92bb6067ff7bc1dadfa6aa9b5994089969603b53b3980a9a5601d0a140e6b9e3`，Ruff/153 文件格式/pip 检查通过。后续 v9 改动仍待新全量/live。

v6 对新中间 JSON 分析/交接产物提供约 6 KiB 软指导，所有原要求、完整代码及最终报告仍须保留，不截断旧产物；Planner 指导在原总额内预留完整 context 审查/响应/修订累计预算。新团队/替换提案及审批校验 operator cap，v7 将 Worker cap 2 与 Gateway 模型调用并发分开；Composer/Worker 使用同一 Worker cap；harness 总 token/并发取 CLI 与场景较小值，并记录有效配置。[Composer 组](audit/phase2/composer-concurrency-20261115T094900.xml) **69 passed / 5.70 秒**、[Worker 指导组](audit/phase2/worker-report-guidance-tests.xml) **99 passed / 28.05 秒**均属本地/Mock，不代表 v6 全量或 live 通过。v7 把软指导扩展到有后继的 `delivery_review`，引用集中避免反复完整哈希，v7 曾建议中间角色 `output_tokens=2048`，v8 已取消该偏好以容纳完整 JSON，source-heavy 首节点在原总额允许时约两 context 累计预算并留至少 10% 协调余量；完整要求和全部硬限制保留。

v7 三次 live 全失败、最终未知均为 0：L1 `20261115T015415Z-L1-d9dedd` 98.792 秒、16 模型/4 工具、57,113/7,877 输入/输出，2048 输出截断耗尽 repair；L2 `20261115T015415Z-L2-b0e9f0` 93.078 秒、19/6、78,714/11,191，只规划两节点不满足 3–4 专业 Worker，14,141 字节产物又受 context limit 阻断；L3 `20261115T015415Z-L3-2732f0` 99.483 秒、24/9、127,932/11,268，真实审查 NEEDS_REVISION 后耗尽 max_steps=10，返工未完成。复杂连续性仍未证实。

v8 明确 Worker 当前节点范围，Planner 仅对整个任务均为简单只读时用单节点并保留明确专长/数量；Composer role ID 唯一且专长匹配，用户允许时建议 max_steps=16；native Core 将自修/审查返工共享 max_repairs 配为 4，原计数与步骤/token/工具/费用/时间/审查轮次仍约束。仅新 TeamWire 显式 null 选择 STRICT 八字段 schema，confidence 0–1，模型必须完整提供，Core 不填默认；历史/direct/显式旧 schema 保留。非有限 JSON 按原有界 repair 拒绝。[185 项合同组](audit/phase2/native-delivery-contract-20261115T151500.xml) 47.49 秒、[最新 36 项](audit/phase2/native-delivery-nonfinite-20261115T152200.xml) 5.97 秒均为有重叠的本地/Mock，v8 全量与 live 结果另录。

v8 三次 live 全失败：L1 `20261115T020604Z-L1-dceb58` 136.466 秒、23 模型/14 工具、已结算 128,890/14,443 输入/输出；L2 `20261115T020604Z-L2-7f6370` 99.597 秒、25/15、109,862/9,567。两次实际 NEEDS_REVISION 后反复 file_read 至原 tool budget 阻断，停机时各有 1 项未结算 Router notice，真实总用量/费用未知、保留 reservation。L1 有 2 个真实 Worker archive（17/6 来源），L2 有 4 个（9/6/6/4），但无 Core 中途重启/停机 Router 压缩。L3 `20261115T020604Z-L3-30acf0` 103.132 秒、18/6、84,067/12,506、未知 0；批准研究节点要求产物却仅允许读工具，真实文件不存在，未进入审查。无 L2/L3 后继执行，见[独立连续性诊断](audit/phase2/continuity-and-live-diagnosis-v8.md)。不能据此断言归档导致循环或前驱交接失败。

[v8 无损引用表示](audit/phase2/reviewer-lossless-v8-diagnostic.json)将确切历史 fixture 的 native input reserve 64,870 降至 64,346，省 524 字节，配 1,190 输出仍在原 65,536 内；原 packet/PASS/hash/raw cap 不变。[124 项](audit/phase2/reviewer-lossless-v8-tests.xml) / 60.43 秒为离线构造，不是 live 成功。[Benchmark v8](audit/phase2/benchmark-final-v8.json)为固定离线 17.598702 秒/0 Provider 调用。

v9 对生成 DAG 的具体产物 verifier 强制同节点已有 file_write，否则走原有界 schema 修复，不自动赋权；Worker 每轮显示原 steps/tools/tokens 余量、归档 source_refs 与当前回执，超余量 batch 在执行任何工具前按原 repair 路径修复。未扩大工具/步骤/token/费用/时间上限；Publisher 仅新增 retry 数字拆分及 review reason/context 白名单。v9 全量/live 与复杂连续性继续 pending。

后续[自产物修订与 Reviewer 修复](audit/phase2/sprint-deg.md)局部组为 **153 passed / 40.63 秒**，租约恢复组 **90 passed / 32.30 秒**，返工 verdict 提交后重排队恢复组 **28 passed / 13.95 秒**。这些仍是有重叠的本地/Mock 工程验证，不构成新的 live 成功结论。

[固定数值套件失败到同 Worker 修订重验](audit/phase2/sprint-ci.md)扩大组为 **119 passed / 44.14 秒**，含首轮 21 个新增案例；后续[语义反馈恢复组](audit/phase2/semantic-recovery-20261115T090801.xml)为 **74 passed / 34.65 秒**，语义测试文件现有 30 个案例。本地真实数值子进程与脚本模型不算真实 Provider 验收。反馈需有来源、显式修订权限、有效 grant、原预算余量且无未结算动作/调用；修订后仍须真实套件通过。反馈提交后 callback 前崩溃可在重验当前结果、真实语义来源、权限/grant 和原预算后幂等恢复，无需发模型审查；旧结果、变化来源、撤权、预算耗尽、未知动作和回调异常仍阻断。

[审查输入无损表示组](audit/phase2/review-context-20261115T091955.xml)为 **118 passed / 36.18 秒**：完整 source、精确字符范围和共享元数据保留原 packet/PASS 哈希；确切 L2 fixture 的本地 native Gateway reserve 为 64,245，仍受 65,536 上限约束。未发网络请求、未追认旧运行，更大输入超界仍拒绝。新发布的运行配置只含白名单字段，旧记录缺失值保持 null。

后续 [Composer 显式 null 选择 Core schema](audit/phase2/composer-contract-20261115T093043.xml)为 **45 passed / 5.89 秒**；动态合同仍必须完整，角色与权限未扩展。[审查节点范围与输出容量组](audit/phase2/review-scope-cap-tests.xml)为 **123 passed / 31.80 秒**：只审查当前节点目标、criteria 与批准角色，最终交付节点仍承担全部原始要求；输出同时受原输出、context 和累计 token 余量约束，最低自适应容量为 `min(1024, original output cap)`，不足或原费用权限不足仍拒绝。原 packet/PASS 哈希和完整来源保持不变，本地构造不算 live 成功。

用户已暂缓 M7 桌面验收；单一持久聊天的桌面联调、Core 生命周期、设置、审批范围、凭据、备份恢复及安装包仍须以最终实际结果为准。历史[后端加固](PHASE1_MILESTONE7_BACKEND_HARDENING.md)冻结快照为 **488 passed，1 warning，107.62 秒**，双工作目录 Ruff、格式及依赖检查通过，见[验证记录](audit/phase1/milestone7-backend-hardening-verification.json)。它不是当前 Phase 2 的完整套件或桌面发布验收。总体桌面待验项见 [M7 报告草稿](PHASE1_MILESTONE7_REPORT.md)。

Milestone 5 的 Native Worker、动态团队、工具治理与独立证据链已完成本机冻结验收：**282 passed，1 warning，44.99 秒**；真实供应商完成有限的 numeric AST 和 JSON 产物演示，范围见 [M5 报告](PHASE1_MILESTONE5_REPORT.md)。Milestone 6 的最终快照本机完整测试为 **372 passed，1 warning，77.78 秒**，静态、依赖与历史证据核验通过；一次有界真实供应商任务恢复成功，前五次诊断失败均保留。有限合成研究及容量边界见 [M6 报告](PHASE1_MILESTONE6_REPORT.md)。这些结果不能证明无限对话或通用任务正确性。

Router、Planner、Composer、benchmark、Worker 与独立 Reviewer 的模型请求沿用统一 Gateway 准入。价格未知时使用 token-only，不推算费用。当前默认 Review 审批保持启用；通用剩余 DAG 自主重规划、完整类型 payload 合同、学习式语义召回和独立 Reviewer 模型选择仍未完成。当前限制和质量门槛见 [QUALITY_GATES](QUALITY_GATES.md)，配置及恢复复核步骤见 [README](../README.md)。

当前 Worker 使用固定工具、语法检查和有界数值 AST，尚无任意代码/测试命令执行或通用代码补丁工具。`file_write` 仅新建；显式批准的 `file_revise` 可凭最新回执链和未变化哈希，原子修订当前 Worker 自己产出的文件并保留不可变版本，不能修改用户文件或前驱产物。Reviewer 的 Core JSON 解析反馈明确标记来源，不冒充模型审查；已结算截断重试消耗原预算与轮次。租约仅在已结算步骤间续期，仍受当前权限、代次围栏和任务截止约束。运行中团队替换保持同一 DAG；这不等于自主重规划。检索为有来源的词法召回，以上缺口不因局部测试通过而视为完成。

## 历史阶段与证据

各阶段报告和审计记录保留当时的测试结果、限制和待办，其历史描述不代表当前状态：

- [Phase 0 审计](PHASE0_AUDIT.md)及[验证证据](audit/phase0/verification.json)。
- [Milestone 1](PHASE1_MILESTONE1_REPORT.md)、[Milestone 2](PHASE1_MILESTONE2_REPORT.md)、[Milestone 3](PHASE1_MILESTONE3_REPORT.md) 和 [Milestone 4](PHASE1_MILESTONE4_REPORT.md) 报告。
- [Milestone 5](PHASE1_MILESTONE5_REPORT.md) 和 [Milestone 6](PHASE1_MILESTONE6_REPORT.md) 报告及各自审计证据。

历史审计脚本可能覆盖历史证据，重跑前应使用独立输出位置。阶段路线及尚未验证的验收目标见 [ROADMAP](ROADMAP.md)。

# ADR 009: Source-bound planning, independent review and durable coordination

Status: Phase 2 implementation in progress; local and live acceptance are recorded separately.
Date: 2026-11-15.

## Context

ADRs [007](ADR-007-native-worker-and-execution-evidence.md) and
[008](ADR-008-context-recall-budget.md) establish approved native execution, trusted
receipts, bounded context and Gateway admission. Phase 2 needs stronger planning,
revision and collaboration without replacing those controls or adding user chats.

## Decision

1. Keep the persistent Router as the only user-facing Agent. A separate Planner
   consumes the original request, source hashes, constraints and offered tools to
   propose a bounded DAG. A proposal never grants execution authority; plan and
   team approval continue to require the authenticated local user.
2. Store literal user clauses, pending model extractions and separately confirmed
   clauses with distinct provenance. Bound context highlights and retain original
   source readback paths. Conflicts, omissions, expiry and revocation remain visible;
   extracted instructions never substitute for action approval.
3. Review a delivery in a fresh context containing the original contract, criteria,
   bounded actual artifacts and verified receipts. Do not copy the Worker's private
   conversation. Bind the verdict to its input hash and admitted model attempt.
   Evaluate the current node's objective, success criteria and approved role; a
   read-only intermediate researcher must not be assigned a downstream writer's
   artifact. Keep the original request in full and retain every original requirement
   for a node assigned the corresponding final deliverable. Revision grants no authority.
   `NEEDS_REVISION` requires concrete goals and consumes the existing bounded budget.
   A fresh PASS is necessary for review criteria but remains subject to NodeVerifier
   and CompletionGate checks. The current reviewer uses the approved Worker's model;
   separate context does not establish independent model identity.
   Large inputs may use a lossless wire envelope with full untrusted source blocks,
   receipt/text-hash/byte bindings, shared repeated constraint fields and exact
   original-message character spans. Keep the original `_packet` and PASS hash
   unchanged; omit no source or review criterion and retain all context/budget limits.
4. Project typed Agent messages from the existing durable event/outbox transport.
   Preserve task identity, lease fencing, Inbox deduplication and Router-mediated
   control. Agent messages confer no right to mutate another Worker's assignment.
5. Reuse observed model performance as a sourced, sample-counted input to new team
   proposals. Preserve explicit user scores, approved profile hashes, completed
   nodes and historical contracts. Replacement never resets cumulative budgets.
6. Keep `file_write` create-only. Add separately approved R1 `file_revise` only for
   the current Worker's own latest successfully produced artifact, with exact prior
   receipt/hash, current authority/grant checks and atomic replacement. Retain old
   content in immutable intent/receipt history; review and completion validate the
   bounded same-Worker chain and latest bytes. Do not extend old contracts or grant
   authority over user files, predecessor artifacts or unsettled outcomes.
7. Distinguish Core JSON-parser feedback (`deterministic_artifact_validation`,
   `core_json_parser`) from model review. Parser failures may request concrete
   bounded revision but create no model attempt or PASS. Reviewer output fits
   8192, approved role/model caps, remaining model context and the original cumulative
   token remainder. Adaptive output has floor `min(1024, original output cap)`;
   insufficient capacity or original cost authority fails closed, while lower original
   caps stay valid. Native input reservation uses the actual serialized Gateway
   payload, including schema/reasoning settings, and matches admission. Settled truncation
   charges exact actual usage before any bounded new verdict. Unknown remote
   outcomes retain reservations. Committed revision verdicts requeue idempotently.
8. Renew Worker ownership only between settled steps after current token/generation,
   plan/team and status checks, to `min(task deadline, now + lease_seconds)`. Do not
   revive expired claims or enlarge task allocations. Individual calls remain
   bounded by their current lease/deadline.
9. Treat a node's token allowance as cumulative input/output/review/repair usage,
   separate from each model context window. Align the node schema ceiling with the
   existing finite 1,000,000-token graph ceiling; keep the sum of node allowances
   within the approved graph total and retain all lower scenario, team and global
   limits. This does not change previously approved budgets or grant unlimited use.
10. Bind fixed numeric-suite failure feedback to the latest delivery, exact
    Quest/plan/revision/Worker/run, real semantic run/report, source and receipt.
    Label it `deterministic_semantic_validation` / `core_fixed_numeric_suite`, with
    at most ten failed-case diagnostics and no LLM verdict or PASS. Invoke the same
    Worker's revision handler only with explicit graph/node/Worker/member revision
    scopes, a current grant, remaining original budgets and no unresolved actions
    or model attempts; a new delivery must pass the real suite again.

11. V7 guidance covers new intermediate JSON artifacts and delivery_review handoffs with downstream consumers
    toward about 4 KiB (at most 6 KiB) only when all assigned requirements fit. Complete code, final reports
    and required detailed schemas remain full even when larger. This is soft writing
    guidance: no stored artifact is truncated, no hard report-size gate is added, and
    original packet/PASS/source/raw/context/evidence requirements remain unchanged.
    Planner guidance recommends about two model contexts for cumulative source-heavy
    entry-node usage when the original task total permits, retaining at least ten percent
    coordination reserve. V8 removes the output_tokens=2048 preference and requires
    sufficient per-call output for complete schema-valid tool arguments and delivery.
    Central citation IDs retain exact sources.
    New/replacement team proposals and approval enforce a trusted operator concurrency
    cap; absent optional configuration preserves compatibility. Existing approved teams and historical evidence retain their contracts. Core
    supplies Composer and WorkerManager the Worker cap `2`, independent of Gateway
    model-call concurrency. Each resource retains its own original admission limits.
    The live harness takes the smaller CLI/scenario total-token and concurrency limits
    and records the effective values. V8 full/live outcomes are recorded; new v9 outcomes remain pending.

12. For new native TeamWire proposals, only explicit `output_schema_json=null`
    selects a deep copy of `STRICT_DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA`: the model must supply
    all eight delivery fields and confidence within 0–1, with no Core-inserted defaults.
    The contract is checked under any node criterion through JSON Schema and bounded
    repair. Legacy/default direct RoleSpec contracts and explicit older schemas retain
    their original meaning; historical approvals/results are unchanged. Non-finite
    JSON values are rejected through the existing bounded repair path. Strict structure
    does not establish semantic correctness or replace review/evidence gates.
13. V8 removes the intermediate output_tokens=2048 preference: per-call output must
    fit complete schema-valid tool arguments and delivery. Worker instructions cover
    the current node's approved objective, role and criteria; downstream nodes retain
    their own deliverables. Planner guidance uses one node only when the entire task
    is simple read-only analysis and preserves explicitly requested specialist/count
    requirements. Composer guidance preserves unique role IDs and correct specialties,
    and prefers max_steps=16 only when the user's ceiling permits. Native Core configures
    a shared self-repair/review-revision maximum of four; existing counters, original
    steps/tokens/tools/cost/time and review-round limits still bind every attempt.
    Worker concurrency two remains independent of Gateway model-call concurrency.

14. V9 rejects a generated node with a concrete artifact verifier unless that same
    node already permits `file_write`; feedback uses the original bounded Planner
    schema-repair path and inserts no tool authority. Worker requests show remaining
    model steps, tool calls and cumulative tokens, and point to integrity-bound archived
    source_refs/current artifact receipts. This guides reuse of evidence without
    assuming the repeated-read cause is proved. A tool batch exceeding remaining calls
    is rejected before any tool executes and may use the existing bounded repair path;
    the settled model attempt stays charged. Original tool/step/token/cost/time and
    repair/round limits remain unchanged. Publisher adds numeric retry totals/breakdown
    and allowlisted review reason/context fields; prompt/reply/log/artifact bodies stay
    excluded, and missing historical fields remain unknown/null. New v9 full/live
    outcomes and final complex continuity remain pending.

## Consequences and limits

The implementation adds focused services and schema changes rather than a parallel
runtime. Default Review autonomy, policy, exact approvals, receipts and Gateway
reservations remain authoritative. Unknown remote effects stay unresolved until
trusted recovery conditions permit settlement; a client timeout permits no replay.
The [118-case review-input group](../audit/phase2/review-context-20261115T091955.xml)
records local/Mock reconstruction and admission checks. Its L2 fixture's native
Gateway construction reserves 64,245 under the same 65,536 ceiling; this made no
network call and establishes no general larger-packet capacity or live success.

The later [123-case review scope/cap group](../audit/phase2/review-scope-cap-tests.xml)
and [read-only diagnostic](../audit/phase2/review-scope-cap.md) retain the failed L2
second-review packet: 59,601 bytes, unchanged original packet/PASS binding and
65,536-byte raw packet limit. Its local native reservation is 59,761 input plus
5,775 output = 65,536 under the unchanged context ceiling. This offline construction
made no network call, resets no budget and expands no permission.

Later L2/L3 live runs still exceeded raw/context limits before review or restart;
L3 also lacked cumulative review headroom, while L2 declared concurrency three
above scenario cap two. The [v5 full suite](../audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v5.xml)
passed 820 tests / one warning / 219.96 seconds before v6 changes. The
[69-case operator-cap group](../audit/phase2/composer-concurrency-20261115T094900.xml)
and [99-case report-guidance group](../audit/phase2/worker-report-guidance-tests.xml)
are local/Mock evidence. The [v6 full suite](../audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v6.xml)
retained 848 passed, one failed, one warning / 283.77 seconds: the actual parallel
lifespan test exposed the incorrect coupling of Gateway model concurrency one and
Worker concurrency two. V7 restores separate limits without editing the original
test. All three v6 live reruns failed at original repair or review capacity limits;
v7 guidance/limits do not retroactively repair them. The [v7 full suite](../audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v7.xml) passed 849 tests /
one warning / 216.87 seconds, manifest `58339132008a97956237ec38c2eb19eb7062f46b4ef2f5f946567ad52be26627`
(155 files; Ruff/152-file formatting passed). All three v7 live attempts failed:
output truncation/repair exhaustion, missing required specialists/context capacity,
and actual NEEDS_REVISION followed by ten-step exhaustion. The
[185-case contract group](../audit/phase2/native-delivery-contract-20261115T151500.xml)
and [latest 36-case file](../audit/phase2/native-delivery-nonfinite-20261115T152200.xml)
are overlapping local/Mock evidence for later v8 changes. The [v8 full suite](../audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v8.xml) passed 886 /
one warning / 283.46 seconds on manifest `92bb6067ff7bc1dadfa6aa9b5994089969603b53b3980a9a5601d0a140e6b9e3`
(156 files; Ruff/153-file formatting/pip passed). All three v8 live attempts failed:
L1/L2 reviewed then exhausted tools through repeated reads, with actual Worker
archives but no Core restart and one unresolved Router-notice attempt each; L3's
read-only node could not produce its required file. The
[independent audit](../audit/phase2/continuity-and-live-diagnosis-v8.md) separates
implemented continuity from these actual failures. The
[lossless-reference diagnostic](../audit/phase2/reviewer-lossless-v8-diagnostic.json)
and [124-case group](../audit/phase2/reviewer-lossless-v8-tests.xml), 60.43 seconds,
verify an exact 524-byte native reservation saving with original packet/hash/raw
cap preserved, no network call and no historical change. Final v9 full/live outcomes remain pending.

Fixed-suite feedback rejects duplicate results, callback errors and fake success;
if a callback commits before raising, the exact queued revision is fenced blocked.
A crash after semantic feedback commit but before callback permits idempotent
recovery through `IndependentReviewService.tick()`, including semantic-only nodes,
without a model-review request. Recovery requires `revision_available=true`, the
current delivery and genuine semantic/source/receipt bindings, current tool
scopes/grants, remaining original budgets and no unsettled actions or Gateway
attempts. The Worker revision interface rechecks approved team, cumulative
repair/step/token/deadline limits and one-time event consumption. Stale or changed
sources, revoked grants, exhausted budgets and originally unavailable revisions
remain blocked. The [74-case recovery group](../audit/phase2/semantic-recovery-20261115T090801.xml)
provides local/Mock evidence; this does not authorize unknown-action replay or
establish live task correctness.

Schema repair, review rounds, Agent counts, context packets and replanning are
bounded. General automatic remaining-DAG replanning, arbitrary hierarchical Agent
expansion, exhaustive per-message payload schemas and learned semantic retrieval
remain incomplete. The legacy summary-only delivery contract stays compatible;
`delivery_review` explicitly requires all eight delivery fields. Local/Mock tests
and synthetic benchmarks do not establish complex live-task acceptance. See the
[Phase 2 report](../PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md) for the current evidence.

The current execution boundary remains the fixed Core toolset: bounded numeric
AST, syntax checks and diagnostics, with create-only writes and explicitly scoped
own-artifact revision. General program execution, arbitrary test runners, general
repository patching and running-DAG revision remain incomplete.

# Phase 2 — Agent Intelligence Report

Updated: 2026-11-15 (Asia/Shanghai). Branch: `codex/phase1-continuous`.
Integration owner: root agent. **Phase 2 is in progress. One strict L1 run passed;
L2/L3 acceptance and final frozen-source verification remain incomplete.**

## Scope and architectural change

This sprint moves the existing backend toward autonomous task execution. Desktop
visual changes, packaging and the deferred M7 desktop Alpha are outside this sprint's
acceptance. Existing Phase 1 reports and failed experiments remain preserved.

The source audit and complete execution diagram are in the
[execution-chain audit](audit/phase2/execution-chain-audit.md). The minimum change is
recorded in [ADR 009](adr/ADR-009-agent-intelligence-contracts-and-review.md):

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    U[One user conversation] --> R[Persistent Router]
    R --> P[Separate Planner and proposed DAG]
    P --> A[Authenticated plan and team approval]
    A --> W[Native private Worker loops]
    W --> T[Governed tools and receipts]
    T --> V[Fresh independent review]
    V -->|concrete revision goals| W
    V --> N[NodeVerifier and CompletionGate]
    N --> R
```

All model requests use the existing Gateway and durable admission ledger. The
Router remains the only user-facing Agent. Workers, reviewers and durable events
do not create extra user conversations or use another Agent product as a backend.

## Implemented mechanisms

| Area | Current behavior | Verification boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Router and Planner | Strict decisions, one bounded repair, atomic turn commits, original and latest goal-update request IDs/hashes, offered-tool/capability checks, DAG limit of eight nodes/sixteen edges | Mock reasoning and local persistence regressions; live protocol coverage below |
| Team intelligence | Existing single-model/greedy/coverage/complementarity strategies consume sourced online observations with counts and Wilson intervals; proposals retain profile/source hashes | Synthetic selection proxies and local/Mock integration; no measured general model-quality gain |
| Team adaptation | Approved replacement may cover remaining nodes while retaining completed assignments and historical approvals | Local regression; general autonomous remaining-DAG replanning and hierarchical expansion incomplete |
| Native Worker | Private model/tool loop, checkpoints, fenced lease renewal between settled steps, bounded repair, distinct failure categories and structured delivery | One earlier strict L1 pass with self-repair; v8 failed L1/L2 show actual Worker archives and NEEDS_REVISION, without mid-execution Core restart; complex continuity pending |
| Artifact revision | Separately approved R1 `file_revise` atomically replaces the same Worker's own latest produced artifact using an intact receipt chain and unchanged hash | Local/Mock race, provenance and immutable-history checks; general repository editing remains absent |
| Independent review | Fresh packet from original goal, criteria, real artifacts and receipts; PASS/NEEDS_REVISION/REJECT/BLOCKED; concrete revision goals, default two-round limit, hard maximum four | Current same approved underlying model in a separate context; independent model diversity is absent |
| Evidence gate | Review provenance plus fixed semantic verifiers and final receipt/artifact/approval checks govern completion | Mock/adversarial regressions and actual local tool checks; self-report never establishes live completion |
| Context and constraints | Bounded Router/Worker highlights, original-source readback, sourced literal/pending/confirmed clauses, potential conflicts, expiry and revocation | 53 combined Router/Planner/context/memory tests; 9 exploratory synthetic source-identity cases |
| Memory | L0 current interaction, L1 Quest, L2 project/history and L3 failure observations; bounded keyword/alias/Quest/time/type filtering | Lexical retrieval; embeddings and learned semantic relevance absent |
| Agent protocol/recovery | Typed projection of existing event transport with task identities, fenced leases and deduplication; unresolved effects retain reservations | Per-type payload validation remains partial; arbitrary in-flight external-effect recovery is unproven |

The delivery vocabulary contains `summary`, `findings`, `decisions`, `artifacts`,
`evidence_references`, `unresolved_issues`, `confidence` and `next_actions`.
`delivery_review` enforces all eight. Legacy/default compatibility schemas still
require only `summary`; missing fields are not evidence of completed work.

For new native TeamWire proposals, only explicit `output_schema_json=null`
selects a deep copy of `STRICT_DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA`: the model must supply
all eight delivery fields and confidence within 0–1, with no Core-inserted defaults.
The contract is checked under any node criterion through JSON Schema and bounded
repair. Legacy/default direct RoleSpec contracts and explicit older schemas retain
their original meaning; historical approvals/results are unchanged. Non-finite
JSON values are rejected through the existing bounded repair path. Strict structure
does not establish semantic correctness or replace review/evidence gates.

`file_write` remains create-only. `file_revise` requires explicit plan/node and
team authority plus a workspace grant, with `path`, `prior_receipt_id`,
`expected_sha256` and full replacement `content`. It checks the latest successful
same-Worker receipt, current file bytes and authority immediately before atomic
replacement. Immutable intent parameters and receipts retain every prior version.
Review and read-only acceptance validate the bounded revision chain (at most 64
receipts) before comparing current bytes with the latest successful version.
Predecessor artifacts, user files, stale hashes and unsettled outcomes are excluded;
old create-only contracts acquire no additional authority.

Reviewer output is capped by 8192, the approved role/model caps, remaining model
context and original cumulative Worker tokens. Adaptive capacity keeps a floor of
`min(1024, original output cap)`; inability to fit that floor or original cost
limits fails closed. Native Gateway input reservation uses the actual serialized
payload, including schema/reasoning settings, and matches Core admission.
Review evaluates the current node's objective, criteria and approved role; an
intermediate read-only researcher is not asked to produce a downstream writer's
artifact. Nodes assigned final deliverables retain all original requirements.
`FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` defaults to two and accepts integers one through four;
the live harness explicitly selects three within its scenario's three-round cap.
Existing runs retain their original review limits and results.
Large packets can use a lossless wire envelope while the original `_packet` and
PASS `packet_sha256` stay unchanged. Full `file_read` source text appears once in
untrusted blocks bound to receipt references, text SHA256 and UTF-8 lengths.
Repeated constraint metadata uses shared fields; a statement already present
verbatim in an original/update message uses that same source's exact Unicode
`[start,end)` span, otherwise its full text remains. Native structured-output
requests retain the Gateway schema while avoiding a duplicate system-prompt copy.
The original L2 fixture packet was 56,755 bytes: its old conservative reserve was
73,065, the review-envelope estimate is 64,622 and actual local
`ProviderGateway._payload` construction reserves 64,245, within the same 65,536
context ceiling. All three source texts remain complete. This construction made
no network call, changed no historical run and establishes admission only for
that exact fixture; larger packets still fail closed when limits are exceeded.
Receipt-bound JSON syntax errors produce concrete line/column and receipt/hash
feedback labelled `deterministic_artifact_validation` / `core_json_parser`, with
`NEEDS_REVISION` only while repair/round/step/token/deadline limits permit, otherwise
`BLOCKED`. This is a Core-parser result, with no fictional model call or PASS.
A truncated model verdict can be retried only after exact admitted/settled usage
is reconciled (or under explicitly labelled Mock tests). `review.response_rejected`
records `reason_code=truncated`; actual usage remains charged, subsequent rounds
consume the same budgets, and unknown remote outcomes are not replayed. A committed
revision verdict can be requeued idempotently after restart.

The fixed numeric verifier has a separate feedback path: a genuine failed
`scheduler-v1` subprocess report can emit `review.result` with
`review_context=deterministic_semantic_validation` and
`validation_source=core_fixed_numeric_suite`. It binds the latest delivery,
Quest/plan/revision/Worker/run, actual semantic run, receipt, source and report
hashes, with at most ten failed-case diagnostics. Requeue calls the same Worker's
revision handler only when graph/node/Worker/member tool scopes explicitly permit
`file_revise`, a current grant exists, repair/step/token/tool/cost/deadline budgets
remain and no action or Gateway attempt is unresolved. A new delivery and genuine
suite PASS are still required; deterministic feedback is no LLM verdict or PASS.
Duplicate result feedback is rejected. Callback errors or fake success fail closed;
a callback that committed before raising has its exact queued revision fenced.
Persisted semantic feedback can recover once after a crash before callback, including
semantic-only nodes, through `IndependentReviewService.tick()` without issuing a
model review. Recovery rechecks `revision_available=true`, actual semantic/source/
receipt and current execution bindings, current tool scopes/grants, tool/cost
headroom and absence of unsettled actions or Gateway attempts. The existing Worker
revision interface still checks the latest delivery, approved team, cumulative
repair/step/token/deadline limits and idempotent consumption. Stale or changed
sources, revoked authority, exhausted budgets and originally unavailable revision
events remain blocked. This does not recover an arbitrary external action.

Valid Worker owners renew between settled steps to the earlier of the task deadline
and `now + lease_seconds`. Renewal preserves token/generation fencing and current
plan/team/status checks; expired claims, competing owners and paused/cancelled or
changed-plan assignments fail closed. Each call still fits the current lease and
deadline. This is not an in-flight heartbeat or a larger task allocation.

Team token allowance and single-request context are separate bounds. A member's
`input_tokens + output_tokens` becomes its cumulative Worker/review allowance;
the allowance may span several context windows. Each request remains bounded by
the approved/current model context, remaining cumulative tokens and the per-response
output limit. Node/team/global approvals, cost ledgers and finite generation caps
remain in force; compaction and review do not refresh the allowance.
The node schema permits at most 1,000,000 cumulative tokens, matching the existing
graph ceiling; summed node allowances still fit the approved graph total. The
lower live scenario caps remain L1 180,000, L2 360,000 and L3 630,000. Existing
approvals are unchanged. See the [budget audit](audit/phase2/cumulative-budget-and-quest-identity.md)
for the distinction between this schema ceiling and an actual approved allocation.

Constraint provenance is separate from execution authority. Literal clauses are
`explicit_user`, model paraphrases are `pending_model`, and a distinct original
user confirmation can produce `user_confirmed`. Original IDs and hashes are checked;
potential conflicts are surfaced rather than silently resolved by recency.

Router archives keep at most 64 user highlights/12,288 UTF-8 bytes and 16 other
highlights/4,096 bytes. Worker highlights are trimmed to their actual input budget;
initial contracts and live tool pairs are protected. Per-Quest evidence and receipt
snapshots each cap at 64 and signal omissions. Original durable records remain
available for checked source readback. These bounds solve repeated full-history
injection, not unlimited context or storage.

A fully settled latest tool exchange may also leave the live message window when
its minimum pinned representation cannot fit, but only after a prior archive makes
the source-read tool available in the current request. The entire call/results
batch is archived together with explicit omitted/raw-readback/untrusted metadata,
same-run successful receipt bindings and original-source integrity. Pending or
uncertain tails and required initial contracts remain protected. The retained L2
failure's offline read-only backup reproduced the block, then fit 12,326 bytes
within the same 21,759-byte input budget with exact source readback and unchanged
budgets/evidence; the original live failure is preserved. [Sprint F](audit/phase2/sprint-f.md)
records the 97-case related regression group and diagnostic limits.

Quest identity recall separately selects actual task/Core Quest records, with at
most 100 returned items/65,536 bytes and the existing 512-candidate scan ceiling.
Omitted ordinary constraint/message facts do not by themselves imply an ambiguous

# FORGE v4 — Persistent Router Agent System

FORGE is a self-built, general-purpose autonomous Agent desktop application.

## Engineering status — 2026-11-15

Phase 2 Agent Intelligence is in progress. The existing native runtime now connects a separate Planner, source-bound constraints and bounded memory, observation-informed team proposals, fresh-context independent review and typed durable Agent coordination. One retained strict L1 live run passed with review revision and Worker self-repair, without compaction or restart; the concurrent L2 and later L3 attempts failed. Later L2/L3 reruns also failed before review at packet/context and cumulative-budget limits. The [v5 full backend suite](docs/audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v5.xml) passed 820 tests with one warning in 219.96 seconds, before later v6 changes. The [v6 full suite](docs/audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v6.xml) retained 848 passed, one failed, one warning / 283.77 seconds; all three v6 live reruns failed. V7 corrects independent Worker/Gateway concurrency and extends bounded handoff/budget guidance. The [v7 full suite](docs/audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v7.xml) passed 849 tests / one warning / 216.87 seconds, while all three v7 live attempts failed. The [v8 full suite](docs/audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v8.xml) passed 886 tests / one warning / 283.46 seconds; all three v8 live attempts failed, despite real review/revision and Worker archiving in L1/L2. L1/L2 each retain an unresolved Router-notice attempt and no mid-execution Core restart occurred. The v9 full suite passed 895 tests / one warning / 237.83 seconds; both v9 L2/L3 live runs still failed before review at the unchanged raw-packet cap. Thirty-nine finished driver records are published without changing original outcomes. V10 capacity-feedback/retry-accounting work and complex-task continuity still await final verification. The local Provider's small live protocol probes passed [11/11 with the proxy default](docs/audit/phase2/provider-probe.json) and [10/11 with explicit `reasoning_effort=none`](docs/audit/phase2/provider-probe-reasoning-none.json); the latter retained a failed exact-text dialogue check. Focused local/Mock suites and exploratory synthetic benchmarks are recorded separately. See the [Phase 2 report](docs/PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md), [status](docs/PHASE2_STATUS.md), [experiments](docs/PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md) and [architecture decision](docs/adr/ADR-009-agent-intelligence-contracts-and-review.md).

Phase 1 Milestones 1–6 provide the persistence, governance, Registry, DAG, native Workers, tool/evidence and context/budget foundation. Historical M6 verification passed 372 tests; one bounded live continuation succeeded after five retained diagnostic failures. The [M7 backend hardening round](docs/PHASE1_MILESTONE7_BACKEND_HARDENING.md) passed 488 local tests. Desktop Alpha, final native integration and packaging are deferred; these historical backend results do not establish a desktop release.

See [current status](docs/STATUS.md), the [Phase 0 audit report](docs/PHASE0_AUDIT.md), and the report's dependency-ordered development plan. The release references `codex/MASTER_PROMPT.md`, but that file is missing from the supplied archive.

**The user has one persistent conversation.** A persistent Router Agent owns that conversation and coordinates multiple long-running Quests and hidden Worker Sessions. Workers have isolated execution contexts, but they are never presented as separate user conversations.

## Product invariants

1. One persistent user-facing conversation per workspace.
2. One persistent Router identity and resumable state per workspace.
3. Multiple durable Quests can run behind that conversation.
4. Worker Sessions are private execution contexts, not user-facing chats.
5. Worker events are selectively relayed into the single conversation timeline.
6. Model Provider, Model Profile, Role Template, Agent Instance, Quest and Session are separate domain entities.
7. Model Registry uses provider metadata, FORGE benchmark results, online performance and explicit user overrides.
8. Team composition combines reusable role templates with bounded dynamic role synthesis.
9. FORGE owns its Agent Loop, Router, Worker Runtime, Tool Engine, Memory, Governance and Evidence.
10. Codex, DSH and Claude Code are architectural references only, never execution backends.

## What this release contains

- Typed Python domain layer and repository interfaces.
- SQLite persistence with schema versioning and transaction boundaries.
- Persistent `main` conversation and Router identity.
- Quest lifecycle state machine and hidden Worker Session records.
- Durable event log with sequence cursor.
- Model Registry and explainable capability-fit team composition baseline.
- Provider gateway and explicit unconfigured provider; Mock protocol tests are labelled.
- FastAPI API with input validation and consistent error handling.
- React single-conversation UI with background Quest panel.
- Automated tests for persistence, lifecycle, router classification and team composition.
- Architecture, threat model, ADRs, detailed roadmap and Codex execution prompts.

## Important maturity statement

This is an engineering foundation with bounded context recovery, sourced lexical recall and evidence-gated execution. The Router uses a configured Provider or explicitly fails. Mock tests, synthetic experiments and real-provider observations are identified separately. The current independent reviewer uses the approved Worker's model in a fresh context. General autonomous replanning, learned semantic retrieval, arbitrary-scale continuity and complex-task correctness remain open. Plan/team/replacement approval stays authenticated and Review mode remains enabled. A proposal record alone never proves execution.

## Backend setup

The model-driven Router requires explicit provider configuration. Set the process environment
variables `FORGE_PROVIDER_ID`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_KIND` (for example `openai_compatible`),
`FORGE_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REF` (for example
`FORGE_PROVIDER_KEY_EXAMPLE`), `FORGE_ROUTER_MODEL_ID`, and
`FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` (an operator-supplied maximum context window). Put the actual
credential only in the process environment variable named by the credential reference. Set
`FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_TOOLS=true` and `FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_JSON_SCHEMA=true` only when
the provider supports them. Without configuration the Core starts but Router message calls fail
explicitly; no keyword or mock provider is selected automatically. The optional `request_id`
in a message request allows safe retry: reuse it only for the same input.
For live calls, register an enabled model with the same provider and model ID and explicitly set
both `tool_calling_support` and `structured_output_support` to supported. Unknown capabilities
are rejected. Values submitted through the model API are recorded as user overrides.

Provider timing, Worker ownership and review/output limits use the process environment:

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Per-attempt timeout in seconds; finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `30`. A timeout does not prove the upstream operation stopped. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_MAX_RETRIES` | Additional Gateway retries, integer `0`–`3`; defaults to `1`. Each HTTP attempt requires its own budget admission. |
| `FORGE_WORKER_LEASE_SECONDS` | Worker ownership lease, finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `60`. Valid current owners renew between steps, capped by the task deadline. The local call wait is bounded by the current lease; an upstream operation may remain unresolved after that wait ends. |
| `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` | Maximum review rounds; integer `1`–`4`, defaults to `2`. The live acceptance harness explicitly selects `3`, matching its scenario cap. This does not reset budgets or change historical runs. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_REASONING_EFFORT` | Optional explicit OpenAI-compatible/DeepSeek request setting: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`. Unset sends no setting. Configure only for a model that advertises support; Anthropic configuration rejects it. |
| `FORGE_ROUTER_OUTPUT_RESERVE` | Router response-token ceiling and reserved output allowance; integer `1`–`8192`, defaults to `2048`. `FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` must be greater than this value. A registered model's known output limit must also support it. |
| `FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` | Operator-supplied Router context ceiling, required when setting a Router model. Core startup requires an integer greater than `2048` and greater than the configured output reserve. |

The Phase 2 live acceptance harness uses a 120-second timeout, a 150-second Worker lease and zero additional
Gateway retries, with a Router output reserve of `4096` and `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS=3`
within the scenario's three-round cap. Router/Planner schema repair remains a separately bounded stage;
neither setting authorizes replay of an unresolved external action.

The current WorkBuddy acceptance harness explicitly requests `reasoning_effort=none`,
which the local proxy implementation advertises for the requested model. This is
an operator setting, not independent proof of the upstream model's internal behavior.
Earlier diagnostic runs used the proxy default and retain their separate results.

The Router reads a bounded snapshot and calls the provider outside the database write
transaction. A successful decision and its messages commit together; provider errors, invalid
decisions, or budget failures leave no messages or Quest changes for that turn. The caller can
retry with the same request ID. The context budget uses a conservative UTF-8 byte estimate,
reserves output and request overhead, and also respects a known registry context window. Tool
access is limited to read-only Core queries. Worker execution separately requires approved plan/team contracts and governed tool permissions.

Python 3.11+ recommended.

```bash
cd backend
python -m venv .venv
# Windows PowerShell:
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
# macOS/Linux:
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-lock.txt
python -m pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation -e .
pytest
python -m forge_api
```

The lock file is verified on Windows with Python 3.13; other platforms and Python versions have not been verified. The editable installation requires build tooling already available. API documentation endpoints are disabled.

### Core authentication and development bootstrap

Core requires a fresh cryptographically random 32-byte process secret; `.env` is explicitly rejected. For manual browser development, supply it as 64 hex characters in `FORGE_CORE_SECRET` using a protected input method and enter the same secret into the UI's password field. Never place it in command history, source files, URLs, logs, or persistent browser storage. In the native desktop integration, the parent supplies the secret through a private pipe and the UI receives the derived session bearer in memory. Restarting Core invalidates old bearer tokens. Native integration is still undergoing final verification.

The unauthenticated public loopback `/health` returns only liveness and a random per-process session challenge; an authenticated request also receives Router identity and background status. A trusted client computes the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 over the UTF-8 challenge using the decoded 32-byte secret, and sends `Authorization: Bearer <digest>` on API requests. Requests without an Origin are allowed only with authentication and a loopback peer and Host; browser requests must also use an explicitly allowed Origin. These boundaries protect against unauthorized webpages and other untrusted clients; they do not protect secrets from an attacker who can read the same OS user's process memory. Keep the development server and any allowed origin trusted.

The authenticated user API supports `POST /api/approvals`, `GET /api/approvals?quest_id=...`, `GET /api/approvals/{id}`, and POSTs to `/{id}/decision` or `/{id}/revoke`. Workspace grants use `GET`/`POST /api/quests/{id}/grants` and `POST /api/quests/{id}/grants/revoke`. Decisions and grants record the authenticated local user, not a caller-supplied actor. The bearer represents that user; it must never be exposed to a model or registered as an Agent tool. These routes do not execute actions or accept trusted evidence. The M7 desktop approval and scope controls are under integration testing.

### Workspace and Settings

`python -m forge_api` is the shared Core launcher. From the repository root on Windows, `./scripts/run-backend.ps1` sets up the virtual environment and uses that launcher without shell activation. Pass `-WorkspaceRoot 'D:\YourWorkspace'` to the script, or `python -m forge_api --workspace-root 'D:\YourWorkspace'` directly. Workspace roots must be absolute paths.

The default Workspace is independent of the checkout, installation and shell directory:

| OS | Default Workspace root |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%/FORGE/workspaces/default` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/FORGE/workspaces/default` |
| Linux | `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/forge/workspaces/default` |

The database defaults to `<WorkspaceRoot>/data/forge.sqlite3`. Settings are loaded as follows:

1. Choose the root using `--workspace-root`, then the process variable `FORGE_WORKSPACE_ROOT`, then the OS default (in that order). A root in `.env` is rejected because the root determines which file to read.
2. Load `<WorkspaceRoot>/.env` if present. `FORGE_ENV_FILE` in the process environment can select another file; relative file names resolve from the root. An explicitly selected missing file is an error. The shell directory's `.env` is ignored. Copy `backend/.env.example` to the selected Workspace root.
3. Process variables override file values. Supported settings are `FORGE_WORKSPACE_ID`, `FORGE_DB_PATH`, `FORGE_HOST` and `FORGE_PORT`; empty values and invalid ports fail startup. `.env` does not expand variables or modify the process environment.
4. Resolve relative database paths from the root and normalize them to absolute paths. The default Workspace ID is a hash of the normalized root; an explicit stable ID supports moving a Workspace. A database already bound to another ID is rejected.

The CLI and desktop Core bootstrap use the same Workspace settings and a new process secret. Direct `uvicorn forge_api.main:app` requires the same secret and loopback binding; prefer the shared launcher.

After a workspace restore, a restore fence blocks writes until an offline review succeeds. Close the desktop and Core, inspect the restored workspace and rollback directory, then use the packaged Python executable with the exact manifest hash and rollback directory shown by the application (replace every placeholder):

```powershell
& 'C:\path\to\packaged\python.exe' -I -m forge_api.maintenance review-restore --workspace-root 'C:\path\to\workspace' --manifest-sha256 '<64-lowercase-hex>' --rollback-directory '.forge-previous-<32-hex>' --reason '<10+ character review reason>'
```

The review validates the source hash, rollback directory name, reason, historical receipts and budget state; unresolved effects or reservations cause it to fail closed. Acknowledging an unknown native operation is a separate action and does not clear the restore fence or establish that the operation succeeded.

Legacy databases are **not discovered or moved automatically**. If an earlier version used `backend/data/forge.sqlite3` or another CWD-relative location, stop its Core process, back up the database with SQLite's backup API (or copy the database and WAL files together while stopped), and set `FORGE_DB_PATH` to its absolute path. The first successful open migrates it in place to the current schema without changing the Router ID or existing records. Migration failure rolls back the entire pending chain; unknown future versions and ambiguous version metadata are rejected. Downgrades are unsupported.

Events and pending Outbox rows commit in the same transaction as their associated business changes. Durable per-consumer delivery uses leases, fencing, bounded retries, Inbox deduplication and dead-letter/replay records. Historical events migrate as pending. External tool effects require their own durable intents and receipts; event delivery alone does not make external effects exactly once.

### Approved Worker execution

Workers consume an approved Quest DAG and a separately approved team. Tool scopes, provider/model identity and token/tool/time/concurrency budgets are bound to those contracts. File writes additionally require a workspace grant; HTTPS/MCP actions require exact action approval and an operator allowlist. `FORGE_TOOL_NETWORK_HOSTS_JSON` is a JSON host list (at most 64); `FORGE_MCP_SERVERS_JSON` maps server names to `{"url":"https://example.invalid/mcp","tools":["example_tool"]}` (at most 16 servers), with the HTTPS host included in the allowlist. Defaults are empty and deny network access. These values are operator configuration, never model output. `jsonschema` validates Worker result contracts; it does not judge domain correctness. Help/reassignment produces a pending team proposal for authenticated approval. An uncertain action cannot be silently retried or discarded during replacement. Unsupported or failed fixed JSON criteria require manual review; infrastructure verification retries are bounded to three attempts.

A member's `input_tokens + output_tokens` defines its cumulative Worker/review
allowance across model turns; it may exceed a single model context window while
remaining within the approved node and team limits. Each request independently
fits the remaining allowance and model context, and `output_tokens` also caps
one response. Compaction does not reset cumulative usage.

V7 guidance covers new intermediate JSON artifacts and delivery_review handoffs with downstream consumers
toward about 4 KiB (at most 6 KiB) only when all assigned requirements fit. Complete code, final reports
and required detailed schemas remain full even when larger. This is soft writing
guidance: no stored artifact is truncated, no hard report-size gate is added, and
original packet/PASS/source/raw/context/evidence requirements remain unchanged.
Planner guidance recommends about two model contexts of cumulative allocation for
a source-heavy entry node, when the task ceiling permits, and at least ten percent
coordination reserve within the original total. V8 removes the fixed intermediate-output
preference and preserves enough per-call output for complete schema-valid tool
arguments and delivery. Shared source citation IDs avoid repeating full hashes while
preserving exact references.
New/replacement team proposals and approval enforce a trusted operator concurrency
cap; existing approved teams and historical evidence retain their contracts. Core
supplies Composer and WorkerManager the Worker concurrency cap `2`, independently
of the Gateway model-call concurrency cap. Both resource limits remain enforced.
The live harness takes the smaller CLI/scenario total-token and concurrency limits
and records the effective values. V8/v9 full/live outcomes are recorded; final post-v10 verification remains pending.

For new native TeamWire proposals, only explicit `output_schema_json=null`
selects a deep copy of `STRICT_DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA`: the model must supply
all eight delivery fields and confidence within 0–1, with no Core-inserted defaults.
The contract is checked under any node criterion through JSON Schema and bounded
repair. Legacy/default direct RoleSpec contracts and explicit older schemas retain
their original meaning; historical approvals/results are unchanged. Non-finite
JSON values are rejected through the existing bounded repair path. Strict structure
does not establish semantic correctness or replace review/evidence gates.

V8 removes the intermediate output_tokens=2048 preference: per-call output must
fit complete schema-valid tool arguments and delivery. Worker instructions cover
the current node's approved objective, role and criteria; downstream nodes retain
their own deliverables. Planner guidance uses one node only when the entire task
is simple read-only analysis and preserves explicitly requested specialist/count
requirements. Composer guidance preserves unique role IDs and correct specialties,
and prefers max_steps=16 only when the user's ceiling permits. Native Core configures
a shared self-repair/review-revision maximum of four; existing counters, original
steps/tokens/tools/cost/time and review-round limits still bind every attempt.
Worker concurrency two remains independent of Gateway model-call concurrency.

V9 rejects a generated node with a concrete artifact verifier unless that same
node already permits `file_write`; feedback uses the original bounded Planner
schema-repair path and inserts no tool authority. Worker requests with an effective per-request allowance ≥8192 show remaining
model steps, tool calls and cumulative tokens, and point to integrity-bound archived
source_refs/current artifact receipts. This guides reuse of evidence without
assuming the repeated-read cause is proved. A tool batch exceeding remaining calls
is rejected before any tool executes and may use the existing bounded repair path;
the settled model attempt stays charged. Original tool/step/token/cost/time and
repair/round limits remain unchanged. Publisher adds numeric retry totals/breakdown
and allowlisted review reason/context fields; prompt/reply/log/artifact bodies stay
excluded, and missing historical fields remain unknown/null. V9 full/live
outcomes are recorded below; final post-v10 complex continuity remains pending.

The [v9 full suite](docs/audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v9.xml) / [log](docs/audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v9.log)
passed 895 tests with one warning in 237.83 seconds. Its [157-file manifest](docs/audit/phase2/source-manifest-v9.json)
is `9a33b199404b777428ff0f0e1a1c1da356ad93b23b4395565fc0d211b3d9203a`;
Ruff, formatting for 154 Python files and pip checks passed. This predates v10.
[Offline benchmark v9](docs/audit/phase2/benchmark-final-v9.json), `benchmark_c4387a6e26ac`,
completed in 5.9372256 seconds with zero Provider calls on the same fixed dataset.

The v9 live runs share snapshot
`624f0ac7cb1873163e2e0a5b1849642bb363d553aedab4331096a0286b134db8`.
L2 `20261115T021801Z-L2-b11011` failed in 80.141 seconds: 17 model/six tool
calls, charged input/output 65,607/9,348 tokens, unknown zero.
L3 `20261115T021801Z-L3-290b7f` failed in 97.584 seconds: 18 model/six tool
calls, charged 71,908/14,522 tokens, one unresolved Router-notice reservation
of 9,985+4,096; total actual usage and cost remain unknown.
Actual receipt-bound intermediate artifacts were 15,235/10,788 bytes respectively.
Read-only reconstruction produced raw packets of 68,207/68,967 bytes, exceeding
the unchanged 65,536 cap. Both retained `review_packet_too_large`, zero
`review.started`, the first Worker at `review_pending`, no successor and no restart.

All 39 finished driver records are safely published in
[snapshot-v2](docs/audit/phase2/live-runs/snapshot-v2/index.json), with original run records and
diagnostic-snapshot-v1 preserved. Publication makes no Provider call and does not
promote failed or unaccepted tasks. Historical retry totals can overlap: the old
`worker_runs.repairs` includes review revisions. V10 counts actual self-repair
events separately and marks future records `retry_accounting=disjoint_event_counts_v2`;
[27 focused regressions](docs/audit/phase2/retry-accounting-v10-fixed.xml) pass, while original
run counters remain unchanged. Final v10 full/live verification is pending;
Core capacity feedback is not independent model review or PASS.


The fixed Worker tools support syntax checking with `python_compile`, bounded
numeric execution with `numeric_ast` and the `python_version` diagnostic through
`shell_inspect`. Arbitrary shell commands, unrestricted Python execution and a
general code patch tool are unavailable. `file_write` only creates new files.
The separately approved R1 `file_revise` tool atomically replaces only the current
Worker's own latest successful artifact. It requires `path`, `prior_receipt_id`,
`expected_sha256` and complete new `content`, an intact same-Worker receipt chain,
the current unchanged hash and a valid workspace grant. Earlier bytes remain in
immutable intent/receipt history. Existing create-only contracts gain no permission;
user files, predecessor artifacts, stale versions and uncertain outcomes cannot be
revised through this tool. All revision remains subject to the original criteria.
Team replacement keeps the current DAG; automatic replanning of a running DAG
remains incomplete.

Independent review uses the approved model in a fresh context and evaluates the
current node's objective, criteria and approved role. The full original request
remains available, and a node assigned a final deliverable retains all original
requirements. Output fits 8192, role/model caps, remaining model context and the
original cumulative token allowance. Adaptive capacity keeps a floor of
`min(1024, original output cap)`; insufficient capacity or original cost authority
fails closed. Native Gateway input reservation accounts for the actual serialized
payload, including schema and reasoning settings. Receipt-bound invalid
JSON produces explicitly labelled Core-parser revision feedback; it is not an LLM
review or PASS. A settled truncated review may request a compact verdict within
the remaining rounds, steps, tokens and deadline after charging actual usage.
Core review defaults to two rounds; `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` accepts only integers
one through four. The live harness selects three within its three-round scenario
cap. Prior runs retain their original round limit and outcome. No revision or
retry resets cumulative budgets or replays an unknown remote outcome.

Large review requests can use a lossless input envelope: full source text stays in
untrusted source blocks, repeated constraint metadata is shared and exact statements
reference their original character spans. The original packet and PASS hash binding
remain unchanged. No source text or review requirement is dropped, and requests
that still exceed the packet/model/budget limits remain blocked. The
[118-test local/Mock group](docs/audit/phase2/review-context-20261115T091955.xml)
includes exact reconstruction and review-round configuration checks.

A genuine fixed numeric-suite failure can also return labelled Core feedback
(`deterministic_semantic_validation`) to the same Worker. Requeue requires explicit
`file_revise` authority, a current grant, remaining repair/step/token/tool/cost/time
budgets and no unresolved actions or model attempts. Revised delivery must pass
the real suite again. This feedback is not LLM review or PASS. Persisted feedback
can recover idempotently after a crash before its callback, including semantic-only
nodes, after rechecking the latest result, true suite/source/receipt bindings,
current authority and remaining original budgets. Recovery issues no model review
request and cannot replay unknown actions. Callback errors and fake success remain
blocked. The [local/Mock recovery group](docs/audit/phase2/semantic-recovery-20261115T090801.xml)
passed 74 tests; it does not establish live task correctness.

Worker lease renewal occurs between settled steps after checking the current
token/generation, approvals and running Quest. It is capped by the task deadline
and cannot revive expired ownership, a paused/cancelled assignment or a changed
plan. Individual calls retain their current lease/deadline bound.

An approved dependent Worker may read a bounded receipt from a successful direct
predecessor only when its plan node, approved role and effective Worker tool
scope all permit `worker_read_action_receipt`. Its initial context contains at
most 32 upstream references and an omission indicator; a reference is not proof
until the read checks the current plan and receipt provenance. Returned content
remains untrusted and retains the source execution mode (`live` or `mock`); a
mock receipt is not promoted to live evidence. Completion rechecks the recorded
tool result. Temporary capacity pressure queues work without treating it as a
semantic failure retry. Lease generations fence ownership; the separate bounded
failure-retry count is recorded by retry events, and authorization retries do
not consume that failure limit.

Model calls through the Gateway share a durable admission ledger, including Router, planner, team composer, benchmark and Worker calls. Configure these trusted process environment variables before enabling a provider:

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `FORGE_MODEL_TOKEN_LIMIT` | Total token reservation ceiling; defaults to `0`, which rejects model calls until explicitly configured. |
| `FORGE_MODEL_CONCURRENCY_LIMIT` | Concurrent admitted attempts; defaults to `1`. |
| `FORGE_MODEL_REMOTE_MAX_SECONDS` | Optional trusted upper bound on remote execution duration. Without one, an attempt with unknown outcome retains its concurrency slot; a client timeout alone cannot establish that remote execution stopped. |
| `FORGE_MODEL_SCOPE_LIMITS_JSON` | Optional array of `{"scope":"quest","scope_id":"<quest-id>","token_limit":10000,"concurrency_limit":1}` entries; scope may be `workspace`, `quest`, or `worker`. Approved task contracts also impose their own limits. |
| `FORGE_PRICE_BOUNDS_JSON` | Optional operator-provided provider/model price ceilings. Unknown prices remain unknown; token-only admission applies when no cost ceiling is configured. |
| `FORGE_MODEL_COST_LIMIT_MICROUNITS`, `FORGE_MODEL_COST_CURRENCY` | Optional global currency ceiling and three-letter currency; both require trusted price bounds and reconciled historical cost. |
| `FORGE_MODEL_HISTORICAL_COST_MICROUNITS` | Operator-reconciled pre-cutover global cost in the configured currency. Unknown historical cost is never assumed to be zero. |
| `FORGE_MODEL_SCOPE_COST_RECONCILIATIONS_JSON` | Optional array of `{"scope":"quest","scope_id":"<quest-id>","currency":"USD","cost_microunits":0}` entries for operator-reconciled historical scope cost. |

An unknown or interrupted remote outcome remains reserved until a trusted remote execution bound and isolation period permit recovery. Without a trusted bound the slot remains reserved; there is currently no operator interface for reconciling an individual unknown attempt. Do not infer that a timeout cancelled the remote request. Current real-provider demonstrations and reproducible research scripts are described in the [M5 report](docs/PHASE1_MILESTONE5_REPORT.md).

### Backend checks

```powershell
# From backend, after installing .[dev]
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ruff check src tests scripts --config pyproject.toml
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ruff format --check src tests scripts
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip check
```

`python-dotenv` is an explicit runtime dependency for Workspace configuration. No model provider or external Agent execution backend is required for these checks.

## Desktop UI setup

Node 22.18+ is required for the desktop test runner's native TypeScript stripping;
the current Windows checks use Node 24.19.0.

```bash
cd desktop
npm install
npm test
npm run build
npm run dev
```

The React/Vite UI can run in browser mode for development. The Tauri shell and Core bootstrap are being integrated; a final native integration and packaging pass is required before calling it a desktop release.

## API quick smoke test

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8765/health
# Authenticated requests require the per-session bearer described above.
```

## Start Codex

### Entire session checkpoints

This repository uses Entire CLI 0.13.4 with the ref-based checkpoint backend
and telemetry disabled. On Windows, install the stable CLI using the [official
PowerShell installation instructions](https://docs.entire.com/installation),
then restart the terminal if the installer updates PATH. The non-Scoop default
installation location is `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin`; a custom installation can
use any suitable directory on PATH. Verify with `entire version`.

Enable Entire in the repository with `entire enable` and install the Codex agent
hooks as directed by the [official agent setup](https://docs.entire.com/agents/setup).
Codex must support hooks and any applicable hook-trust approval must be granted
before hooks run. Enabling without history import begins tracking new sessions;
it does not import previous conversations. With this repository's ref backend
and automatic push policy, checkpoint refs are pushed with Git pushes. The
shared settings retain Betterleaks' default scanner and add a generic 32-hex
pattern plus email and phone redaction. Redaction has limits: never put provider
credentials or other secrets into chat; use the configured credential store or
protected environment instead.

The locally verified Codex 0.139.0 supports six of the seven hooks generated by
Entire 0.13.4, and those six have been trusted. Its `SessionEnd` event is not
supported by this Codex version, so Entire may still report one hook needing
approval. The official seven-hook template is retained; after upgrading to a
Codex version that supports this event, review hook trust again via `/hooks`.
This limitation does not prevent the six supported hooks or Git hooks from
working.

Open this folder as the project root and first read:

1. `docs/PRODUCT_ARCHITECTURE.md`
2. `docs/DOMAIN_AND_LIFECYCLE.md`
3. `docs/ROUTER_AND_WORKER_PROTOCOL.md`
4. `docs/MODEL_REGISTRY_AND_TEAM_COMPOSITION.md`
5. `docs/CONTEXT_MEMORY_GOVERNANCE.md`
6. `docs/ROADMAP.md`
7. `codex/MASTER_PROMPT.md`

Follow the user's continuous development authorization and the acceptance gates in `docs/STATUS.md`. The referenced `codex/MASTER_PROMPT.md` remains missing from the supplied release.

## Native desktop build (after Rust toolchain installation)

```bash
cd desktop
npm install
npm run tauri dev
```

The Tauri Rust shell and v2 capability manifest are included. Preliminary native startup has been observed on Windows; final target-OS integration and packaging checks remain pending.
