9. Permit artifact replacement only with explicitly approved `file_revise`, the same current Worker's latest successful receipt chain, unchanged file hash and current workspace grant. Recheck the chain and latest bytes at review/completion; retain immutable prior versions. Existing create-only contracts gain no permission.
10. Keep parser/fixed-suite revision feedback distinguishable from LLM review or PASS. Bind semantic failure to the actual suite/report/source/receipt and latest delivery, require explicit revision authority and remaining original budgets with no unresolved actions/calls, and rerun the real suite after repair. Charge settled truncated reviews before bounded retry; never reset cumulative budgets or replay unknown remote outcomes. Lease renewal must retain fencing, current authority and the original task deadline.

## Known limits

V7 guidance covers new intermediate JSON artifacts and delivery_review handoffs with downstream consumers
toward about 4 KiB (at most 6 KiB) only when all assigned requirements fit. Complete code, final reports
and required detailed schemas remain full even when larger. This is soft writing
guidance: no stored artifact is truncated, no hard report-size gate is added, and
original packet/PASS/source/raw/context/evidence requirements remain unchanged.
Planner guidance recommends about two model contexts of cumulative allocation for
a source-heavy entry node, when the task ceiling permits, and at least ten percent
coordination reserve within the original total. V8 removes the fixed intermediate-output
preference and preserves enough per-call output for complete schema-valid tool
arguments and delivery. Shared source citation IDs avoid repeating full hashes while
preserving exact references.
New/replacement team proposals and approval enforce a trusted operator concurrency
cap; existing approved teams and historical evidence retain their contracts. Core
supplies Composer and WorkerManager the Worker concurrency cap `2`, independently
of the Gateway model-call concurrency cap. Both resource limits remain enforced.
The live harness takes the smaller CLI/scenario total-token and concurrency limits
and records the effective values. V8/v9 full/live outcomes are recorded; final post-v10 verification remains pending.


For new native TeamWire proposals, only explicit `output_schema_json=null`
selects a deep copy of `STRICT_DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA`: the model must supply
all eight delivery fields and confidence within 0–1, with no Core-inserted defaults.
The contract is checked under any node criterion through JSON Schema and bounded
repair. Legacy/default direct RoleSpec contracts and explicit older schemas retain
their original meaning; historical approvals/results are unchanged. Non-finite
JSON values are rejected through the existing bounded repair path. Strict structure
does not establish semantic correctness or replace review/evidence gates.

V8 removes the intermediate output_tokens=2048 preference: per-call output must
fit complete schema-valid tool arguments and delivery. Worker instructions cover
the current node's approved objective, role and criteria; downstream nodes retain
their own deliverables. Planner guidance uses one node only when the entire task
is simple read-only analysis and preserves explicitly requested specialist/count
requirements. Composer guidance preserves unique role IDs and correct specialties,
and prefers max_steps=16 only when the user's ceiling permits. Native Core configures
a shared self-repair/review-revision maximum of four; existing counters, original
steps/tokens/tools/cost/time and review-round limits still bind every attempt.
Worker concurrency two remains independent of Gateway model-call concurrency.

V9 rejects a generated node with a concrete artifact verifier unless that same
node already permits `file_write`; feedback uses the original bounded Planner
schema-repair path and inserts no tool authority. Worker requests with an effective per-request allowance ≥8192 show remaining
model steps, tool calls and cumulative tokens, and point to integrity-bound archived
source_refs/current artifact receipts. This guides reuse of evidence without
assuming the repeated-read cause is proved. A tool batch exceeding remaining calls
is rejected before any tool executes and may use the existing bounded repair path;
the settled model attempt stays charged. Original tool/step/token/cost/time and
repair/round limits remain unchanged. Publisher adds numeric retry totals/breakdown
and allowlisted review reason/context fields; prompt/reply/log/artifact bodies stay
excluded, and missing historical fields remain unknown/null. V9 full/live
outcomes are recorded below; final post-v10 complex continuity remains pending.

The [v9 full suite](audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v9.xml) / [log](audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v9.log)
passed 895 tests with one warning in 237.83 seconds. Its [157-file manifest](audit/phase2/source-manifest-v9.json)
is `9a33b199404b777428ff0f0e1a1c1da356ad93b23b4395565fc0d211b3d9203a`;
Ruff, formatting for 154 Python files and pip checks passed. This predates v10.
[Offline benchmark v9](audit/phase2/benchmark-final-v9.json), `benchmark_c4387a6e26ac`,
completed in 5.9372256 seconds with zero Provider calls on the same fixed dataset.

The v9 live runs share snapshot
`624f0ac7cb1873163e2e0a5b1849642bb363d553aedab4331096a0286b134db8`.
L2 `20261115T021801Z-L2-b11011` failed in 80.141 seconds: 17 model/six tool
calls, charged input/output 65,607/9,348 tokens, unknown zero.
L3 `20261115T021801Z-L3-290b7f` failed in 97.584 seconds: 18 model/six tool
calls, charged 71,908/14,522 tokens, one unresolved Router-notice reservation
of 9,985+4,096; total actual usage and cost remain unknown.
Actual receipt-bound intermediate artifacts were 15,235/10,788 bytes respectively.
Read-only reconstruction produced raw packets of 68,207/68,967 bytes, exceeding
the unchanged 65,536 cap. Both retained `review_packet_too_large`, zero
`review.started`, the first Worker at `review_pending`, no successor and no restart.

All 39 finished driver records are safely published in
[snapshot-v2](audit/phase2/live-runs/snapshot-v2/index.json), with original run records and
diagnostic-snapshot-v1 preserved. Publication makes no Provider call and does not
promote failed or unaccepted tasks. Historical retry totals can overlap: the old
`worker_runs.repairs` includes review revisions. V10 counts actual self-repair
events separately and marks future records `retry_accounting=disjoint_event_counts_v2`;
[27 focused regressions](audit/phase2/retry-accounting-v10-fixed.xml) pass, while original
run counters remain unchanged. Final v10 full/live verification is pending;
Core capacity feedback is not independent model review or PASS. The proposed
pre-stop read-only settlement wait also awaits integration/full/live verification.


- Router/Planner repair is bounded once; autonomous plans cap at eight nodes/sixteen edges. General remaining-DAG replanning and arbitrary hierarchical Agent expansion are incomplete.
- Goal updates/new DAG proposals accept only proposed/awaiting-approval Quests. Team replacement preserves the current DAG; it does not implement autonomous replanning of a running DAG.
- Cumulative Worker/review token allowance is distinct from the per-request context/output bound; both remain enforced, along with approved node/team limits. Bounded Quest identity recall is separate from ordinary fact/constraint recall; true identity omissions/cursors and multiple candidates still require clarification.
- Dynamic team changes retain completed nodes and require approval. Performance snapshots are bounded, sourced and sample-counted; the current five-observation eligibility threshold does not establish statistical sufficiency or automatically learned general capability.
- Independent review uses the same approved underlying model in a fresh context. It evaluates the current node's objective, criteria and approved role; full original requirements still govern nodes assigned final deliverables. Independent model diversity is not implemented. `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` defaults to two and accepts integers one through four; the live harness selects three within its scenario's three-round cap, without changing historical runs. Output fits 8192, role/model caps, remaining context and the original cumulative token allowance, with adaptive floor `min(1024, original output cap)`. Inability to fit that floor or original cost authority fails closed; lower original caps remain valid. Native input reservation uses the actual serialized Gateway schema/reasoning payload and matches admission. Labelled Core JSON-parser revision feedback supplies no LLM review or PASS. Legacy/default delivery compatibility requires only `summary`, while `delivery_review` requires all eight fields.
- A lossless review envelope can remove duplicate escaping/schema/constraint metadata while preserving full source text, exact source spans and the original packet/PASS hash. It changes representation, not context or evidence limits. Oversized packets, model-context overflow and exhausted budgets still block. Published runtime settings use an explicit whitelist including effective model token/concurrency limits; missing legacy values remain null.
- Router/Worker archives have bounded highlights, preserve original-source recovery and signal omissions. Active-Quest snapshots, indexing batches, evidence/receipt pages and model windows remain finite. Long histories can require multiple reads or fail closed.
- Constraint literal extraction and potential-conflict dimensions are bounded heuristics. User/model provenance does not prove domain facts or grant action approval. Confirmation/revocation have Core operations but no new public interface in this sprint.
- Recall uses bounded lexical terms, bilingual aliases and source/Quest/time/type filters. Learned semantic retrieval, general relevance and arbitrary-scale memory are not established.
- Worker execution tools are fixed: `python_compile` checks syntax, `numeric_ast` runs a bounded pure numeric subset and `shell_inspect` permits `python_version`. Arbitrary shell, unrestricted Python, arbitrary test runners and a general code patch tool are absent.
- `file_write` remains exclusive-create. Explicitly approved `file_revise` only replaces the current Worker's own latest produced artifact with receipt-chain/hash checks and immutable version history; user files, predecessor artifacts, stale versions and uncertain outcomes are excluded. General repository patch/test loops remain incomplete, and all revision must preserve the original approved criteria.
- Worker leases renew only between settled steps for a valid current owner, bounded by the task deadline. Expired/stale claims, changed plans, competing owners and paused/cancelled assignments cannot be revived; calls remain capped by the current lease/deadline and unknown outcomes retain reservations.
- Fixed semantic-suite feedback is deterministic Core validation, not independent LLM review. Persisted feedback before callback can recover once after restart, including semantic-only nodes, only after current result/semantic/source/receipt, scope/grant and original-budget checks with no unsettled actions or model attempts. It issues no model-review request; stale sources, revoked authority, exhausted budgets, unknown actions and callback errors remain blocked. This does not establish arbitrary in-flight recovery.
- ACP is a typed projection of durable events with task identities and fenced ownership; exhaustive payload contracts remain partial. Unknown external effects and unresolved model attempts may conservatively block progress until trusted settlement is possible.
- Team/context/governance benchmarks use small deterministic cases, synthetic profiles, fixed extractive summaries and byte budgets. Same-budget real task quality, measured token/cost savings, independent LLM governance quality and statistical generalization remain open.
- SQLite migration/restart tests do not establish production durability under every failure mode. Packaged Windows Alpha, full native lifecycle, credential vault and backup/restore integration remain outside this sprint's completed evidence.

## Historical verification

Phase 1 reports retain their original results and limitations. In particular, the
[M3 report](PHASE1_MILESTONE3_REPORT.md) records 140 local/Mock tests at that stage;
later bounded real-provider observations are in M5/M6 and the Phase 2 protocol probe.
Earlier native/UI checks and dependency audits do not establish final packaging or
cross-platform safety. Never describe a proposed Worker as a running Worker.

## Reproduction and live acceptance contract

From `backend`, using the existing virtual environment, write to a new output path:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/phase2/intelligence_benchmark.py --output 'D:\path\to\new-benchmark.json'
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/phase2/retrieval_evaluation.py --output 'D:\path\to\new-retrieval.json'
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/test_constraints_phase2.py tests/test_context_m6.py tests/test_memory_m6.py tests/test_router_intelligence_phase2.py -q
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/test_phase2_driver.py -q
```

Scripts reject overwriting historical outputs. No new production dependency or
environment variable is introduced by the offline benchmark. Live scripts require a
protected process credential reference and finite budget; credentials must not appear
in arguments, output records or source. `verify_provider.py` accepts `--credential-env`;
`live_e2e.py` reads the process-only `FORGE_PROVIDER_KEY_LIVE_TEST` variable. Supply its
value through a protected process input method. Do not place a value in shell history.

Process-only `FORGE_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` defaults to 30 seconds and accepts a
finite value greater than 0 through 600. `FORGE_PROVIDER_MAX_RETRIES` defaults to 1
and accepts integers 0–3. `FORGE_WORKER_LEASE_SECONDS` defaults to 60 and accepts
finite values greater than 0 through 600. The current live harness selects a
120-second Provider timeout, a 150-second Worker lease and zero additional retries
after the retained Composer timeout diagnostic. Valid owners renew only between
settled steps, within the task deadline and existing authority. Every actual
attempt still requires Gateway admission; an unknown remote result stays reserved.

`FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` defaults to 2 and accepts integers 1–4. The current
acceptance harness explicitly selects 3 within its scenario cap of 3. Historical

README.md:7:Phase 2 Agent Intelligence is in progress. The existing native runtime now connects a separate Planner, source-bound constraints and bounded memory, observation-informed team proposals, fresh-context independent review and typed durable Agent coordination. One retained strict L1 live run passed with review revision and Worker self-repair, without compaction or restart; the concurrent L2 and later L3 attempts failed. Later L2/L3 reruns also failed before review at packet/context and cumulative-budget limits. The [v5 full backend suite](docs/audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v5.xml) passed 820 tests with one warning in 219.96 seconds, before later v6 changes. The [v6 full suite](docs/audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v6.xml) retained 848 passed, one failed, one warning / 283.77 seconds; all three v6 live reruns failed. V7 corrects independent Worker/Gateway concurrency and extends bounded handoff/budget guidance. The [v7 full suite](docs/audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v7.xml) passed 849 tests / one warning / 216.87 seconds, while all three v7 live attempts failed. The [v8 full suite](docs/audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v8.xml) passed 886 tests / one warning / 283.46 seconds; all three v8 live attempts failed, despite real review/revision and Worker archiving in L1/L2. L1/L2 each retain an unresolved Router-notice attempt and no mid-execution Core restart occurred. The v9 full suite passed 895 tests / one warning / 237.83 seconds; both v9 L2/L3 live runs still failed before review at the unchanged raw-packet cap. Thirty-nine finished driver records are published without changing original outcomes. The v10 full suite passed 915 tests / one warning / 279.54 seconds, while all three v10 strict live attempts failed. L2 did demonstrate actual research PASS, a settled mid-execution Core restart with two-source Router archive/readback and preserved counters, followed by architect continuation; the successor later blocked on the original receipt-read bound. Forty-two driver records are now published. V11 receipt recovery/Planner budget changes and final complex-task acceptance remain pending. The local Provider's small live protocol probes passed [11/11 with the proxy default](docs/audit/phase2/provider-probe.json) and [10/11 with explicit `reasoning_effort=none`](docs/audit/phase2/provider-probe-reasoning-none.json); the latter retained a failed exact-text dialogue check. Focused local/Mock suites and exploratory synthetic benchmarks are recorded separately. See the [Phase 2 report](docs/PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md), [status](docs/PHASE2_STATUS.md), [experiments](docs/PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md) and [architecture decision](docs/adr/ADR-009-agent-intelligence-contracts-and-review.md).

- Router/Planner repair is bounded once; autonomous plans cap at eight nodes/sixteen edges. General remaining-DAG replanning and arbitrary hierarchical Agent expansion are incomplete.
- Goal updates/new DAG proposals accept only proposed/awaiting-approval Quests. Team replacement preserves the current DAG; it does not implement autonomous replanning of a running DAG.
- Cumulative Worker/review token allowance is distinct from the per-request context/output bound; both remain enforced, along with approved node/team limits. Bounded Quest identity recall is separate from ordinary fact/constraint recall; true identity omissions/cursors and multiple candidates still require clarification.
- Dynamic team changes retain completed nodes and require approval. Performance snapshots are bounded, sourced and sample-counted; the current five-observation eligibility threshold does not establish statistical sufficiency or automatically learned general capability.
- Independent review uses the same approved underlying model in a fresh context. It evaluates the current node's objective, criteria and approved role; full original requirements still govern nodes assigned final deliverables. Independent model diversity is not implemented. `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` defaults to two and accepts integers one through four; the live harness selects three within its scenario's three-round cap, without changing historical runs. Output fits 8192, role/model caps, remaining context and the original cumulative token allowance, with adaptive floor `min(1024, original output cap)`. Inability to fit that floor or original cost authority fails closed; lower original caps remain valid. Native input reservation uses the actual serialized Gateway schema/reasoning payload and matches admission. Labelled Core JSON-parser revision feedback supplies no LLM review or PASS. Legacy/default delivery compatibility requires only `summary`, while `delivery_review` requires all eight fields.
- A lossless review envelope can remove duplicate escaping/schema/constraint metadata while preserving full source text, exact source spans and the original packet/PASS hash. It changes representation, not context or evidence limits. Oversized packets, model-context overflow and exhausted budgets still block. Published runtime settings use an explicit whitelist including effective model token/concurrency limits; missing legacy values remain null.
- Router/Worker archives have bounded highlights, preserve original-source recovery and signal omissions. Active-Quest snapshots, indexing batches, evidence/receipt pages and model windows remain finite. Long histories can require multiple reads or fail closed.
- Constraint literal extraction and potential-conflict dimensions are bounded heuristics. User/model provenance does not prove domain facts or grant action approval. Confirmation/revocation have Core operations but no new public interface in this sprint.
- Recall uses bounded lexical terms, bilingual aliases and source/Quest/time/type filters. Learned semantic retrieval, general relevance and arbitrary-scale memory are not established.
- Worker execution tools are fixed: `python_compile` checks syntax, `numeric_ast` runs a bounded pure numeric subset and `shell_inspect` permits `python_version`. Arbitrary shell, unrestricted Python, arbitrary test runners and a general code patch tool are absent.
- `file_write` remains exclusive-create. Explicitly approved `file_revise` only replaces the current Worker's own latest produced artifact with receipt-chain/hash checks and immutable version history; user files, predecessor artifacts, stale versions and uncertain outcomes are excluded. General repository patch/test loops remain incomplete, and all revision must preserve the original approved criteria.
- Worker leases renew only between settled steps for a valid current owner, bounded by the task deadline. Expired/stale claims, changed plans, competing owners and paused/cancelled assignments cannot be revived; calls remain capped by the current lease/deadline and unknown outcomes retain reservations.
- Fixed semantic-suite feedback is deterministic Core validation, not independent LLM review. Persisted feedback before callback can recover once after restart, including semantic-only nodes, only after current result/semantic/source/receipt, scope/grant and original-budget checks with no unsettled actions or model attempts. It issues no model-review request; stale sources, revoked authority, exhausted budgets, unknown actions and callback errors remain blocked. This does not establish arbitrary in-flight recovery.
- ACP is a typed projection of durable events with task identities and fenced ownership; exhaustive payload contracts remain partial. Unknown external effects and unresolved model attempts may conservatively block progress until trusted settlement is possible.
- Team/context/governance benchmarks use small deterministic cases, synthetic profiles, fixed extractive summaries and byte budgets. Same-budget real task quality, measured token/cost savings, independent LLM governance quality and statistical generalization remain open.
- SQLite migration/restart tests do not establish production durability under every failure mode. Packaged Windows Alpha, full native lifecycle, credential vault and backup/restore integration remain outside this sprint's completed evidence.

## Historical verification

Phase 1 reports retain their original results and limitations. In particular, the
[M3 report](PHASE1_MILESTONE3_REPORT.md) records 140 local/Mock tests at that stage;
later bounded real-provider observations are in M5/M6 and the Phase 2 protocol probe.
Earlier native/UI checks and dependency audits do not establish final packaging or
cross-platform safety. Never describe a proposed Worker as a running Worker.

# Phase 2 — Actual Agent Execution Chain Audit

Date: 2026-11-15 (Asia/Shanghai). Branch: `codex/phase1-continuous`.
This is a source/retained-evidence audit of the evolving Phase 2 working tree, not a
frozen acceptance result. Root is the unique integration owner. Phase 1 M1–M7 reports,
the M7 backend-hardening report, required architecture/protocol documents, and the
named Router/Worker/team/graph/dispatcher/context/memory/provider/tool/evidence/
governance modules were read. Earlier audits under `_audit/` describe the pre-change
state; conclusions below include the current Phase 2 changes.

## Executable chain

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    U[One main user conversation] --> R[Persistent Router: observe, recall, strict decision]
    R -->|chat| A[One user-facing response]
    R -->|create Quest and durable quest.proposed| D[Dispatcher: outbox, leases, inbox, dedup]
    D --> P[Separate Planner: original request, constraints, strict bounded DAG]
    P --> PA[Pending plan: digest, revision, criteria, dependencies]
    PA -->|authenticated local user approves| C[Composer: model profiles, online observations, hard budgets]
    C --> TA[Pending team: roles and models decoupled]
    TA -->|authenticated local user approves| S[WorkerScheduler: ready nodes and concurrency]
    S --> W[Native Worker: private context, model/tool loop, checkpoints]
    W --> T[ToolEngine: policy, grants, exact approvals, intent and receipt]
    T --> W
    W -->|structured worker.result| V[Fresh independent review context]
    V -->|NEEDS_REVISION with concrete goals| RW[Bounded revision of same approved assignment]
    RW --> W
    V -->|PASS| N[NodeVerifier: current provenance and fixed criteria checks]
    N --> G[CompletionGate: recheck approved plan, receipts and evidence]
    G --> Q[Verified task and Quest transitions]
    Q --> D
    D --> RN[Router notice: silent or user progress/result update]
    RN --> A
    W -->|help or blocker event| D
    D -->|help: pending approved replacement proposal| C
    X[ProviderGateway and durable admission ledger] -. all model calls .-> R
    X -.-> P
    X -.-> C
    X -.-> W
    X -.-> V
    M[Task capsules, constraints, source archives and memory] -. bounded context .-> R
    M -. original source recovery .-> W
```

`forge_api.main._core_lifespan` starts six background loops: Dispatcher, Router notices,
Planner, Composer, WorkerScheduler, and review/verification. Provider latency runs
outside SQLite write transactions. A proposal is not an approved plan, an approved
team, a running Worker or a completed task.

1. `RouterService.handle_user_message` synchronizes memory, observes a bounded snapshot,
   calls the configured Gateway, validates `RouterDecision`, and permits one bounded
   schema-repair request. The final user/assistant messages, Quest, source constraints,
   events and idempotent turn record commit atomically. Chat creates no Quest/Worker.
2. `process_pending_plan` consumes the durable creation event. `QuestGraphService.generate`
   receives the original user-message ID/content with its hash, sourced constraints,
   offered tool catalogue and capability names. Generated plans are limited to eight
   nodes/sixteen edges; invalid names/graphs receive one repair opportunity. `propose`
   persists the DAG; `approve` binds authenticated actor, revision, digest and version.
3. `process_pending_team` proposes bounded role contracts. `TeamComposerEngine.compose`
   filters tool/context/cost/budget incompatibilities and offers single-model, greedy,
   coverage and complementarity search. `performance_snapshot` supplies separate,
   source-digested live/Mock observations with sample counts and Wilson intervals for
   rates; it does not rewrite manually supplied capability scores or infer task success
   from transport success. Team approval binds the plan and selected profile hashes.
4. `WorkerScheduler.tick` launches only approved, ready assignments. `WorkerManager.start`
   checks dependencies, effective tool scope, model identity and token/tool/time/agent/
   depth/concurrency limits. `_run` owns a native checkpointed model/tool loop. `_repair`
   preserves failed diagnostics and bounded repair history; provider, contract, budget,
   dependency, authorization, code and tool failures have distinct classifications.
5. `ToolEngine.prepare/execute` enforces current permissions before action, persists an
   exact intent and records its receipt. R1 writes require a Workspace grant; R2 requires
   exact action approval and operator allowlists; unknown/R3 actions fail closed.
   Separately approved `file_revise` can atomically replace only the same Worker's
   own latest artifact after receipt-chain/hash and current authority checks; immutable
   intents and receipts preserve old content. Existing create-only contracts gain no tool.
   Uncertain external effects are not silently repeated after restart or reassignment.
6. `IndependentReviewService` constructs a fresh packet from the original contract,
   criteria, structured delivery, actual bounded artifacts and trustworthy receipts.
   Judgment covers the current node's objective, criteria and approved role. The
   original request stays complete; nodes assigned final deliverables retain all
   original requirements, while intermediate research retains its read-only scope.
   It does not copy the Worker's private conversation. It currently uses the same
   approved underlying model in a separate context: independent context is not model
   diversity. PASS/NEEDS_REVISION/REJECT/BLOCKED are schema-checked; revision requires
   concrete goals and has a default two-round limit, hard maximum four.
   Large review inputs use a lossless envelope of complete untrusted source blocks,
   exact original-message constraint spans and shared repeated metadata; the original
   `_packet` and PASS hash bindings remain unchanged. Full source text and review
   criteria remain, with unchanged context limits; the [118-case input group](review-context-20261115T091955.xml)
   is local/Mock evidence, with larger over-limit packets still rejected.
   Labelled Core JSON-parser errors can request revision without claiming an LLM review or PASS.
   Settled truncated reviews retain actual charges before a bounded fresh verdict;
   output fits 8192, role/model caps, remaining context and the original cumulative
   token remainder, with adaptive floor `min(1024, original output cap)`. Native
   reservation uses the actual serialized schema/reasoning payload and matches
   Gateway admission; insufficient capacity or original cost authority fails closed.
   Budget/source bindings persist,
   and a committed revision verdict can requeue idempotently after restart.
7. `NodeVerifier` requires the applicable fresh PASS, then performs fixed JSON or numeric
   semantic verification. A genuine failed fixed numeric report may produce labelled
   `deterministic_semantic_validation` feedback for the same Worker's governed revision,

Integration owner: root agent. **Phase 2 is in progress. One strict L1 run passed;
L2/L3 acceptance and final frozen-source verification remain incomplete.**

## Scope and architectural change

This sprint moves the existing backend toward autonomous task execution. Desktop
visual changes, packaging and the deferred M7 desktop Alpha are outside this sprint's
acceptance. Existing Phase 1 reports and failed experiments remain preserved.

The source audit and complete execution diagram are in the
[execution-chain audit](audit/phase2/execution-chain-audit.md). The minimum change is
recorded in [ADR 009](adr/ADR-009-agent-intelligence-contracts-and-review.md):

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    U[One user conversation] --> R[Persistent Router]
    R --> P[Separate Planner and proposed DAG]
    P --> A[Authenticated plan and team approval]
    A --> W[Native private Worker loops]
    W --> T[Governed tools and receipts]
    T --> V[Fresh independent review]
    V -->|concrete revision goals| W
    V --> N[NodeVerifier and CompletionGate]
    N --> R
```

All model requests use the existing Gateway and durable admission ledger. The
Router remains the only user-facing Agent. Workers, reviewers and durable events
do not create extra user conversations or use another Agent product as a backend.

## Implemented mechanisms

| Area | Current behavior | Verification boundary |

| Native Worker | Private model/tool loop, checkpoints, fenced lease renewal between settled steps, bounded repair, distinct failure categories and structured delivery | One earlier strict L1 pass with self-repair; v8 failed L1/L2 show actual Worker archives and NEEDS_REVISION, without mid-execution Core restart; v10 L2 shows settled restart/Router archive/readback and architect continuation before later receipt-read block; whole-task continuity pending |
| Artifact revision | Separately approved R1 `file_revise` atomically replaces the same Worker's own latest produced artifact using an intact receipt chain and unchanged hash | Local/Mock race, provenance and immutable-history checks; general repository editing remains absent |
| Independent review | Fresh packet from original goal, criteria, real artifacts and receipts; PASS/NEEDS_REVISION/REJECT/BLOCKED; concrete revision goals, default two-round limit, hard maximum four | Current same approved underlying model in a separate context; independent model diversity is absent |
| Evidence gate | Review provenance plus fixed semantic verifiers and final receipt/artifact/approval checks govern completion | Mock/adversarial regressions and actual local tool checks; self-report never establishes live completion |
| Context and constraints | Bounded Router/Worker highlights, original-source readback, sourced literal/pending/confirmed clauses, potential conflicts, expiry and revocation | 53 combined Router/Planner/context/memory tests; 9 exploratory synthetic source-identity cases |

The delivery vocabulary contains `summary`, `findings`, `decisions`, `artifacts`,
`evidence_references`, `unresolved_issues`, `confidence` and `next_actions`.
`delivery_review` enforces all eight. Legacy/default compatibility schemas still
require only `summary`; missing fields are not evidence of completed work.

For new native TeamWire proposals, only explicit `output_schema_json=null`
selects a deep copy of `STRICT_DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA`: the model must supply
all eight delivery fields and confidence within 0–1, with no Core-inserted defaults.
The contract is checked under any node criterion through JSON Schema and bounded
repair. Legacy/default direct RoleSpec contracts and explicit older schemas retain
their original meaning; historical approvals/results are unchanged. Non-finite
JSON values are rejected through the existing bounded repair path. Strict structure
does not establish semantic correctness or replace review/evidence gates.

`file_write` remains create-only. `file_revise` requires explicit plan/node and
team authority plus a workspace grant, with `path`, `prior_receipt_id`,
`expected_sha256` and full replacement `content`. It checks the latest successful
same-Worker receipt, current file bytes and authority immediately before atomic
replacement. Immutable intent parameters and receipts retain every prior version.
Review and read-only acceptance validate the bounded revision chain (at most 64
receipts) before comparing current bytes with the latest successful version.
Predecessor artifacts, user files, stale hashes and unsettled outcomes are excluded;
old create-only contracts acquire no additional authority.

Reviewer output is capped by 8192, the approved role/model caps, remaining model
context and original cumulative Worker tokens. Adaptive capacity keeps a floor of
`min(1024, original output cap)`; inability to fit that floor or original cost
limits fails closed. Native Gateway input reservation uses the actual serialized
payload, including schema/reasoning settings, and matches Core admission.
Review evaluates the current node's objective, criteria and approved role; an
intermediate read-only researcher is not asked to produce a downstream writer's
artifact. Nodes assigned final deliverables retain all original requirements.
`FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` defaults to two and accepts integers one through four;
the live harness explicitly selects three within its scenario's three-round cap.
Existing runs retain their original review limits and results.
Large packets can use a lossless wire envelope while the original `_packet` and
PASS `packet_sha256` stay unchanged. Full `file_read` source text appears once in
untrusted blocks bound to receipt references, text SHA256 and UTF-8 lengths.
Repeated constraint metadata uses shared fields; a statement already present
verbatim in an original/update message uses that same source's exact Unicode
`[start,end)` span, otherwise its full text remains. Native structured-output
requests retain the Gateway schema while avoiding a duplicate system-prompt copy.
The original L2 fixture packet was 56,755 bytes: its old conservative reserve was
73,065, the review-envelope estimate is 64,622 and actual local
`ProviderGateway._payload` construction reserves 64,245, within the same 65,536
context ceiling. All three source texts remain complete. This construction made
no network call, changed no historical run and establishes admission only for
that exact fixture; larger packets still fail closed when limits are exceeded.
Receipt-bound JSON syntax errors produce concrete line/column and receipt/hash
feedback labelled `deterministic_artifact_validation` / `core_json_parser`, with
`NEEDS_REVISION` only while repair/round/step/token/deadline limits permit, otherwise
`BLOCKED`. This is a Core-parser result, with no fictional model call or PASS.
A truncated model verdict can be retried only after exact admitted/settled usage
is reconciled (or under explicitly labelled Mock tests). `review.response_rejected`
records `reason_code=truncated`; actual usage remains charged, subsequent rounds
consume the same budgets, and unknown remote outcomes are not replayed. A committed
revision verdict can be requeued idempotently after restart.

The fixed numeric verifier has a separate feedback path: a genuine failed
`scheduler-v1` subprocess report can emit `review.result` with
`review_context=deterministic_semantic_validation` and
`validation_source=core_fixed_numeric_suite`. It binds the latest delivery,
Quest/plan/revision/Worker/run, actual semantic run, receipt, source and report
hashes, with at most ten failed-case diagnostics. Requeue calls the same Worker's
revision handler only when graph/node/Worker/member tool scopes explicitly permit
`file_revise`, a current grant exists, repair/step/token/tool/cost/deadline budgets
remain and no action or Gateway attempt is unresolved. A new delivery and genuine
suite PASS are still required; deterministic feedback is no LLM verdict or PASS.
Duplicate result feedback is rejected. Callback errors or fake success fail closed;
a callback that committed before raising has its exact queued revision fenced.
Persisted semantic feedback can recover once after a crash before callback, including
semantic-only nodes, through `IndependentReviewService.tick()` without issuing a
model review. Recovery rechecks `revision_available=true`, actual semantic/source/
receipt and current execution bindings, current tool scopes/grants, tool/cost
headroom and absence of unsettled actions or Gateway attempts. The existing Worker
revision interface still checks the latest delivery, approved team, cumulative
repair/step/token/deadline limits and idempotent consumption. Stale or changed
sources, revoked authority, exhausted budgets and originally unavailable revision
events remain blocked. This does not recover an arbitrary external action.

Valid Worker owners renew between settled steps to the earlier of the task deadline
and `now + lease_seconds`. Renewal preserves token/generation fencing and current
plan/team/status checks; expired claims, competing owners and paused/cancelled or
changed-plan assignments fail closed. Each call still fits the current lease and
deadline. This is not an in-flight heartbeat or a larger task allocation.

Team token allowance and single-request context are separate bounds. A member's
`input_tokens + output_tokens` becomes its cumulative Worker/review allowance;
the allowance may span several context windows. Each request remains bounded by
the approved/current model context, remaining cumulative tokens and the per-response
output limit. Node/team/global approvals, cost ledgers and finite generation caps
remain in force; compaction and review do not refresh the allowance.
The node schema permits at most 1,000,000 cumulative tokens, matching the existing
graph ceiling; summed node allowances still fit the approved graph total. The
lower live scenario caps remain L1 180,000, L2 360,000 and L3 630,000. Existing
approvals are unchanged. See the [budget audit](audit/phase2/cumulative-budget-and-quest-identity.md)
for the distinction between this schema ceiling and an actual approved allocation.

Constraint provenance is separate from execution authority. Literal clauses are
`explicit_user`, model paraphrases are `pending_model`, and a distinct original
user confirmation can produce `user_confirmed`. Original IDs and hashes are checked;
potential conflicts are surfaced rather than silently resolved by recency.

Router archives keep at most 64 user highlights/12,288 UTF-8 bytes and 16 other
highlights/4,096 bytes. Worker highlights are trimmed to their actual input budget;
initial contracts and live tool pairs are protected. Per-Quest evidence and receipt
snapshots each cap at 64 and signal omissions. Original durable records remain
available for checked source readback. These bounds solve repeated full-history
injection, not unlimited context or storage.

A fully settled latest tool exchange may also leave the live message window when
its minimum pinned representation cannot fit, but only after a prior archive makes
the source-read tool available in the current request. The entire call/results
batch is archived together with explicit omitted/raw-readback/untrusted metadata,
same-run successful receipt bindings and original-source integrity. Pending or
uncertain tails and required initial contracts remain protected. The retained L2
failure's offline read-only backup reproduced the block, then fit 12,326 bytes
within the same 21,759-byte input budget with exact source readback and unchanged
budgets/evidence; the original live failure is preserved. [Sprint F](audit/phase2/sprint-f.md)
records the 97-case related regression group and diagnostic limits.

Quest identity recall separately selects actual task/Core Quest records, with at
most 100 returned items/65,536 bytes and the existing 512-candidate scan ceiling.
Omitted ordinary constraint/message facts do not by themselves imply an ambiguous
Quest when identity recall is complete. Multiple Quest IDs, identity result omissions
or a remaining candidate cursor still require clarification without an explicit
user-supplied Quest ID. Filtering after the candidate cap remains conservative.

98,513/160,000 left 61,487, insufficient for the guarded capacity revision plus
review floor, so Core issued `review_capacity_unrepairable` / BLOCKED. No Core
restart occurred. Its early unsettled-call stop label remains in history; the
final read-only wait observed settlement and the final ledger has unknown zero.
Retry totals under disjoint accounting are 0/0/2, with L3 one review revision and
one background-notice retry, zero Worker self-repairs and zero HTTP retries.

[Snapshot-v3](audit/phase2/live-runs/snapshot-v3/index.json) publishes 42 finished driver
records and preserves snapshot-v2/v1 plus original run records. Publication made
no Provider request and does not promote failed tasks. V11 is in progress:
bounded correction after a rejected local receipt read and byte/availability hints
have [79 focused passing cases](audit/phase2/receipt-read-repair-v11-tests.xml);
Planner operator-budget enforcement is under integration. V10 L3's model-generated
node budgets summed to 920,000 above its 630,000 scenario ceiling, while actual
Gateway admission always retained that hard ceiling. V11 full/live/final verification
is pending, and the general complex-task continuity acceptance is still incomplete.


The [retained v9 hint regression](audit/phase2/budget-feedback-intermediate-failure-v9.md)
records six legacy context failures after unconditional budget hints; interrupted
larger groups are not counted. Hints now require an effective per-request allowance
of at least 8192. The unchanged legacy file passed 48 cases / 15.81 seconds and
Planner/publication passed 36 / 3.64 seconds; the corrected combined
[66-case JUnit](audit/phase2/worker-budget-feedback-v9-fixed-tests.xml) has no failure.
These overlapping local/Mock groups are separate from the full suite and live runs.


## Reproduction and live acceptance contract

From `backend`, using the existing virtual environment, write to a new output path:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/phase2/intelligence_benchmark.py --output 'D:\path\to\new-benchmark.json'
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/phase2/retrieval_evaluation.py --output 'D:\path\to\new-retrieval.json'
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/test_constraints_phase2.py tests/test_context_m6.py tests/test_memory_m6.py tests/test_router_intelligence_phase2.py -q
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/test_phase2_driver.py -q
```

Scripts reject overwriting historical outputs. No new production dependency or
environment variable is introduced by the offline benchmark. Live scripts require a
protected process credential reference and finite budget; credentials must not appear
in arguments, output records or source. `verify_provider.py` accepts `--credential-env`;
`live_e2e.py` reads the process-only `FORGE_PROVIDER_KEY_LIVE_TEST` variable. Supply its
value through a protected process input method. Do not place a value in shell history.

Process-only `FORGE_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` defaults to 30 seconds and accepts a
finite value greater than 0 through 600. `FORGE_PROVIDER_MAX_RETRIES` defaults to 1
and accepts integers 0–3. `FORGE_WORKER_LEASE_SECONDS` defaults to 60 and accepts
finite values greater than 0 through 600. The current live harness selects a
120-second Provider timeout, a 150-second Worker lease and zero additional retries
after the retained Composer timeout diagnostic. Valid owners renew only between
settled steps, within the task deadline and existing authority. Every actual
attempt still requires Gateway admission; an unknown remote result stays reserved.

`FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` defaults to 2 and accepts integers 1–4. The current
acceptance harness explicitly selects 3 within its scenario cap of 3. Historical
runs keep their original round limits, approvals and outcomes; this setting does
not refresh cumulative budgets or retroactively turn failed reviews into passes.

An example live scenario invocation, after configuring that protected process variable:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/phase2/live_e2e.py --level L1 --scenario --restart-after-plan --token-limit 300000 --concurrency 2
```

`acceptance_scenarios.py` provides L1 actual registry/observation analysis inputs,
L2 bounded Router/Worker/Composer architecture inputs and L3 scheduler research/code/
experiment inputs. Descriptors include hashes and goals without seeded plans,
teams, approval, receipts or a hidden implementation. New artifacts are scoped to
`work/`. A plan-boundary restart alone cannot prove in-flight tool recovery.

These are requested scenario goals, not claims of completed runs. The current
Worker toolset permits file creation, syntax checks and bounded numeric AST
experiments; it supplies no unrestricted Python/test runner, arbitrary shell or
general code patch operation. `file_write` remains create-only. Explicitly approved
`file_revise` replaces only the current Worker's own latest artifact, with a checked
receipt chain, unchanged hash and retained immutable prior content. Read-only
acceptance follows that chain before comparing current bytes to the latest receipt;
old hashes remain historical evidence. Review/rework observations must state the
exact paths, authority and fixed execution mechanism used, and cannot be generalized
to arbitrary repository repair.

The retained L2 review-context failure also has an offline representation diagnostic:
the original 56,755-byte packet is unchanged, while complete untrusted source blocks,
shared constraint fields and exact original-message character spans remove repeated
JSON escaping/metadata. The old conservative reserve of 73,065 becomes a 64,622
review-envelope estimate; actual local `ProviderGateway._payload` construction
reserves 64,245 under the unchanged 65,536 context ceiling. All three original
source texts remain present, with no source/review-criterion truncation. This is a
local construction for that exact fixture, not a network call, a successful live
review or proof that a larger packet fits. Exceeded bounds still fail closed;
`_packet` and PASS hash binding retain their original values. [Sprint C/I](audit/phase2/sprint-ci.md)
records the reproduction and 118-test related group.

Receipt-bound invalid JSON triggers labelled Core-parser revision feedback; no LLM
call or PASS is inferred. Reviewer output is capped by 8192, the role output limit
and the registered model output limit. Only settled truncation with trustworthy
exact usage can request a further compact verdict within the same cumulative
budgets and review rounds. These paths have local/Mock evidence above; successful
live autonomous repair must still appear in the final run's actual history.

The fixed numeric-suite repair path is separately labelled
`deterministic_semantic_validation` / `core_fixed_numeric_suite`. Its failed report,
latest result, source/receipt and plan/Worker identities are checked before emitting
at most ten failed-case diagnostics. Same-Worker requeue requires explicit revision
authority, current grant, remaining original budgets and settled prior actions and
model attempts. No synthetic feedback or model claim substitutes for rerunning the
real suite. Persisted feedback can recover once after a crash before callback,
including semantic-only nodes, without a model-review call. Recovery requires an
originally available revision, current result/semantic/source/receipt bindings,
current scopes/grants and remaining original budgets with no unsettled actions or
Gateway attempts. Changed or stale inputs, revoked authority, exhausted budgets,
callback errors and fake success remain fail closed. This bounded recovery is not
replay permission for an unknown external action.

Each final live record must retain Run ID, Provider/model, execution mode, model/tool
calls, charged/unknown token usage, duration, retries, review verdicts/revisions,
artifact hashes, final status and failure diagnostics. Price stays unknown when no
trusted price is configured. Report success denominator, evidence completeness,
compaction source readback and observed restart boundary explicitly. The retained
L1 pass and L2/L3 failures above are recorded; later reruns and final freeze remain
pending. Run directories and proposed tasks are not acceptance evidence.
The driver's `runtime_settings` and Publisher whitelist retain only reasoning
effort, review-round limit, Worker lease seconds, Provider timeout seconds, retry limit
and effective model token/concurrency limits.
Missing values in older records remain null, with no retrospective inference or
approval/configuration change.
